
## Motion and animation

- **Hero:** 6 walk frames per stride, `frame = floor(anim·0.5·6) % 6`; hop `|sin(2π·anim·0.5)|·1.1`; idle frame with breathing bob `0.35 + 0.35·sin(2.4·t)`. Yaw follows velocity via `angleLerp(rate 0.22)`, quantised to 16 baked angles.
- **Small enemy:** 4 frames, `anim·0.55` cycles, hop 1.4, yaw rate 0.16. **Brute:** 4 frames at `anim·0.42`, hop 0.6, yaw rate 0.08 (turns heavily). **Ghost:** 4 frames at 1.4 cycles/s regardless of speed, hover `2.5 + 1.6·sin(2.6·t)`.
- Animation is mesh-level (limb rotation around pivots, leaf sway, cape flare), never sprite squash — except the 0.22 s death squash.
- **Gems:** 1.5 quarter-turns/s, bob `2.2 + 0.8·sin(3t)`, pop-hop 9 units when spawned. **Lanterns:** hover `9 + 1.2·sin(4t)`, glow alpha `0.5 + 0.12·sin(11t)`.
- **Damage numbers:** pop from 0.55 to 1.15 scale in the first 14 % of life, then settle to 1.0, fade in the last third.
- **Hurt:** white overlay at `hurtT`; invulnerability blinks at 18 Hz (alpha 0.5/1).
- **Carved-face glow:** flicker `0.22 + 0.06·sin(9t)`.

## Do and don't

**Do**
- Build every visible thing as a real triangle mesh and shade it with the same sun and ambient constants.
- Pre-render meshes into sprites at 16 yaws × a few frames; blit sprites per frame.
- Keep facets big: 5–9 segment lathes, icospheres with subdivision 0–1, ±10–15 % jitter on organic forms.
- Paint faces, windows and cracks as emissive polygons (rim / fill / hot core) with negative depth bias.
- Give every object a sun-projected, blurred indigo shadow plus an AO blob.
- Finish with the tilt-shift bands and the soft violet side vignette.
- Pick 2–4 base colours per material and let lighting create the ramp.

**Don't**
- Don't add black outlines or cel ink lines.
- Don't use smooth / per-vertex shading or gradients on models — one colour per triangle.
- Don't use bitmap textures or noise grain on surfaces.
- Don't render meshes live per frame for crowds.
- Don't use grey/black shadows or let actors float without shadows.
- Don't mix pitches or light directions between assets.
- Don't over-saturate the ground; it must stay a calm mid-value backdrop.

## Implementation recipe

1. Define the world: 360 world units of height on screen, ground plane = world xy, camera pitch 44°, sun `normalize(−0.58, 0.3, 0.76)`, ambient constants from *Rendering technique*.
2. Copy the 3D core from `starter.js`: matrices (`T`, `SC`, `RX`, `RY`, `RZ`, `chain`), `Mesh` (`vert`, `tri`, `add`, `orient`), `lathe`, `box`, `ico`, `leaf`, `triangulate`, `feature`, `carved`, `shadeRGB`, `drawMesh`.
3. At startup compute `K = clamp(round(screenH/360·4)/4, 2, 4)`.
4. Model the hero: big lathe/sphere head (≈ 60 % of height) with a carved emissive face on +x, a small lathe body, box feet, icosphere hands. Write it as a function of `phase` and `walk` so legs/arms rotate around pivots.
5. Model 2–3 enemy types with distinct silhouettes and hues (round + leaf crown, tapered sheet, huge cracked rock). Give each a face on +x.
6. Bake: for each actor `spriteSet(frames, 16 yaws)`; for each prop a single yaw. Bake a shadow (`makeShadow`) per type. Bake white flash silhouettes lazily.
7. Build the ground per 256-unit chunk: jittered triangle lattice (24 units), biome + height per vertex, 4 colour variants per biome, height-field normal → `shadeRGB`, decals on an 11-unit grid, prop shadows multiplied in at 0.62.
8. Per frame: blit ground chunks; draw gems; draw actor shadows (alpha 0.5); y-sort props + actors and blit (pixel-snap to view scale); additive face glows; projectiles with trails; shard/puff/spark particles; damage numbers in Baloo 2.
9. Screen post: tilt-shift top 20 % / bottom 17 % via 1/8 downscale + haze gradients, then side vignette.
10. HUD in HTML/CSS with the cream pill styles above; render upgrade icons with the same mesh pipeline at a custom pitch.

## Code

The snippets below are the core techniques, standalone. `starter.js` (same folder) contains the complete, runnable kit (meshes, hero, enemies, trees, ground, tilt-shift, preview scene). The full reference module is [`../../js/styles/lowpoly.js`](../../js/styles/lowpoly.js).

**Camera, light and flat shading**

```js
const SP = Math.sin(44 * Math.PI / 180), CP = Math.cos(44 * Math.PI / 180);
const LV = (() => { const v = [-0.58, 0.3, 0.76], l = Math.hypot(...v); return v.map((c) => c / l); })();
const SKY = [0.47, 0.52, 0.67], GND = [0.52, 0.44, 0.38], SUN = [0.7, 0.62, 0.45];
function shadeRGB(c, nx, ny, nz, lift = 0) {
  const d = Math.max(0, nx * LV[0] + ny * LV[1] + nz * LV[2]), h = 0.5 + 0.5 * nz;
  return c.map((v, i) => { const s = v * (SKY[i] * h + GND[i] * (1 - h) + SUN[i] * d); return s + (v - s) * lift; });
}
const rgbs = (c) => 'rgb(' + c.map((v) => Math.max(0, Math.min(255, v)) | 0).join(',') + ')';
```

**Projecting, culling, sorting and filling a mesh** (`m.v` = flat xyz array, `m.f` = `{a, b, c, col, em, ds, bias}`)

```js
function drawMesh(ctx, m, { yaw = 0, K, ax, ay, lw = 0.85, lift = 0 }) {
  const cs = Math.cos(yaw), sn = Math.sin(yaw), v = m.v, n = v.length / 3;
  const X = new Float32Array(n), Y = new Float32Array(n), Z = new Float32Array(n), list = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { X[i] = v[i*3] * cs - v[i*3+1] * sn; Y[i] = v[i*3] * sn + v[i*3+1] * cs; Z[i] = v[i*3+2]; }
  for (const f of m.f) {
    const { a, b, c } = f;
    const e1 = [X[b]-X[a], Y[b]-Y[a], Z[b]-Z[a]], e2 = [X[c]-X[a], Y[c]-Y[a], Z[c]-Z[a]];
    let nx = e1[1]*e2[2] - e1[2]*e2[1], ny = e1[2]*e2[0] - e1[0]*e2[2], nz = e1[0]*e2[1] - e1[1]*e2[0];
    const l = Math.hypot(nx, ny, nz); if (l < 1e-9) continue;
    nx /= l; ny /= l; nz /= l;
    if (ny * CP + nz * SP <= 1e-4) { if (!f.ds) continue; nx = -nx; ny = -ny; nz = -nz; } // back-face
    const dep = -((Y[a]+Y[b]+Y[c]) / 3) * CP - ((Z[a]+Z[b]+Z[c]) / 3) * SP + (f.bias || 0);
    list.push({ a, b, c, dep, s: rgbs(f.em ? f.col : shadeRGB(f.col, nx, ny, nz, lift)) });
  }
  list.sort((p, q) => q.dep - p.dep);
  ctx.lineJoin = 'round'; ctx.lineWidth = lw;
  for (const t of list) {
    ctx.fillStyle = ctx.strokeStyle = t.s; ctx.beginPath();
    for (const i of [t.a, t.b, t.c]) ctx.lineTo(ax + X[i] * K, ay + (Y[i] * SP - Z[i] * CP) * K);
    ctx.closePath(); ctx.fill(); ctx.stroke(); // same-colour stroke hides AA seams
  }
}
```

**A lathe — the workhorse primitive** (pumpkins, bodies, legs, cones, ghosts)

```js
function lathe(prof, segs, o = {}) { // prof: [[r, z], ...] bottom -> top, r = 0 is a pole
  const m = { v: [], f: [] }, vert = (x, y, z) => (m.v.push(x, y, z), m.v.length / 3 - 1);
  const col = typeof o.col === 'function' ? o.col : () => o.col, rings = [];
  prof.forEach(([r, z], i) => {
    if (r <= 1e-4) return rings.push({ pole: vert(0, 0, z) });
    const idx = [];
    for (let j = 0; j < segs; j++) {
      const a = (j / segs) * Math.PI * 2 + (o.twist || 0) * i, rr = r * (o.ribs && j & 1 ? o.ribs : 1);
      idx.push(vert(Math.cos(a) * rr, Math.sin(a) * rr, z));
    }
    rings.push({ idx });
  });
  for (let i = 0; i < rings.length - 1; i++) {
    const A = rings[i], B = rings[i + 1];
    for (let j = 0; j < segs; j++) {
      const j1 = (j + 1) % segs, tri = (a, b, c, k) => m.f.push({ a, b, c, col: col(i, j, k), bias: 0 });
      if (A.idx && B.idx) { tri(A.idx[j], A.idx[j1], B.idx[j1], 0); tri(A.idx[j], B.idx[j1], B.idx[j], 1); }
      else if (A.idx) tri(A.idx[j], A.idx[j1], B.pole, 0);
      else tri(A.pole, B.idx[j1], B.idx[j], 1);
    }
  }
  return m;
}
// ribbed pumpkin: alternating rib colours, 16 segments, radius 7.8, half-height 6.5
const hex = (h) => [1, 3, 5].map((i) => parseInt(h.slice(i, i + 2), 16));
const pumpkin = lathe([-90, -62, -34, -8, 18, 44, 66].map((e) => [e <= -89.99 ? 0 : 7.8 * Math.cos(e * Math.PI / 180), 6.5 + 6.5 * Math.sin(e * Math.PI / 180)])
  .concat([[1.56, 12.8], [0, 12]]), 16, { ribs: 0.88, col: (i, j) => hex(j & 1 ? '#e27526' : '#f48a2c') });
```

**Sun-projected soft shadow sprite**

```js
function makeShadow(mesh, yaw, K, { ao = 6, aoA = 0.85, dirA = 0.6, blur = 1.6, col = '#2c3263' } = {}) {
  const cs = Math.cos(yaw), sn = Math.sin(yaw), kx = -LV[0] / LV[2], ky = -LV[1] / LV[2], v = mesh.v, PX = [], PY = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < v.length / 3; i++) {
    const x = v[i*3], y = v[i*3+1], z = Math.max(0, v[i*3+2]);
    PX[i] = (x * cs - y * sn + z * kx) * K; PY[i] = (x * sn + y * cs + z * ky) * SP * K; // slide along the sun ray
  }
  const pad = Math.ceil(blur * K * 2.5) + 2, x0 = Math.min(-ao * K, ...PX), y0 = Math.min(-ao * SP * K, ...PY);
  const w = Math.ceil(Math.max(ao * K, ...PX) - x0) + pad * 2, h = Math.ceil(Math.max(ao * SP * K, ...PY) - y0) + pad * 2;
  const ax = Math.round(-x0 + pad), ay = Math.round(-y0 + pad);
  const A = Object.assign(document.createElement('canvas'), { width: w, height: h }), a = A.getContext('2d');
  const B = Object.assign(document.createElement('canvas'), { width: w, height: h }), b = B.getContext('2d');
  a.fillStyle = '#000';
  for (const f of mesh.f) { a.beginPath(); a.moveTo(ax + PX[f.a], ay + PY[f.a]); a.lineTo(ax + PX[f.b], ay + PY[f.b]); a.lineTo(ax + PX[f.c], ay + PY[f.c]); a.fill(); }
  b.globalAlpha = dirA; b.filter = `blur(${(blur * K).toFixed(1)}px)`; b.drawImage(A, 0, 0); b.filter = 'none'; b.globalAlpha = 1;
  b.save(); b.translate(ax, ay); b.scale(1, SP * 0.95);                      // ambient-occlusion blob
  const g = b.createRadialGradient(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, ao * K);
  g.addColorStop(0, `rgba(0,0,0,${aoA})`); g.addColorStop(0.55, `rgba(0,0,0,${aoA * 0.55})`); g.addColorStop(1, 'rgba(0,0,0,0)');
  b.fillStyle = g; b.beginPath(); b.arc(0, 0, ao * K, 0, Math.PI * 2); b.fill(); b.restore();
  b.globalCompositeOperation = 'source-in'; b.fillStyle = col; b.fillRect(0, 0, w, h); // recolour to indigo
  return { c: B, ax, ay };
}
```

## Adapting it to your game

- **Keep fixed:** pitch 44°, the sun vector, SKY/GND/SUN constants, outline-free fill+stroke facets, 16 baked yaws, indigo shadows, tilt-shift + side vignette, chunky faceting (≤ 16 segments), the cream-pill HUD.
- **May change:** the palette, as long as you keep (a) a calm mid-value ground in 4 close variants per biome, (b) 2–4 base colours per material, (c) saturated colours only on emissive parts. A winter re-theme: ground `#dfe7ef`-ish variants, shadows stay indigo, pines stay, crowns become white icospheres.
- **New characters:** compose from lathe + box + ico + leaf; put a readable face on +x with `feature`/`carved`; animate with pivot rotations per phase; bake 4–6 frames. Keep the hero ≈ 17 × 31 units and enemies 14–20 units; bosses 3× size.
- **Other genres:** a city builder uses `box` houses with gable roofs (already in the reference); a tactics game can snap units to the triangle lattice; a side-on view is *not* supported — rotate the camera pitch only if you re-bake everything.
- **Other resolutions:** only `K` changes; bake at `clamp(round(H/360·4)/4, 2, 4)` and keep world units. Low-end devices: bake 8 yaws instead of 16.

## Performance notes

- Baking is the main cost: hero 16 × 7 sprites, each enemy 16 × 4, ~20 props, ~25 decal sprites, puffs, icons — a few hundred milliseconds at init. Ghost/brute meshes have 300–900 triangles; bake them, never draw live.
- Per frame: one `drawImage` per actor/shadow, plus a handful of additive glows. Hundreds of enemies stay under budget.
- Ground chunks (256 units at ≤ 3 px/unit) are built by a generator that yields every 4 rows and every 64 decals, within a 5 ms/frame budget, so streaming never hitches. Prop shadows are baked into chunks.
- Shadows use `ctx.filter = blur()` only at bake time.
- Tilt-shift: two 1/8-scale copies of screen bands and 14 slice blits per frame — cheap.
- `starter.js` renders its whole preview in ~4–8 ms by caching every sprite and the ground canvas.

## Copy-paste prompt

```text
Build my game <X> in the "Low-Poly Diorama" style (miwale Game Style Library):
- Canvas 2D, no image assets. Write a tiny 3D pipeline: triangle meshes -> yaw -> orthographic 3/4
  projection (pitch 44°, screenY = (Y*sin44 - Z*cos44)*K) -> back-face cull -> painter's sort -> fill.
- Flat shading per triangle: col*(SKY*h + GND*(1-h) + SUN*max(0,n·L)), h = .5+.5*nz,
  L = normalize(-0.58, 0.3, 0.76), SKY [.47,.52,.67], GND [.52,.44,.38], SUN [.7,.62,.45]. No outlines.
- Build models from lathes (5-16 segments), boxes, icospheres (sub 0-1, jittered) and folded leaf blades.
  Faces/windows/cracks are emissive polygons stacked rim/fill/hot core on the model's +x front.
- Pre-render every actor at 16 yaw angles x 4-6 animation frames into sprites; props at one yaw.
- Hero ~17x31 world units (360 units of screen height), big head ~60 % of the height, glowing face.
- Ground: jittered triangle lattice (24 units), 4 close colour variants per biome (meadow #9cb876,
  forest #c98e57, sand #e2cb9c), lit from a tiny height field with the same shading; baked tufts/leaves.
- Shadows: mesh projected along the sun, blurred, + AO blob, tinted indigo #2c3263 (never black).
- Palette: pumpkin #f48a2c, lilac #a77ccf, cream #f3e5bb, cape #4b68a3, glow #ffc43a, gems #4fe3b0.
- Effects: faceted triangle shards, low-poly icosphere puffs, ground ellipse rings, additive warm glows.
- Post: tilt-shift (top 20 % / bottom 17 % via 1/8 downscale + haze) and a soft violet side vignette.
- HUD: cream #fffaf2 pills, violet drop shadows, glossy gradient bars, fonts Baloo 2 800 + Nunito.
```


---

<!-- style: linocut · https://miwale.com/styles/library/linocut/STYLE.md -->

# Linocut — Game Art Style Spec

> A moving linocut print: cream paper, carbon-black key plate, one misregistered pumpkin-orange spot plate and a sparing teal.

The game looks like a hand-pulled linocut or woodcut print come alive. Every shape is either solid black ink with white gouges carved out of it, or bare paper with black knife marks cut into the surrounding block. Lines never have constant width: each mark is a pointed "lens" or a "taper" with a blunt start and sharp tip, exactly like a V-gouge cut. Colour comes from one pumpkin-orange spot plate printed slightly off-register, so a sliver of paper shows along one edge, and a very sparing teal second spot. There are no gradients anywhere – tone is only line density, stipple and hatching. The reference game is *Jack vs. the Turnip Ancestors* (pumpkin-headed hero vs. turnips, ghosts and a turnip colossus); use it only as an example.

## At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Family | Printmaking · Linocut |
| Mood | folkloric, bold, graphic, eerie, handmade |
| Best for | top-down action/survivor, folk-horror and fairy-tale games, card/board games, narrative art |
| Renderer | Canvas 2D, procedural, no image assets |
| Pixel art | No – native resolution, sprites baked at 2–5 px per world unit |
| Difficulty | 6/10 – carving white lines into black is detail work per figure; hordes blur to black |
| Fonts | Rye, Alfa Slab One, Special Elite |
| Key colours | paper `#f0e7d2`, ink `#1b1715`, orange `#ea6820`, teal `#2e7674` |

## When to use it

Good fits:
- **Top-down action with clear silhouettes** – two values make every figure pop on paper.
- **Folk horror, fairy tales, legends, western** – reads as an old broadsheet or chapbook.
- **Card, board and narrative games** – static art looks like real prints.
- **Low-budget but striking**: one spot colour is a strong brand.

Bad fits:
- **Many-colour coding** (match-3, team colours) – you only have ink, paper, orange and a hint of teal.
- **Massive hordes** – dozens of black enemies merge into one black mass unless halos and spacing are generous.
- **Soft, cozy pastel games** – the style is high-contrast and graphic.

## Color palette

| Swatch | Hex | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Paper | `#f0e7d2` | Ground, halos, carved highlights (~65%) |
| Ink | `#1b1715` | Key plate – outlines, solid masses, all marks (~30%) |
| Pumpkin Orange | `#ea6820` | The one spot plate – hero head, cores, lantern faces, gems, XP, crits (~4%) |
| Teal | `#2e7674` | Sparing second spot – ghost frost stipple, brute core ring, big gem centre (<1%) |
| Paper Shade | `#e2d6ba` | Darkest paper fibres (paper − 14) |
| Ink Deep | `#0d0b0a` | Hard offset shadows on cards and panels |

Palette rules:
- **Two values + flat spots.** No gradients, no alpha shading, no blur, no grey.
- **Misregistration**: the orange plate is always drawn offset by `MX = 0.8, MY = 0.55` world units (x mirrored with facing); teal by `TX = −0.55, TY = 0.45`. Same offset on every object – it is the style's signature.
- Spot colour appears inside a hole cut in the key plate (`holeSpot`: fill paper, then the colour shifted and clipped), or as its own plate under a black outline (gems, seeds).
- Darker = more/wider black marks. Lighter = more white gouges.
- Paper fibres darken ink slightly (`ink + fibre·0.4`) and ink has pinholes where paper shows through.

## Typography

- **Rye** 400 – woodtype display for titles (72px level-up, 66px game over), the clock (34px) and card keys. `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Rye`
  `font: 400 34px/1.05 'Rye', Georgia, serif; letter-spacing: 2px; color: #1b1715; text-shadow: 2px 2px 0 #ea6820;`
  Titles on dark overlays: paper colour with `text-shadow: 5px 4px 0 #ea6820` (the misregistered orange plate behind the type).
- **Alfa Slab One** 400 – numbers: HP text (17px), kills (22px), level badge (13px, paper on an ink block), damage numbers, card names (20px with a 2px ink underline). `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Alfa+Slab+One`
  HP text gets an 8-direction 2px paper outline via `text-shadow` so it reads over the striped bar.
- **Special Elite** 400 – typewriter labels and descriptions (11–19px, letter-spacing 2–3px, labels with a 2px ink rule above). `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Special+Elite`

Damage numbers (canvas): normal = ink fill over a paper stroke of 0.3× font size (8.5 units tall); crit = 11.5 units, paper stroke 0.36×, an ink copy offset by `(MX, MY)·0.6`, a thin ink outline, then orange fill – i.e. a two-plate print.

## Rendering technique

1. **Init** – `K = clamp(round(screenH / 360 · 4) / 4, 2, 5)` px per world unit. Build textures: the 512² paper fibre map `FIB` (Int8, −22…+14) and the 256² ink void map `VOID`.
2. **Carving toolkit** (all marks are *fills*, see Code): `lens(x0,y0,x1,y1,w,bend)` – two quadratic curves meeting in points; `taper` – blunt round start, sharp tip; `limb(pts,w0,w1)` – Catmull-Rom spline with tapering width and round caps; `smoothPath`; `crescent` – shape minus a shrunken copy shifted to the light, filled even-odd (heavy shadow contour); `holeSpot` – cut hole showing a misregistered spot plate.
3. **Figure recipe**: fill the form (paper or ink) → print the orange plate offset → clip and carve (black lenses on paper / white lenses on black) → `crescent` on the shadow side → thin ink outline 0.5–0.75 → carved face → top details (stem, leaf, teeth).
4. **Sprite bake `mk`**: draw at K px/unit with feet at the anchor; **paper halo** – a paper-tinted silhouette drawn 12× around a 0.5–0.9-unit circle with `destination-over`; **inkify** – per pixel: dark pixels where `VOID > 238` move 72% toward paper (pinholes), orange pixels get ×0.93–1.05 density and rare paper voids.
5. **Derived sprites**: negative print (`invert`, luminance mapped paper↔ink, saturated pixels → ink) for hit flashes; death shards (4–5 wedges cut from the centre with jittered radial cuts, paper-coloured cut edges 0.7 units wide); orange-tinted ghost of the hero for dash after-images.
6. **Variants**: hero 4 walk + 2 idle poses × 2 carving variants (seeds `100 + v·7 + i`) × 2 facings (drawn mirrored, the orange offset mirrors too); enemies 4 × 2 × 2.
7. **Ground chunks** (256 units, ≤ 2.5 px/unit): generator; 84×84 field grid, distances via value/|gradient|, per-pixel analytic ink coverage `a` per region, then `paper + fibre → mix toward ink by a` with pinholes; then decals.
8. **Per frame**: ground → splats → gems → hatched shadows → y-sorted props/enemies/hero → orbitals → projectiles → particles → numbers → ragged ink frame. Only `drawImage` of cached canvases; blit positions snapped to screen pixels.

## Background and ground

Fields (world units): `B = warped fbm(x/1000)` (biome), `D = fbm(x/300) + (B − 0.55)·0.6` (dark soil when `D > 0.74`), `R = perlin(x/3400)` warped (road where distance < 11). Biomes: `B < 0.455` field, `B > 0.565` forest, else meadow. All regions are separated by a **1.5-unit paper gutter** – carved patterns stop short of the edge, like separately cut areas of the block.

Per-region carved pattern (analytic per pixel, coverage 0…1 anti-aliased with `(halfwidth − distance)·res + 0.5`):
- **Meadow** (mostly clean paper): grass ticks on a 9-unit hashed grid, density `0.1 + 0.5·smoothstep(0.32, 0.72, T)` (T = fbm/140); each tick has 1–3 tapered blades (angles 0.16, −0.5, 0.75 rad; length 2.2–3.55; half-width 0.46 → 0). Rare "chatter": 3–5 parallel short gouges on a 27-unit grid (30% of cells).
- **Ploughed field**: furrow lines from a warped scalar `F = (y + 0.22x + 110·(fbm − 0.5) + 9·perlin) / 4.4`; distance to the nearest line centre is `|frac(F) − 0.5| / |∇F|`; half-width `0.66·smoothstep(0.27, 0.7, M)·(0.72 + 0.56·T)` (34% of lines thinner). A carved ditch line 0.88 wide along the field edge. Turnip sprouts and clods are snapped onto furrows.
- **Forest floor**: stipple dots r 0.3–0.54 on a 2.5-unit hashed grid, density 0.14–0.66; an 0.84-wide edge line 0.5 units inside the border and a clean gap behind it.
- **Dark soil**: solid ink; two paper "echo" contours at 1.8 (width 0.6) and 3.4 (0.44) units inside the edge – the classic linocut outline ripple; deeper than 4.3 units, short oriented white gouge flecks (cell 4.3, 62% filled, length 1.3–2.8, aligned with the field direction ± 0.35 rad).
- **Road** (22 units wide): a curb line, then cobbles from Worley noise (cell 4.4): paper joints `(f2 − f1)·2.2 < 0.36`, stones hatched with 45° lines on their shadow side, 1 in 16 stones solid ink.
- **Paper**: `#f0e7d2 + FIB` (1300 short curved fibres ±0.13 alpha, mottling ±4.5, grain ±3).
- **Decals** (knocked out with a paper disc first, then carved): 5-petal flowers, stars, pebbles, skulls, bones, leaves with veins, twigs, mushrooms, sprouts, turnips, clods, and **carved roots** radiating from every tree into the ground (4–6 tapered limbs, 9–16 units).

## Characters

**Hero** (Jack), feet at (0,0), ~16 × 30 units, facing via `scale(f,1)`:
- **Legs**: `limb` half-width 1.15 → 0.9, boots = ink ellipses 1.8 × 1.05 with a paper shine lens.
- **Cloak**: 14-point polygon, solid ink, jittered ±0.125; **white carved folds** on the lit side: lenses of half-width 0.44, 0.34, 0.26 from the hem upward, plus an arm separation gouge.
- **Scarf**: paper shape with a 0.45–0.5 ink outline and ink stripe lenses; tail flutters with `scarf` ±0.6.
- **Hand**: paper disc r 1.25 with ink outline.
- **Pumpkin head**: 22-point lobed ellipse 7.3 × 6.2 (top flattened near the stem); paper fill, **orange plate offset** `(MX·f, MY)`; clipped carving: 4 rib lenses (half-width 0.26/0.34), 6 shading lenses on the right widening 0.16 → 0.44, 4 horizontal lenses at the bottom; **crescent** shift (−1.0, −0.85) scale 0.93; ink outline 0.75.
- **Face** (shifted 0.95 toward facing): solid ink triangle eyes and nose, a jagged grin with two "teeth" notches; two white gouge highlights at the upper left of the head.
- **Stem** taper 1.1 wide, one leaf (ink lens with a paper midrib).
- Poses: `WALK` = 4 keyframes (feet `[3.3,0]/[-3,0]`, `[1,0]/[-0.4,-1.5]`…, bob −0.8 on passing poses), `IDLE` = 2.

## Enemies and props

- **Small melee enemy** (turnip creeper, ~16 × 28): root legs (`limb` 0.85 → 0.55 + two toe tapers), three leaves behind, smooth bulb; inside the clip a **solid ink crown** above a wavy line `y = −12.4 + 0.45·sin(0.95x + 0.6)`, an **engraved comb** of 13 tapers hanging into the paper underside (getting longer to the right = shadow), white crown highlights, ink lenses on the lower right; carved paper lens eyes with ink pupils, a black grimace lens with two paper teeth; crescent + 0.7 outline; root hairs.
- **Floating enemy** (ghost, ~15 × 24): paper body; **teal stipple plate** (230 candidate dots r 0.26–0.42, probability rising to the lower right) offset by (TX, TY); 4 ink shading lenses on the right; crescent; black eye/mouth ellipses; reaching tapered arms with 3 finger tapers; the tail dissolves into 3 shrinking ink dots.
- **Brute** (colossus, ~37 × 57): solid ink body (18-point blob, narrowed top) with **concentric white arc gouges** on the upper left (6 arcs shrinking 14.4 → 2.9), white crack limbs from the core, a paper rim crescent on the lit edge, a **teal ring + orange core** in holes, a paper 4-point star and 10 carved rays; thick limbs 3.1 → 1.8 with root fingers; crown of 5 leaves.
- **Pickups**: small gem = orange 4-point star (offset plate) with ink outline and 4 ink spark lenses (2 frames: lengths 3.8/4.6); big gem = 8-point orange star, teal centre hole, 8 sparks.
- **Orbiting lantern**: turnip lantern (ink top, comb, orange face holes) over a rotating 14-spike orange ray star.
- **Props**: bare oaks (roots, trunk `limb` 4.4 → 3.0, recursive branches 3 levels deep with widths ×0.6, white bark gouges on the lit side, knot hole), crowned trees (8 ink lobes with 3 scalloped white arc gouges each), spruces (6 toothed tiers with white lenses), graves (round with cross, Celtic cross, slab with carved skull), fences with a broken rail, scarecrow, lantern poles with orange rays, crows (2-frame beak), haystacks (paper dome with 17 converging ink lenses). Grass tufts at every base.
- **Shadows**: never soft – horizontal ink lenses filling an ellipse (one per 0.75 units of height, half-width 0.33–0.45), shifted right (light from upper left). Hero 6.4 × 2.0, small enemy 7.4 × 2.2, ghost 4.6 × 1.4, brute 16 × 4, tree 19 × 4.6.

## Effects and particles

- **Spawn – block stamped down**: for `spawnT < 0.5` draw the sprite at scale `1 + (1−k)²·0.9`, raised 10·(1−k) units, alpha 0.25 → 1; at contact stamp an **ink splat** (smooth 14-point blob with tapered spatters, 3 paper gouges) on the ground and squash `±sin(kπ)·0.14·(1−k)`.
- **Hit**: negative-print sprite while `flash > 0.45`, a radial burst of 10 black lenses (orange 8-lens burst for lantern hits), wood chips flying with gravity.
- **Death – carved shatter**: 0.16 s negative print scaled 1 + t·0.6, then 4 (brute 5) pre-cut shards fly out `2 + 12·outQuad(u)` units, rotate ±1.6 rad, fall `26u²`, alpha `1 − u²`; ink drops and a ground splat that fades in its last 0.5 s.
- **Projectile**: orange seed plate offset under a black outlined seed with a carved shine; trail of 3 black lenses.
- **Dash**: 2 orange-tinted after-images (alpha 0.55/i) and a trail sprite.
- **Pickup**: orange 4-point star sprite; **level up**: a 16-segment orange gouge-arc ring and a big rotating 18-spike orange ray star behind the hero.
- **Halftone puff** (dust): hex grid of ink dots (spacing 1.55) whose radius shrinks toward the edge; 3 frames get lighter.

## Lighting, shadows and post-processing

- Fixed light from the **upper left**: crescents at the lower right, white gouges at the upper left, shadows shifted right.
- **Glow = printed rays**, not light: flat orange spike stars (12–18 spikes, alternating lengths) on the offset plate.
- **Paper halo** (0.5–0.9 units) behind every sprite – the knock-out that keeps black figures readable on dark soil and in crowds.
- **Ink texture**: pinhole voids and fibres in all ink, ground and sprites alike.
- **Frame**: ragged ink strips (thickness `max(6, 1.1% of H)`, inner jagged edge every 6–18 px) plus an inner rule; no vignette.
- Overlays (level up, game over): `rgba(27,23,21,.8)` with a halftone dot pattern `radial-gradient(circle, rgba(240,231,210,.16) 0 1.3px, transparent 1.7px)` at 8px.

## UI and HUD

- Panels: paper with an SVG noise texture, `3px solid` ink borders, radius 2px, **hard offset shadows** `4px 4px 0` ink (cards `8px 8px 0 #0d0b0a`, hovered `10px 12px 0` orange).
- XP bar: orange with ink rules `repeating-linear-gradient(-62deg, orange 0 7px, ink 7px 8.5px)`; HP bar: ink with paper rules (9px / 1.5px).
- Level badge: paper Alfa Slab One on a solid ink block at the bar's right end.
- Clock: double-ruled box (`box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px paper, 0 0 0 6px ink, 7px 7px 0 6px ink`), Rye time with a 2px orange offset shadow, typewriter label under a 2px rule.
- Hurt: the HP bar flips to `filter: invert(1)` (negative print). Transitions use `steps()`.
- Icons are carved in a 100-unit box, big ones on a round medallion.

```css
:root { --paper:#f0e7d2; --ink:#1b1715; --org:#ea6820; --teal:#2e7674; }
.hud { font-family: 'Special Elite', 'Courier New', monospace; color: var(--ink); }
.xp { height: 20px; background: var(--paper); border: 3px solid var(--ink); border-radius: 2px; box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 var(--ink); }
.xp-fill { height: 100%; background: repeating-linear-gradient(-62deg, var(--org) 0 7px, var(--ink) 7px 8.5px);
  box-shadow: 3px 0 0 var(--ink); transition: width .15s steps(3); }
.hp-bar { width: 230px; height: 22px; background: var(--paper); border: 3px solid var(--ink); border-radius: 2px; box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 var(--ink); }
.hp-fill { height: 100%; background: repeating-linear-gradient(-62deg, var(--ink) 0 9px, var(--paper) 9px 10.5px); transition: width .12s steps(2); }
.hp-text { font: 400 17px 'Alfa Slab One', Georgia, serif;
  text-shadow: 2px 0 var(--paper), -2px 0 var(--paper), 0 2px var(--paper), 0 -2px var(--paper), 2px 2px var(--paper), -2px -2px var(--paper), 2px -2px var(--paper), -2px 2px var(--paper); }
.clock { background: var(--paper); border: 3px solid var(--ink); padding: 3px 22px 4px;
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--paper), 0 0 0 6px var(--ink), 7px 7px 0 6px var(--ink); }
.clock-time { font: 400 34px/1.05 'Rye', Georgia, serif; letter-spacing: 2px; text-shadow: 2px 2px 0 var(--org); }
.clock-label { font: 11px 'Special Elite', monospace; letter-spacing: 3px; border-top: 2px solid var(--ink); padding-top: 2px; }
.card { background: var(--paper); border: 3px solid var(--ink); border-radius: 9px;
  box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 6px var(--paper), inset 0 0 0 8px var(--ink), 8px 8px 0 #0d0b0a; transition: transform .1s steps(2); }
.title { font: 400 72px 'Rye', Georgia, serif; letter-spacing: 3px; color: var(--paper); text-shadow: 5px 4px 0 var(--org); }
.hurt .hp-bar { filter: invert(1); }
```

## Motion and animation

- **Carving boil**: 2 variants per pose, `v = floor(t·6 + seed·10) & 1` (6 fps).
- **Hero**: walk pose `floor(anim·1.25) & 3`, idle `floor(t·2.2) & 1`. Hurt: negative print while `hurtT > 0.6`, then blink at 14 Hz for 0.75 s.
- **Small enemy**: `floor(anim·3.2) & 3`; **brute**: `anim·2.4`; **ghost**: `floor(t·5 + seed·9) & 3`, hovering 2.2 units with a bob quantised to 0.4-unit steps (`round(sin·2.5)·0.4`) – even motion feels stepped.
- **Gems**: 2 frames at 4 fps, bob ±0.7; pop to ×1.7 on pickup.
- **Props**: lantern pole rays alternate at 3.2 fps; crows open their beak occasionally.
- **Numbers**: pop 1.7 → 1.0 in 0.07 s, fade in the last 0.22 s.

## Do and don't

Do:
- Draw only with filled marks: lenses, tapers, limbs, smooth paths.
- Give each figure a solid ink mass with white carving and a paper area with black carving.
- Print orange on a separate offset plate (same `MX, MY` everywhere).
- Shade with widening parallel lenses; put a crescent on the shadow side.
- Bake a paper halo and ink pinholes into every sprite.
- Use hatched-lens shadows and paper gutters between ground regions.
- Keep animation stepped (variant swaps, quantised bobs).

Don't:
- Don't use gradients, blur, glow, or semi-transparent shading.
- Don't add colours beyond orange and a hint of teal.
- Don't register colour perfectly inside outlines.
- Don't use constant-width vector strokes or hairlines as the main line.
- Don't tween shapes smoothly.
- Don't place black figures on black areas without a paper halo.

## Implementation recipe

1. Camera in world units (360 visible vertically); clear to paper `#f0e7d2`.
2. Copy the carving toolkit (`lens`, `taper`, `spline`, `limb`, `smoothPath`, `crescent`, `holeSpot`) and a seeded RNG.
3. Build the paper fibre map and the ink void map once.
4. Write `mk(box, draw, {halo, seed})`: draw at K px/unit → paper halo (12 offset silhouettes, destination-over) → inkify.
5. Design each character as: one solid ink mass + one paper mass, carved with lenses; add the orange plate offset on its key element; crescent bottom-right; thin outline; carved face. Use 4 key poses as data tables (foot positions, bob, cloth swing).
6. Bake 4 poses × 2 jitter seeds × 2 facings; derive negative prints and shatter shards.
7. Ground: noise fields → signed distances → per-pixel coverage pattern per region (grass ticks, furrows, stipple, solid with echo contours, cobbles), 1.5-unit paper gutters, paper fibres and ink pinholes. Bake in chunks with a time budget.
8. Decals: knock out a paper disc, then carve the motif.
9. Shadows as horizontal lens hatching; effects as baked lens bursts, chips, drops, halftone puffs, orange stars/rays.
10. HUD in DOM with the CSS above; damage numbers on canvas as two-plate prints.

## Code

The core techniques, standalone. [`starter.js`](starter.js) contains a full runnable scene (paper ground with grass ticks, forest stipple and dark soil with echo contours, hero, turnips, ghosts, bare trees, gems, projectile, HUD, frame). The complete reference module is [`../../js/styles/linocut.js`](../../js/styles/linocut.js).

```js
// The two basic knife marks. Both are FILLS with the current fillStyle (ink or paper).
const TAU = Math.PI * 2;
function lens(ctx, x0, y0, x1, y1, w, bend = 0) { // pointed both ends, half-width w, centre bent by `bend`
  const dx = x1 - x0, dy = y1 - y0, L = Math.hypot(dx, dy) || 1e-6, nx = -dy / L, ny = dx / L;
  const mx = (x0 + x1) / 2, my = (y0 + y1) / 2, u = 2 * (bend + w), l = 2 * (bend - w);
  ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(x0, y0);
  ctx.quadraticCurveTo(mx + nx * u, my + ny * u, x1, y1);
  ctx.quadraticCurveTo(mx + nx * l, my + ny * l, x0, y0);
  ctx.fill();
}
function taper(ctx, x0, y0, x1, y1, w, bend = 0) { // blunt round start, sharp tip (blades, toes, hairs)
  const dx = x1 - x0, dy = y1 - y0, L = Math.hypot(dx, dy) || 1e-6, nx = -dy / L, ny = dx / L;
  const mx = (x0 + x1) / 2 + nx * bend * 2, my = (y0 + y1) / 2 + ny * bend * 2, th = Math.atan2(dy, dx);
  ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(x0 + nx * w, y0 + ny * w);
  ctx.quadraticCurveTo(mx + nx * w * 0.6, my + ny * w * 0.6, x1, y1);
  ctx.quadraticCurveTo(mx - nx * w * 0.6, my - ny * w * 0.6, x0 - nx * w, y0 - ny * w);
  ctx.arc(x0, y0, w, th - Math.PI / 2, th + Math.PI / 2, true); ctx.closePath(); ctx.fill();
}
// Example: shade the right side of a round form with widening black lenses (darker = wider)
function shadeRight(ctx, cx, cy, rx, ry) {
  ctx.fillStyle = '#1b1715';
  for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) { const x = cx + rx * (0.36 + i * 0.105); lens(ctx, x - 0.5, cy - ry * 0.75 + i * 0.35, x + 0.1, cy + ry * 1.05, 0.16 + i * 0.055, 0.45); }
}
```

```js
// Crescent shadow contour + misregistered spot plate in a cut hole
const MX = 0.8, MY = 0.55; // orange plate offset in world units – identical for every object
function crescent(ctx, shape, cx, cy, dx, dy, s, color = '#1b1715') {
  ctx.save(); ctx.beginPath(); shape(ctx); ctx.clip();           // stay inside the form
  ctx.beginPath(); shape(ctx);                                    // outer shape ...
  ctx.save(); ctx.translate(cx + dx, cy + dy); ctx.scale(s, s); ctx.translate(-cx, -cy); shape(ctx); ctx.restore(); // ... minus a shrunken copy moved to the light
  ctx.fillStyle = color; ctx.fill('evenodd'); ctx.restore();
}
function holeSpot(ctx, shape, color, dx, dy) {
  ctx.beginPath(); shape(ctx); ctx.fillStyle = '#f0e7d2'; ctx.fill();   // the hole shows paper ...
  ctx.save(); ctx.beginPath(); shape(ctx); ctx.clip();
  ctx.translate(dx, dy); ctx.beginPath(); shape(ctx); ctx.fillStyle = color; ctx.fill(); // ... and the offset colour plate
  ctx.restore();
}
// Usage: a pumpkin = paper + offset orange plate + crescent + outline
function pumpkin(ctx, x, y, r) {
  const shape = (c) => c.ellipse(x, y, r, r * 0.85, 0, 0, TAU);
  ctx.beginPath(); shape(ctx); ctx.fillStyle = '#f0e7d2'; ctx.fill();
  ctx.save(); ctx.translate(MX, MY); ctx.beginPath(); shape(ctx); ctx.fillStyle = '#ea6820'; ctx.fill(); ctx.restore();
  crescent(ctx, shape, x, y, -r * 0.14, -r * 0.12, 0.93);
  ctx.beginPath(); shape(ctx); ctx.strokeStyle = '#1b1715'; ctx.lineWidth = 0.75; ctx.stroke();
}
```

```js
// Sprite bake: paper halo behind + uneven ink (pinholes from a void-noise map)
function hash2(x, y, s) { let h = (Math.imul(x, 374761393) + Math.imul(y, 668265263) + Math.imul(s, 1442695041)) | 0; h = Math.imul(h ^ (h >>> 13), 1274126177); h ^= h >>> 16; return (h >>> 0) / 4294967296; }
const VOID = new Uint8Array(65536).map((_, i) => Math.max(0, Math.min(255, Math.round((0.5 * hash2(i & 255, i >> 8, 5) + 0.5 * hash2((i & 255) >> 3, i >> 11, 77)) * 300 - 40))));
function paperHalo(c, rPx) {
  const s = document.createElement('canvas'); s.width = c.width; s.height = c.height;
  const sc = s.getContext('2d'); sc.drawImage(c, 0, 0); sc.globalCompositeOperation = 'source-atop'; sc.fillStyle = '#f0e7d2'; sc.fillRect(0, 0, s.width, s.height);
  const ctx = c.getContext('2d'); ctx.globalCompositeOperation = 'destination-over';
  for (let i = 0; i < 12; i++) ctx.drawImage(s, Math.cos(i / 12 * TAU) * rPx, Math.sin(i / 12 * TAU) * rPx);
  ctx.globalCompositeOperation = 'source-over';
}
function inkify(c, seed) {
  const ctx = c.getContext('2d', { willReadFrequently: true }), im = ctx.getImageData(0, 0, c.width, c.height), d = im.data;
  const P = [240, 231, 210], sx = (seed * 37) & 255, sy = (seed * 91) & 255;
  for (let y = 0, i = 0; y < c.height; y++) for (let x = 0; x < c.width; x++, i += 4) {
    if (d[i + 3] < 100) continue;
    const v = VOID[(((y + sy) & 255) << 8) + ((x + sx) & 255)];
    if (d[i] < 80 && d[i + 1] < 80 && d[i + 2] < 80) { if (v > 238) for (let k = 0; k < 3; k++) d[i + k] += (P[k] - d[i + k]) * 0.72; } // pinhole
    else if (d[i] > 160 && d[i] - d[i + 2] > 100) { const f = 0.93 + v / 255 * 0.12; for (let k = 0; k < 3; k++) d[i + k] *= f; } // orange density grain
  }
  ctx.putImageData(im, 0, 0);
}
```

```js
// Ground: analytic grass ticks (1–3 tapered blades per hashed 9-unit cell). Returns ink coverage 0..1 at world X,Y.
function hashInt(x, y, s) { let h = (Math.imul(x, 374761393) + Math.imul(y, 668265263) + Math.imul(s, 1442695041)) | 0; h = Math.imul(h ^ (h >>> 13), 1274126177); h ^= h >>> 16; return h >>> 0; }
const clamp01 = (v) => (v < 0 ? 0 : v > 1 ? 1 : v);
function blade(dx, dy, ang, L, res) {
  const ux = Math.sin(ang), uy = -Math.cos(ang); let t = (dx * ux + dy * uy) / L;
  if (t > 1) return 0; if (t < 0) t = 0;
  return clamp01((0.46 * (1 - t) - Math.hypot(dx - ux * t * L, dy - uy * t * L)) * res + 0.5); // tapering half-width 0.46 -> 0
}
function grass(X, Y, dens, res) {
  const GC = 9, fx = X / GC, fy = Y / GC, ix = Math.floor(fx), iy = Math.floor(fy);
  const sx = fx - ix < 0.5 ? ix - 1 : ix, sy = fy - iy < 0.5 ? iy - 1 : iy; let a = 0;
  for (let j = 0; j < 2; j++) for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
    const h = hashInt(sx + i, sy + j, 4141); if ((h & 1023) > dens * 1024) continue;
    const dx = X - (sx + i + 0.15 + ((h >>> 10) & 255) / 255 * 0.7) * GC, dy = Y - (sy + j + 0.35 + ((h >>> 18) & 255) / 255 * 0.55) * GC;
    if (dx < -3.3 || dx > 3.3 || dy > 0.7 || dy < -4.6) continue;
    const type = (h >>> 26) & 3, L = 2.2 + ((h >>> 28) & 3) * 0.45;
    let v = blade(dx, dy, 0.16, L, res);
    if (type >= 1) v = Math.max(v, blade(dx + 0.55, dy, -0.5, L * 0.72, res));
    if (type >= 2) v = Math.max(v, blade(dx - 0.55, dy, 0.75, L * 0.66, res));
    a = Math.max(a, v);
  }
  return a; // final pixel = mix(paper + fibre, ink, a)
}
// Dark soil with echo contours (dS = signed distance inside the soil edge, world units):
//   a = clamp01(dS*res + .5); k = max((.3 - |dS-1.8|)*res + .5, (.22 - |dS-3.4|)*res + .5); a *= 1 - clamp01(k)
```

## Adapting it to your game

Keep fixed: two values + flat spots, filled knife marks only, fixed misregistration offset, light from the upper left, crescent + white gouge carving, paper halos, ink pinholes, hatched shadows, stepped animation.

May change:
- **Spot colour**: swap orange for any single strong ink (vermilion `#d8432b`, mustard `#d9a420`, ultramarine `#2f4aa0`); keep the second spot muted and rare. Paper may be white-ish or kraft (`#d9c4a0`) – keep ink at least 8:1 contrast.
- **New characters**: decide which part is solid ink and which is paper; put the spot colour on the single focal element (eyes, core, weapon). Brutes = mostly ink with concentric white arcs; small fodder = paper bodies with an ink cap so crowds don't merge.
- **Hordes**: increase the halo to 1.2 units, mix paper-bodied and ink-bodied enemy types.
- **Side view**: ground becomes a band of solid ink with echo contours on top and grass ticks; sky is plain paper with carved stars.
- **Resolution**: everything is in world units; only K changes.

## Performance notes

- **Init cost**: every pose × variant × facing is drawn, then halo'd and inkified with `getImageData` – the main init cost (plus negative prints and shards). Use `willReadFrequently: true` canvases.
- **Ground**: chunk generators yield every 8 rows inside a 5 ms per-frame budget; the 84×84 field grid avoids per-pixel noise; per pixel only cheap hashed-cell patterns (2×2 cells), with Worley only on roads.
- **Per frame**: only sprite blits; no path rendering at runtime except the frame strips (cached) – 1000+ actors stay cheap.
- **starter.js** bakes paper, sprites and the full-screen ground on the first `draw()` (~0.3 s at 960×540) and then draws a frame in well under 1 ms.

## Copy-paste prompt

```text
Build my game <X> in the "Linocut" style (miwale Game Style Library):
- A moving linocut print: paper #f0e7d2, ink #1b1715, ONE spot colour orange #ea6820, rare teal #2e7674.
- No gradients, blur, glow or alpha shading. Tone only via line density, stipple and hatching.
- Every mark is a filled knife cut: "lens" (pointed both ends) or "taper" (blunt start, sharp tip);
  limbs are tapered splines. No constant-width strokes.
- Each figure = one solid ink mass carved with white gouges + one paper area carved with black lenses.
- Light from the upper left: heavy crescent (shape minus shifted shrunken copy) at the lower right,
  white gouge highlights upper left; shade = parallel black lenses getting wider.
- Orange is printed on its own plate offset by (+0.8, +0.55) world units everywhere (misregistration).
- Bake sprites with a 0.9-unit paper halo and ink pinholes; 4 poses × 2 jittered variants swapped at 6 fps.
- Shadows = horizontal ink lens hatching. Hits = negative print; deaths = carved shards + ink splat.
- Ground: fibrous paper with grass ticks, furrows, stipple forest, solid-ink soil with echo contours,
  1.5-unit paper gutters between regions.
- HUD: paper panels, 3px ink borders, hard 4px offset shadows, striped bars, Rye / Alfa Slab One / Special Elite.
```


---

<!-- style: nes8bit · https://miwale.com/styles/library/nes8bit/STYLE.md -->

# 8-Bit Arcade — Game Art Style Spec

> A lost NES cartridge: strict 2C02 palette, black-outlined 3-colour sprites, tile-language meadows and checker-flicker ghosts.

The game should look like it ships on a forgotten NES/Famicom cartridge. Every colour comes from the NES PPU (2C02) palette. Every sprite uses at most three colours plus a 1-px pure-black outline. The world is made of flat colour areas with hard, tile-like edges: a dark-green meadow with light-green lips, brown forest floor behind black cliff lines, ochre dirt roads, navy ponds with a blue ring, and grey brick graveyards. Nothing is anti-aliased, nothing has a gradient, and the world uses no alpha. Transparency is drawn as a checkerboard and invulnerability as sprite flicker, so the screen reads like real 1986 hardware. The reference implementation is the survivor game *Jack vs. the Turnip Ancestors* (pumpkin-head hero, turnip creepers, ghosts and a turnip colossus). Everything below is written so you can apply it to any top-down or side-view game.

## At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Family | Pixel Art · NES 8-bit |
| Mood | nostalgic, punchy, playful, arcade, crisp |
| Best for | top-down action / survivors, arcade shooters, Zelda-likes, retro platformers, jam games |
| Renderer | Canvas 2D, procedural; all sprites are text grids baked at init |
| Pixel art | yes, 1 art pixel = **1.5 world units** (360-unit-tall view = **240 art rows**, NES height) |
| Difficulty | 3/10: small sprites as text grids; the strict NES rules help because there are fewer decisions |
| Fonts | Press Start 2P (Google Fonts) |
| Key colours | `#005800` meadow · `#503000` forest floor · `#AC7C00` road · `#E45C10` hero · `#940084` enemies · `#FCFCFC` ghosts · `#000000` outlines |

## When to use it

- **Good fits:** top-down survivors and arena shooters, Zelda-like adventures, platformers, score-attack arcade games, game jams. The constraints make content fast to produce and keep everything consistent.
- **Good when** many actors share the screen. Black outlines and saturated flat colour keep a horde readable on the busy ground.
- **Bad fits:** atmospheric horror or moody lighting (there is no light system), painterly or soft cozy games, and games that need many subtly different unit types (3 colours per sprite leave little room for nuance).
- **Bad for** UI-heavy strategy with dense text, because the 8-px font is big and chunky.

## Color palette

All values are from the NES 2C02 master palette (the module's `P` table). Use **nothing else** in the world.

| Swatch | Hex | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Black `k` | `#000000` | outlines, cliff lines, shadows, HUD/menu background |
| White `w` | `#FCFCFC` | ghosts, tombstones, HUD text, window borders, sparks |
| Light grey `g1` | `#BCBCBC` | plaza highlight, stones, dead trees |
| Mid grey `g2` | `#7C7C7C` | plaza bricks, rocks |
| Meadow `gr0` | `#005800` | grass base (~50 % of the screen) |
| Leaf green `gr1` | `#00A800` | tufts, grass lip, canopy, leaves on sprites |
| Light green `gr2` | `#58D854` | canopy/bush highlight |
| Dark brown `br0` | `#503000` | forest floor, road edge, brute feet |
| Ochre `ochre` | `#AC7C00` | road, forest lip, autumn canopy, brute body |
| Sand `sand` | `#F0D0B0` | road lip at water, light pebbles |
| Cream `cream` | `#FCE0A8` | enemy faces/bodies, seed projectile, lantern glass |
| Dark red `red0` | `#881400` | tree trunks, empty hearts, leaf litter |
| Crimson `crim` | `#A80020` | spare accent |
| Red `red` | `#F83800` | hearts, HUD labels, explosion rays, hurt flash |
| Orange `orange` | `#E45C10` | hero head, pumpkins, projectile trail |
| Light orange `lorange` | `#FCA044` | spare accent |
| Gold `gold` | `#F8B800` | big gems, crit numbers, lantern glow, flowers |
| Yellow `yellow` | `#F8D878` | hero's carved face, autumn highlight |
| Navy `navy` | `#0000BC` | water base |
| Blue `blue` | `#0058F8` | water ring, small-gem shade |
| Royal blue `blue2` | `#0078F8` | hero overalls |
| Cyan `cyan` | `#3CBCFC` | ghost tails, small gems, XP fill, wave tops |
| Ice `ice` | `#A4E4FC` | spare accent |
| Purple `purple` | `#940084` | small-enemy heads, brute head, lantern cap |
| Magenta `magenta` | `#D800CC` | second small-enemy palette |
| Pink `pink` | `#F878F8` | brute hurt flash |
| Violet `violet` | `#6844FC` | spare accent |

**Palette rules**

- **Max 3 colours + black per sprite part.** The hero is built like two stacked NES sprites: the head uses orange, yellow and green, and the body uses blue and green.
- **Ground ratio:** about 50 % `#005800`, 25 % `#503000`, 10 % `#AC7C00` road, and the rest water, stone and decals.
- **Enemy families are palette swaps** of one grid: the purple and magenta creepers share a sprite.
- **Hurt flash is a palette swap**, never an overlay: hero → white head and red body, creeper → red and white, ghost → yellow and red, brute → pink, white, yellow and red.
- **Pure black** is only for outlines, cliff lines, dithered shadows and UI windows.

## Typography

**Press Start 2P**, weight 400. Google Fonts: `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Press+Start+2P&display=swap`

- It is used for everything. Use sizes that are multiples of 8 px: 8 px for hints, 16 px for labels and stats, 24 px for the kill counter, 32 px for the clock and titles.
- Labels are **UPPERCASE in red `#F83800`** (`-LIFE-`, `XP`, `TO MIDNIGHT`). Values are white `#FCFCFC`. Titles and card names are gold `#F8B800`.
- No text shadows, no outlines, `letter-spacing: 0`. Blinking uses `steps(1)`.

```css
.label { font: 16px/1 'Press Start 2P', monospace; color: #f83800; text-transform: uppercase; }
.value { font: 16px/1 'Press Start 2P', monospace; color: #fcfcfc; text-shadow: none; }
.clock { font: 32px/1 'Press Start 2P', monospace; color: #fcfcfc; }
```

On canvas, draw text into the low-res art buffer at 8 px (the font's native 8×8 grid) so it upscales with the pixels.

## Rendering technique

1. **Art buffer.** `PS = 1.5` world units per art pixel. The upscale factor is `up = max(1, round(screenH / 240))`, and the buffer is `ceil(screenW / up) × ceil(screenH / up)`. Draw everything into the buffer with `imageSmoothingEnabled = false`, then `drawImage(buffer, 0, 0, bw * up, bh * up)` onto the display.
2. **Bake at init.** Every sprite comes from the `mk(rows, map, opt)` builder. A text grid (one char per pixel, `.` = empty) plus a char→hex map becomes a small canvas, with a 1-px black outline added on every empty pixel whose 4-neighbour is filled. Each sprite is baked as `{r, l}` (right and left facing, `l` = horizontal flip), for 2 frames and every palette variant (normal, flash, checker ghost copy).
3. **Bake ground per chunk.** Chunks are 256 world units = 171 × 171 px. The material map is evaluated per 2×2 px block, then each pixel gets its base colour or an edge colour, then decals are stamped. A generator `yield`s every few rows so baking never stalls a frame.
4. **Per frame, in this order:** ground chunks (integer positions) → animated water waves → all shadows → y-sorted props, enemies and hero → orbiting lanterns → projectiles → particles → damage numbers → (display) optional scanlines.
5. **Snap everything.** The blit helpers convert world → screen with `Math.round(x * S + ox)` and draw at an integer anchor (`feet`: bottom-centre, `mid`: centre). Never draw a sprite at a fractional position or with a transform scale.
6. **CRT hint.** Only when `up ≥ 3`, a pattern darkens the bottom display row of every art-pixel row with `rgba(0,0,0,0.16)`. This is the only alpha in the whole style, and it lives in display space.

## Background and ground

There are five materials, decided per 2×2 art-pixel block (this gives the chunky 2-px stair steps of NES tiles):

| Material | Rule (reference) | Base | Edge colours |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Plaza | octagonal rect, 88–132 × 60–92 px, `cut = 6`, ~42 % of 460-px cells | brick tile | black outer ring, light-grey `#BCBCBC` second ring |
| Water | warped noise `/520` < 0.335 | `#0000BC` | black outer ring, blue `#0058F8` second ring |
| Road | distance to 2 domain-warped Perlin zero-lines < 11 world units | `#AC7C00` | sand `#F0D0B0` next to water, dark brown `#503000` next to grass/forest |
| Forest floor | warped noise `/640` > 0.555 | `#503000` | **black** cliff line next to grass, ochre lip next to road/water |
| Grass | everything else | `#005800` | leaf-green `#00A800` lip next to any other material |

The brick tile is 12 × 6 px running bond, with rows offset by 6. Mortar (`ly === 5` or `lx === 11`) is black. The top-left 5×1 and 1×3 of each brick is `#BCBCBC`, and the rest is `#7C7C7C`. Every ~10th brick gets a 4-px black crack.

**Decals** are glyphs (`[dx, dy, colour]` triplets built from text rows). One glyph is stamped per hashed grid cell, only on its own material and never on edge pixels:

- grass tufts on an 8-px grid (`'a.a' / '.a.'`, `'a.a.a' / '.a.a.'`, and others) in `#00A800`. Density follows big fbm patches (`0.3 + dn * 0.5`), and where `dn > 0.6` the 3-row "tall grass" variants are used
- flowers on a 19-px grid: `'.w.' / 'w.w' / '.w.'` in white or gold
- forest leaf litter on a 5-px grid (42 %): single `#881400`/`#AC7C00` pixels and 2-px pairs; black 3-px twigs on a 17-px grid
- road pebbles on a 7-px grid (32 %): `#503000` dots, with `#F0D0B0` highlights

**Water** gets anchors on an 11 × 7 px grid (only where the whole 9 × 6 neighbourhood is water). A 5 × 2 px wave glyph in cyan or blue toggles between two shapes at 2.2 Hz.

**Props** are outlined sprites standing on the ground: round trees 24 × 28 (green, or 16 % autumn ochre/yellow), dead grey trees 22 × 30 in forests, bushes 18 × 10, rocks, pumpkins 11 × 8, fences 16 × 9, signposts beside roads, rows of tombstones and a stone pumpkin statue on plazas. When the hero walks behind a tree, its `see` variant (a checker copy, `checker: 0`) is drawn instead.

## Characters

The hero grid is 13 px wide and 19 rows tall. With the outline that is 15 × 21 px, about 22 × 31 world units. Verbatim from the module:

```text
......gg.....   HEAD (10 rows)          o = #E45C10 orange
.....gg......                           y = #F8D878 yellow (carved face)
..ooooooooo..                           g = #00A800 green (stem, vine sleeves)
.ooooooooooo.                           b = #0078F8 blue overalls
oooooyoooyooo   <- eyes (1-px peaks)    k = #000000 shoes
ooooyyyoyyyoo
ooooooooooooo
ooooyoyoyoyoo   <- zig-zag mouth
.oooyyyyyyyo.
..ooooooooo..
...ggggggg...   BODY (7 rows)
..ggbbbbbbb..
.gg.bbbbbbbb.
...bbbbbbbbbg
..gbbbbbbbbb.
..bbbbbbbbbb.
..bbbbbbbbb..
....bb.bb....   LEGS frame 0  |  frame 1: '...bb...bb...'
...kkk.kkk...                 |           '..kkk....kk..'
```

- **Proportions:** the head is more than half the height. A big readable face makes the character, and the body is a simple block.
- **Face:** made only from the second colour cut into the head (yellow on orange). Eyes are 3-px triangles and the mouth is an alternating row.
- **Frames:** 2 walk frames (legs together / legs apart). Idle has no leg change, just a 1-px bob at 1.8 Hz.
- **Facing:** a horizontal flip of the baked canvas (`{r, l}`).
- **Hurt:** the flash palette `{o: white, y: red, g: white, b: red}` for the first 0.4 s, then flicker.
- **Dash:** 2 afterimages 9 and 18 world units behind, all orange, with `checker: 0` and no outline.
- **Shadow:** a 12-px checker-dithered black ellipse (12 × 4) under the feet. It is skipped on flicker frames.

## Enemies and props

All enemies are text grids run through the same builder. Families differ by **silhouette first, palette second**.

**Small melee enemy (creeper):** 14 × 15 px. It has a leafy green top, a round purple head with black slit eyes, and a cream lower half with a checkered `k/c` mouth. One row of legs alternates between 2 frames, and the sprite lifts 1 px on frame 1 (a hop). Palette variants: `P = #940084` or `#D800CC`.

```text
...gg.g.gg....
....ggggg.....
......g.......
....PPPPPP....
..PPPPPPPPPP..
.PPPkPPPPPPkP.
.PPPPkkPPkkPP.
.PPPPckPPckPP.
.PPPPccPPccPP.
.cPcPcPcPcPcP.     <- checker seam between the two colour bands
.cccccccccccc.
..cckckckckcc.     <- teeth
...cckkkkkkc..
....cccccc....
...c..cc..c...     legs frame 0 (frame 1: '....c.cc.c....')
```

**Fast / floating enemy (ghost):** a 13-px-wide white `#FCFCFC` head with cyan `#3CBCFC` shading and black eyes and mouth, plus a 6-row tail. The tail is built with `tailFrom: 10`: rows from 10 on keep only pixels where `(x + y + parity) & 1 == 0` and get **no outline**. Two parities are baked, and the parity flips with the frame counter, so the tail shimmers like NES flicker transparency. It hovers 3–4 px above an 8-px shadow, and its 2 tail frames alternate at 3 Hz.

**Brute (colossus):** 22 × 27 px. The top is a purple turnip head with gold eyes. The body is ochre `#AC7C00` with dark-brown `#503000` cracks and a checkered black mouth, and it has arms. Legs have 2 frames, each footfall spawns a dust sprite, and it casts a 24-px shadow. It dies with a big explosion (`R = 1.7`) and 3 extra booms.

**Pickups:** small gems are 5 × 6 px cyan/blue diamonds and big gems are 7 × 8 px gold/orange. Both are outlined and spin through 4 frames whose width shrinks to a sliver.

**Orbiting lantern:** a 9 × 10 px purple-capped cream lantern whose glass blinks between gold and white at 4 Hz.

**Props:** trees use canopy circles. The lower-right rim (`dd > 0.72 && nx + ny > 0.45`) is black, the upper-left crescent is the light colour, and a global checker shade (`gx + gy > 0.55`, every other pixel black) is laid over the canopy. Tombstones are white with a light-grey right side and a black cross. Everything gets the black outline. Shadows (checker ellipses) go only under trees (20 px), dead trees (12) and the statue (16).

## Effects and particles

- **Explosion (death):** 4 procedural frames on an odd `ceil(18R)` square, no outline: (0) white core + gold cross; (1) white disc, gold ring, red diagonal rays; (2) red/gold checker ring; (3) 8 red/gold bits flying out. Each frame lasts 1/4 of the 1-s death.
- **Spawn puff:** 3 frames on a 17 × 15 grid. Overlapping white circles with a light-grey bottom grow, then 7 grey dots in a ring. 0.2 s per frame, and the last frame lingers over the new enemy.
- **Hit:** 2 square particles (2 px) in the enemy's own two colours (creeper: cream + purple; ghost: white + cyan), plus a 1-px white spark for 0.08 s. Gravity 160.
- **Kill:** 6 particles (14 for brutes), speed 50 to 70, gravity 220, life 0.6–0.9 s. They **blink** (skip odd frames) in their last 30 %.
- **Pickup / hurt / level-up:** a 3-frame star: 3×3 white plus, 5×5 star with gold arms, 4 corner dots. Cyan for small gems. Level-up throws a ring of 10 stars.
- **Projectile:** a 2×2 cream/white seed (outlined to 4×4) that alternates colour every frame. A 1-px gold/cream dot 4 px behind and an orange dot 7 px behind form the trail.
- **Damage numbers:** 3×5 bitmap digits, white, 1-px gaps, 8-neighbour black outline (`diag: true`). Crits are gold at 2× scale. Cache per value.

## Lighting, shadows and post-processing

- **No lighting.** The world is evenly lit with flat colour, and light is implied only by sprite highlights (upper-left on canopies) and blinking glows.
- **Shadows** are black ellipses `w × round(w/3)` where only checker pixels are set (`(x + y + par) & 1`). Two parities are baked, and the one where `(screenX + screenY) & 1` matches is picked so the dither stays locked to the screen grid. Sizes: 8 (ghost), 12 (hero, small enemy), 16, 20 (tree), 24 (brute).
- **Post:** none in the world. On the display only, when `up ≥ 3`, faint scanlines darken one display row per art row (`rgba(0,0,0,0.16)`).
- **Menus dim** the world with a **checker dither** (CSS `repeating-conic-gradient(#000 0 25%, transparent 0 50%) 0 0 / 8px 8px`), never with a translucent overlay.

## UI and HUD

The HUD is a solid **black status bar** across the top, like an NES status area:

- Left: a red `-LIFE-` label, then a row of hearts. Each heart is the 8 × 7 grid `'.rr.rr..','rWrrrrr.','rrrrrrr.','rrrrrrr.','.rrrrr..','..rrr...','...r....'`, drawn at 3× (24 × 21 px). Full hearts are red with a white glint, empty hearts are `#881400`. The bar is a repeat-x of hearts clipped to the HP percentage, with a white `100/100` beside it.
- Centre: the clock in 32 px white, with a 16 px red uppercase label below.
- Right: the kill counter, a 48-px enemy icon, a gold `×` and the count in white.
- Below: a red `XP` label and a 16-px-tall bar with a 4-px white frame. The fill repeats 8 px cyan, 4 px blue, 4 px black, giving a segmented meter. `LV 4` sits at the right.
- **Windows** (level-up cards, pause, stats) are black with a double white border, made from box-shadow rings. A blinking white triangle cursor marks the selected card. Card names are gold and keys are red.

```css
.hud { font-family: 'Press Start 2P', monospace; color: #fcfcfc; background: #000;
  padding: 14px 32px 12px; box-shadow: 0 4px 0 #000; image-rendering: pixelated; }
.hud .label { font-size: 16px; color: #f83800; text-transform: uppercase; }
.xp { height: 16px; background: #000; box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px #fcfcfc; border-radius: 0; }
.xp-fill { height: 100%; transition: none;
  background: repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, #3cbcfc 0 8px, #0058f8 8px 12px, #000 12px 16px); }
.window { background: #000; border: 4px solid #fcfcfc; border-radius: 0;
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px #000, inset 0 0 0 4px #000, inset 0 0 0 8px #fcfcfc; }
.dim { background: repeating-conic-gradient(#000 0 25%, transparent 0 50%) 0 0 / 8px 8px; }
.blink { animation: nesblink 1s steps(1) infinite; }
@keyframes nesblink { 0% { opacity: 1; } 50% { opacity: 0; } }
```

Icons are 16 × 16 text-grid sprites with the same palette rules. Render them as pixelated SVG data URLs (`shape-rendering='crispEdges'`, one `<rect>` per run) or as canvases scaled by an integer factor.

## Motion and animation

- **2 frames for everything.** Hero walk: `floor(anim) & 1`. Small enemy: `floor(anim * 1.6) & 1`, with a 1-px hop on frame 1. Brute: `floor(anim * 1.2) & 1`, with a dust puff on each frame change. Ghost tail: 3 Hz, plus a hover toggle of 3/4 px at 2 Hz.
- **Idle bob:** 1 px at 1.8 Hz. **Gem spin:** sequence `0,0,0,1,2,3` at 9 fps, 1-px bob at 2.5 Hz, and a pop arc of up to 8 px when spawned.
- **Snap, don't ease.** Positions are rounded to art pixels every frame, and the camera moves in whole pixels. UI has `transition: none` and blinks use `steps(1)`.
- **Flicker = invisibility.** For invulnerable actors, fading particles (last 30 %) and fading numbers (last 25 %), skip drawing when `frameCounter & 2`.
- **Death:** a 4-frame explosion over 1 s. **Spawn:** a 3-frame puff over 0.6 s before the enemy appears.

## Do and don't

**Do**

- Encode every sprite as a text grid plus a char→colour map, and let the builder add the black outline.
- Keep each sprite to 3 colours + black, all from the NES palette table.
- Round every blit to whole art pixels and upscale with smoothing off.
- Use checker pixels for transparency and shadows, and flicker for invulnerability.
- Create enemy variants by palette swap before drawing new grids.
- Give every ground boundary a 1-px lip or a black cliff line.
- Use Press Start 2P at multiples of 8 px, with uppercase red labels.

**Don't**

- Don't use gradients, glows, blur, alpha fades or anti-aliased shapes in the world.
- Don't use colours outside the NES palette (no `#333`, no pastel mixes).
- Don't use coloured or 2-px outlines.
- Don't rotate or scale sprites. Bake extra frames or flips instead.
- Don't animate ordinary actors with more than 2 frames.
- Don't use rounded, blurred or tweened UI.
- Don't put noise textures on the ground. Use only flat fills and glyph decals.

## Implementation recipe

1. Set the view: 360 world units tall, `PS = 1.5`, a 240-row art buffer, integer upscale `up = max(1, round(screenH / 240))`, smoothing off.
2. Copy the NES palette table (`PALETTE` in `starter.js`) and the `mk(rows, map, opt)` sprite builder.
3. Draw your hero as a ~13 × 19 text grid: a big head with a 2-colour face, a small body in 1–2 colours, and 2 leg rows × 2 frames. Bake `{r, l}` for both frames, plus a flash palette.
4. Draw each enemy family as one grid (small: ~14 × 15, brute: ~22 × 27) and palette-swap it for variants. Floating or ethereal enemies get a checker tail (`tailFrom`, two parities).
5. Build effect frames procedurally on small grids: explosion (4 frames), puff (3), star (3), gem spin (4), 3×5 digits.
6. Ground: define 3–5 materials from noise or level data on a 2×2 px block grid. Fill base colours and apply the edge table (lip, cliff or ring), then stamp decal glyphs on hashed grid cells. Bake per chunk with a generator.
7. Props: build trees and bushes procedurally from circles (light upper-left crescent, black lower-right rim, checker shade). Write rocks, tombs, fences and signs as grids.
8. Each frame: blit chunks → 2-frame tile animations → checker shadows → y-sorted actors → orbitals → projectiles → particles → numbers, all at rounded art-pixel positions.
9. HUD: a black bar, Press Start 2P, red labels, a heart row, a segmented XP bar, and double-bordered black windows. Dim the world with checker dither.
10. Check: zoom into a screenshot and verify that every pixel is a palette colour, every sprite has a black 1-px rim, and no pixel is blended.

## Code

Everything below runs on its own. `starter.js` contains the full preview scene (ground baker, all sprites, HUD). The complete reference module is `../../js/styles/nes8bit.js`.

**1. The sprite builder: text grid → outlined NES sprite (ported 1:1).**

```js
function mk(rows, map, opt = {}) {
  const h = rows.length, w = Math.max(...rows.map((r) => r.length));
  const o = opt.outline === false ? 0 : 1, W = w + 2 * o, H = h + 2 * o;
  const cell = new Array(W * H).fill(null), src = new Uint8Array(W * H);
  const tailFrom = opt.tailFrom ?? 1e9, par = opt.parity || 0;
  for (let y = 0; y < h; y++) for (let x = 0; x < rows[y].length; x++) {
    const c = map[rows[y][x]]; if (!c) continue;
    const i = (y + o) * W + x + o;
    if (y >= tailFrom) { if (((x + y + par) & 1) === 0) cell[i] = c; src[i] = 2; } // checker tail, no outline
    else { cell[i] = c; src[i] = 1; }
  }
  if (o) for (let y = 0; y < H; y++) for (let x = 0; x < W; x++) {
    const i = y * W + x; if (src[i]) continue;
    let n = (x > 0 && src[i - 1] === 1) || (x < W - 1 && src[i + 1] === 1) || (y > 0 && src[i - W] === 1) || (y < H - 1 && src[i + W] === 1);
    if (!n && opt.diag) n = (x > 0 && y > 0 && src[i - W - 1] === 1) || (x < W - 1 && y > 0 && src[i - W + 1] === 1) ||
      (x > 0 && y < H - 1 && src[i + W - 1] === 1) || (x < W - 1 && y < H - 1 && src[i + W + 1] === 1);
    if (n) cell[i] = '#000000';
  }
  if (opt.checker !== undefined) for (let i = 0; i < W * H; i++) if ((((i % W) + ((i / W) | 0)) & 1) !== opt.checker) cell[i] = null;
  const c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width = W; c.height = H;
  const ctx = c.getContext('2d'), img = ctx.createImageData(W, H);
  cell.forEach((hex, i) => { if (!hex) return; const v = parseInt(hex.slice(1), 16);
    img.data.set([v >> 16, (v >> 8) & 255, v & 255, 255], i * 4); });
  ctx.putImageData(img, 0, 0);
  return c;
}
// usage: a ghost (head rows 0-9 solid, tail rows 10+ checkered), two parities
const GHOST_ROWS = ['...WWWWW.....', '..WWWWWWW....', '.WWWWWWWWW...', '.WWWkkWWkkW..', '.WWWkkWWkkW..', '.BWWWWWWWWWW.',
  '.BWWWWkkWWWWW', '.BBWWkkkkWWW.', '..BWWWkkWWW..', '..BBWWWWWWB..', '..BBBWWWWBB..', '...BBWWWBB...', '...BBBWBB....',
  '....BBBB.....', '....BBB......', '.....B.......'];
const ghost = [0, 1].map((p) => mk(GHOST_ROWS, { W: '#FCFCFC', B: '#3CBCFC', k: '#000000' }, { tailFrom: 10, parity: p }));
```

**2. Pixel-snapped blitting and the low-res buffer.**

```js
const PS = 1.5;                                        // world units per art pixel
function setupBuffer(display) {
  const up = Math.max(1, Math.round(display.height / (360 / PS)));
  const buf = document.createElement('canvas');
  buf.width = Math.ceil(display.width / up); buf.height = Math.ceil(display.height / up);
  return { buf, ctx: buf.getContext('2d'), up };
}
// world -> art pixel, always rounded; anchor = bottom-centre of the sprite ("feet")
function blitFeet(ctx, img, wx, wy, cam, lift = 0) {
  const x = Math.round((wx - cam.x) / PS + ctx.canvas.width / 2);
  const y = Math.round((wy - cam.y) / PS + ctx.canvas.height / 2);
  ctx.drawImage(img, x - (img.width >> 1), y - (img.height - 1 + lift));
}
function present(display, b) {
  const d = display.getContext('2d');
  d.imageSmoothingEnabled = false;
  d.drawImage(b.buf, 0, 0, b.buf.width * b.up, b.buf.height * b.up);
  if (b.up >= 3) { d.fillStyle = 'rgba(0,0,0,0.16)'; for (let y = b.up - 1; y < display.height; y += b.up) d.fillRect(0, y, display.width, 1); }
}
```

**3. Tile-language edge rules for the ground (per pixel, after the 2×2-block material map).**

```js
// mat: Uint8Array with a margin M around the chunk, EW = row width. 0 grass, 1 forest, 2 road, 3 water, 4 plaza
function edgeColour(mat, i, EW, C, brick) {
  const m = mat[i], n = [mat[i - 1], mat[i + 1], mat[i - EW], mat[i + EW]];
  const diff = n.some((q) => q !== m);
  const far = mat[i - 2] !== m || mat[i + 2] !== m || mat[i - 2 * EW] !== m || mat[i + 2 * EW] !== m;
  if (m === 4) return diff ? C.k : far ? C.g1 : brick();          // black ring, light-grey ring, bricks
  if (m === 3) return diff ? C.k : far ? C.blue : C.navy;           // black ring, blue ring, navy
  if (m === 0) return diff ? C.gr1 : C.gr0;                         // light-green lip on grass
  if (m === 1) return n.includes(0) ? C.k : diff ? C.ochre : C.br0; // black cliff vs grass
  return n.includes(3) ? C.sand : diff ? C.br0 : C.ochre;           // road: sand at water, brown edge
}
```

**4. Checker shadow and invulnerability flicker.**

```js
function shadowSprite(w, par) {
  const h = Math.max(2, Math.round(w / 3)), rows = [];
  for (let y = 0; y < h; y++) {
    let s = '';
    for (let x = 0; x < w; x++) {
      const dx = (x + 0.5 - w / 2) / (w / 2), dy = (y + 0.5 - h / 2) / (h / 2);
      s += dx * dx + dy * dy <= 1 && ((x + y + par) & 1) === 0 ? 'k' : '.';
    }
    rows.push(s);
  }
  return mk(rows, { k: '#000000' }, { outline: false });
}
// pick the parity that matches the screen grid so the dither never crawls
const pickShadow = (set, sx, sy) => set[(sx + sy) & 1];
// flicker: skip drawing on every other 2-frame window while invulnerable
const visible = (frame, invulnerable) => !(invulnerable && (frame & 2));
```

## Adapting it to your game

- **Keep fixed:** the NES palette table, 3 colours + black per sprite, the 1-px black auto-outline, 2 animation frames, rounding to art pixels, checker transparency and flicker, Press Start 2P with red uppercase labels, and the black HUD bar.
- **Free to change:** which palette entries you pick for your biome. A dungeon could use `#7C7C7C`, `#BCBCBC` and `#503000` floors with `#881400` lava, and a snow level `#FCFCFC`, `#A4E4FC` and `#0058F8`. The materials and edge table, the sprite grids and the sizes are yours too.
- **New characters:** start from a 13 × 19 (hero) or 14 × 15 (minion) grid with a big head and face, then palette-swap for variants. Bosses can be built from several outlined grids stacked (head + body + legs) as long as each part stays at ≤ 3 colours.
- **Side-view games:** use the same builder for 16 × 16 tiles. Give the ground surfaces the grass-lip and black-cliff rules and keep the 8-px decal grid.
- **Other resolutions:** keep `PS` so that the view is about 240 rows tall (NES), and only ever upscale by integers.

## Performance notes

- Sprites are tiny canvases baked once at init: 2 frames × 2 facings × palette variants, plus effect frames and shadows in 6 sizes. Damage numbers are cached per value (the cache is cleared after 300).
- Ground: the reference samples the noise fields on an 8-px grid, bilinearly interpolates them per 2×2 block, and bakes 171 × 171 px chunks in a generator that yields every 4–8 rows, so bakes spread over frames.
- Per frame: only `drawImage` blits, a few wave `fillRect`s and the optional scanline pattern. Thousands of actors stay well under 8 ms. The starter scene draws in about 1 ms.
- Avoid per-frame `getImageData`. Keep all pixel loops at bake time.

## Copy-paste prompt

```text
Build my game <X> in the "8-Bit Arcade" (NES) style:
- Render into a low-res buffer: 1 art pixel = 1.5 world units, view = 240 art rows, integer upscale, imageSmoothingEnabled = false.
- Only use NES 2C02 palette colours: #000000 #FCFCFC #BCBCBC #7C7C7C #005800 #00A800 #58D854 #503000 #AC7C00 #F0D0B0
  #FCE0A8 #881400 #F83800 #E45C10 #F8B800 #F8D878 #0000BC #0058F8 #0078F8 #3CBCFC #940084 #D800CC #F878F8.
- Every sprite is a text grid (one char per pixel) + char->colour map; a builder adds a 1-px pure black outline.
- Max 3 colours + black per sprite part; big heads with 2-colour faces; exactly 2 animation frames; flip for facing.
- Variants and hurt flashes are palette swaps. No gradients, no alpha, no anti-aliasing, no rotation or scaling in the world.
- Transparency = checkerboard pixels (ghost tails, afterimages, shadows); invulnerability = flicker (skip when frame & 2).
- Ground = flat material areas on a 2x2-pixel block grid: grass #005800 with #00A800 lip, forest #503000 behind a black cliff
  line, road #AC7C00 with #503000 edge, water #0000BC with black + #0058F8 rings, 12x6 grey brick plazas.
- Decals: 2-row grass tufts on an 8-px grid, 3x3 flowers, 1-px leaf litter, pebbles; water waves toggle 2 frames.
- Effects: 4-frame white/gold/red explosion, 3-frame puff and star, 4-frame spinning gems, 3x5 bitmap damage digits.
- Round every blit to whole art pixels; snap, never ease.
- HUD: black status bar, Press Start 2P at 8/16/32 px, red uppercase labels, rows of 8x7 hearts, segmented cyan/blue XP bar,
  black windows with double white borders, checker-dither dimming behind menus.
```
