<!-- style: stainedglass · https://miwale.com/styles/library/stainedglass/STYLE.md -->

# Cathedral Glass — Game Art Style Spec

> A living cathedral window: jewel-tone glass pieces in dark lead came, lit from behind by warm light and coloured rays.

The whole game world is one backlit stained-glass window. Floor, props, characters, pickups, HUD icons and even damage numbers are built from the same single unit: a **glass piece** with a luminous off-centre core, a darker rim, two faint cathedral-glass streaks and an occasional glint, separated from its neighbours by near-black **lead came** (`#17131c`). The floor is a per-pixel Voronoi mosaic whose material regions (green meadow, crimson leaf carpet, amber path lanes, night-blue glass, grey diamond quarries) are separated by heavier lead. Props cast coloured light pools on the floor, glowing faces shine through, and a slow layer of coloured light rays drifts over the screen. The reference game (*Jack vs. the Turnip Ancestors*, a top-down horde survivor with a pumpkin-headed hero) is used below as an example only.

## At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Family | Mosaic · Stained Glass |
| Mood | luminous, sacred, festive, handcrafted, storybook |
| Best for | top-down survivor / horde games, fairy-tale action RPGs, puzzle and match games, holiday-themed arcade games, card/board UIs |
| Renderer | Canvas 2D, fully procedural, no image assets |
| Pixel art | No — native resolution, sprites baked at 3–5 px per world unit |
| Difficulty | 7/10 — every new figure has to be split sensibly into glass pieces and still stay readable; the ground is already busy |
| Fonts | Cinzel Decorative (700/900), Cinzel (500/700/900) |
| Key colours | lead `#17131c`, meadow `#2a6e48`, crimson `#a23a4e`, amber `#c28a38`, pumpkin `#ff8a22`, candle gold `#ffd23a`, amethyst `#9351c8`, ruby `#e3203c`, aqua `#3ac6c6`, gold fillet `#d9ad4e` |

## When to use it

Good fits:
- **Top-down horde / survivor games** — the fat lead silhouette keeps 200+ enemies readable on a busy floor (see the reference screenshots).
- **Fairy-tale, religious, medieval or seasonal themes** (harvest, Halloween, Christmas, saints, knights, gardens).
- **Puzzle, match-3 and board games** — the piece-and-lead grammar maps naturally onto tiles and cards.
- **Menus, level-up screens, card games** — arched leaded cards with gold fillets look premium.

Bad fits:
- **Fast competitive shooters** that need a calm, low-contrast background — the floor is intentionally busy.
- **Gritty realism, horror without whimsy, hard sci-fi** — glass reads as warm and sacred.
- **Pixel-art or retro games** — this is smooth, antialiased vector-like glass.
- **Minimalist UIs** — everything here is ornamented.

## Color palette

| Swatch | Hex | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lead came | `#17131c` | All outlines, seams, text strokes, UI borders |
| Lead ridge | `#544e60` | Metallic highlight in the centre of floor lead (rgb 84,78,96) |
| Meadow green | `#2a6e48` | Main floor; family `#327a4e #265f44 #3a8250 #2a7058 #2f6c40` |
| Olive meadow | `#5f7a33` | Alternate meadow patches; `#55702f #4c652b #687f38 #59702d` |
| Leaf carpet crimson | `#a23a4e` | Autumn region; `#8e2a3c #7c2234 #ad4c38 #963046 #a35c2c #b0405a` |
| Amber path | `#c28a38` | Path centre lane `#cf9a44 #b98034 #d4a24c`; outer lanes `#a8742e #b07c33 #9c6a2a #b5813a` |
| Night glass | `#304296` | Graveyard region; `#28388a #3a2e86 #46348e #243478 #2c4e90 #383a92` |
| Clear quarry | `#646e8a` | Diamond-quarry plazas; `#5c6884 #6c7088 #58647e #6a6486 #62727e` |
| Pumpkin orange | `#ff8a22` | Hero head ribs `#e2681a #ffa63c`; pumpkin props `#c85a14 #e47820 #f39232` |
| Candle gold | `#ffd23a` | Carved faces, flames (`#ff9a2a`, `#fff2a0`), lantern faces `#ffe066` |
| Hem gold | `#f2c040` | Clasps, hems (`#e0a830`), fruit jewels, stars |
| Cloak green | `#2a6e40` | Hero clothes; `#1f5a34 #184a2c #2f7a3c #22603e` |
| Scarf red | `#c4283e` | Hero accent; `#a51d34 #d8404e` |
| Amethyst | `#9351c8` | Small enemy caps, variants `[#7a3fae #9351c8 #6a3298]`, `[#a8378c #c24ca2 #8e2c76]`, `[#5a48b8 #7060d0 #4a3a9e]` |
| Ivory | `#f4e2b4` | Small enemy bodies `#e8cc90`, roots `#e6cf9a #cfae72`, seeds `#fff0c4 #e6c27a` |
| Ember | `#ff5a26` | Angry glowing eyes |
| Opal | `#e9e9fb` | Ghost mosaic; `#f0f5ff #dde8fb #f6ecfb #e0f3f4 #fbf6ec`; hollow eyes `#1e2452` |
| Earth brown | `#7e5a3c` | Brute body, trunks; `#6b4a32 #5a3b2a #8a6440 #644530` |
| Dusk violet | `#704690` | Brute shoulders/arms; `#5e3a7a #52306a #7c5098` |
| Ruby | `#e3203c` | Brute core, hearts; `#ff4a5a #b8142e #ff7080` |
| Aqua gem | `#3ac6c6` | XP gems `#8ff6ea #c4fff6 #279fb0`; big gem `#ffe27a #f0a82a #fff4c0 #d88a1a` |
| Window gold fillet | `#d9ad4e` | 2 px gold ring inside UI lead borders |

Palette rules:
- **Lead is the only dark.** About 12–18 % of floor pixels are lead. No glass piece goes darker than its colour × 0.6; pure black/white never appear as a surface.
- **Floor = cool/earthy mid tones, actors = warmer, paler, brighter.** Ivory-and-amethyst turnips, opal ghosts and an orange pumpkin all separate from green/crimson floor glass.
- **Gold and yellow mean "light source"**: faces, eyes, flames, jewels, UI numbers. Don't spend gold on large surfaces.
- **Never flat**: every piece picks a random swatch from a 4–7 colour family and gets ±6–7 % brightness jitter.
- Dark accents inside actors (mouths `#3a1a2a`, hollow eyes `#1e2452`) are still glass, not lead.

## Typography

**Cinzel Decorative** — weights 700, 900 — titles, timer, kill counter, damage numbers, card names.
`https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Cinzel+Decorative:wght@700;900`

**Cinzel** — weights 500, 700, 900 — labels, HP text, card descriptions, hints.
`https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Cinzel:wght@500;700;900`

```css
.title { font: 900 66px/1 'Cinzel Decorative', 'Cinzel', serif; letter-spacing: 4px; color: #ffd86a; }
.label { font: 700 11px/1 'Cinzel', Georgia, serif; letter-spacing: 3px; color: #cfdaff; text-shadow: 0 1px 2px #17131c; }
.card-desc { font: 700 15px/1.3 'Cinzel', serif; color: #2a1a10; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #fbefcf, #e8cf96); }
```

Text effects:
- **Lead outline via text-shadow**: 12 shadows around a circle (`cos(i/12·2π)·w px sin(i/12·2π)·w px 0 #17131c`) with w = 1.5–3.5 px, plus an optional `0 0 14px rgba(255,200,90,.7)` glow for headline gold text.
- Gold text colours: `#ffdf7e`, `#ffd86a`, `#ffe7a0`, `#ffe08a`; parchment descriptions use dark brown `#2a1a10` on cream.
- **Canvas damage numbers**: `900 9.2u` (crit `12.5u`) Cinzel Decorative, stroked twice in lead (width 0.26 × font size, once shifted down by 0.06 × size), gradient fill (crit `#fff6c0 → #ffcf40 → #ff7a1a`, normal `#ffffff → #e6eeff → #a9c0ee`), then a `source-atop` white 50 % band across the top 22 %.

## Rendering technique

The visible world is 360 world units tall; the hero is ~24 units wide and ~42 tall at its 1.15 draw scale.

At init:
1. Compute the sprite resolution `K = clamp(round(screenPxPerUnit × 1.5), 3, 5)` px per world unit.
2. **Bake every figure with the two-pass Painter** (`build(box, fn, mode, seed)`): a figure is a function that declares parts back-to-front. Pass 1 (`outline`) fills *and* strokes each part's shape in lead with lineWidth `2 × 0.95` units — the union becomes one clean fat outer came. Pass 2 (`fill`) clips into each part, paints its glass cells, then strokes the part border at `0.55 × 1.2` units and every cell edge at 0.55 units.
3. Bake a **flash copy** of every animated frame with mode `flash` (each piece mixed 58 % toward warm white `rgb(255,250,232)`, glow pieces 40 %) — the lead stays dark.
4. Bake glow sprites (radial gradients), glint stars, shard sprites (3 shapes × 12 colours), projectile, trail, beams, props (3 trees, 2 bushes, 2 arches, 2 candle groups, 3 graves, 3 pumpkin groups) and HUD icons with the same Painter (icons at outline 2.0 / inner 1.15).
5. Bake the screen overlay per screen size (vignette, frame, ripples) plus a half-resolution light layer.

Per frame (renderer order):
1. Ground chunks (256 units, generated per pixel as time-sliced generators and cached).
2. Gems → shadows/light pools under actors → y-sorted props, enemies and player → orbitals → projectiles → particles → damage numbers.
3. Screen overlay: dark layer with `source-over`, light layer with `lighter`, offset `sin(t·0.12) × 2.5 % W`.

Every actor draw is just `drawImage` of a baked canvas with `setTransform(S·sx, 0, 0, S·sy, …)`, optional rotation, plus 1–3 additive glow blits.

**Glass piece shading** (`Painter.glass`): colour × (1 ± 0.06) → radial gradient from `(cx − 0.25r, cy − 0.3r, 0.05r)` to `(cx, cy, 1.3r)` with stops `0: mix(col, white, .3)`, `.48: col`, `1: col × .64`. Glow pieces: `0: mix(col, rgb(255,255,236), .78)`, `1: col × .9`. Pieces with r > 1.4 units get two curved streaks (white 12 %, width 0.16 r, random angle) and, with 50 % chance and r > 1.6, an elliptical glint (0.26 r × 0.1 r, rotated −0.7, white 55 %) at the upper left.

## Background and ground

The floor is computed **per pixel** in world space so it is seamless and identical between chunks:

1. **Fields** on a 4-unit grid (`GSTEP = 4`), 5 layers: leaf carpet `warped(x/640, …) − 0.565`, night glass `warped(x/860, …) − 0.585`, path = a domain-warped fbm at scale 1150 (iso-line), plaza `fbm(x/520) − 0.66`, macro brightness `fbm(x/1150)`.
2. Per pixel the 4 surrounding nodes are interpolated bilinearly; value divided by the bilinear gradient magnitude gives a **signed distance in world units** — this makes borders smooth curves of constant lead width. A path pixel is where `21 − |d| > 0` (42 units wide).
3. Material priority: plaza > path > night > leaf carpet > meadow. `re` = distance to the nearest region border.
4. **Voronoi glass**: jittered grid (sites at `(i + 0.08 + 0.84·hash) × C`), cell size C: meadow 20, leaf carpet 15, night 23, path 30. Find the 3 nearest sites in the 3×3 neighbourhood; edge distance `e = (d2² − d1²) / (2·|s2 − s1|)` for the 2nd and 3rd site, combined with `smin(e1, e2, 1.6)` so vertices round off. The path additionally splits into 3 lanes at ±7 units (different palettes, extra lead along the lane lines). Plazas use 45° diamond quarries: `(x ± y) / 17`, distance to the diamond edge × 0.7071.
5. **Per-piece colour**: hashed swatch × brightness 0.93–1.07; meadow switches to the olive family where `hash < smoothstep(0.42, 0.6, fbm(site/380))`.
6. **Luminance**: `(0.6 + 0.38·smoothstep(e / (0.34·C))) × streak × (0.86 + (macro − 0.3)·0.5)`, streak = `1 + 0.055·sin((x·cos a + y·sin a)·f + φ)` per piece.
7. **Lead**: coverage `max(0.78 − eP, 1.2 − re) × res + 0.5` (antialiased over one pixel); colour ramps from `rgb(28,24,34)` at the edge to `rgb(84,78,96)` at the centre with `q = tl² × 0.85` — a soft metallic ridge.
8. **Decals** (seeded jittered scatter, only where the material is safe within a radius): 5-petal leaded flowers (`#e8668a #f2c040 #7ab8f0 #efe6ff #c87ae8`, orange centre) with two leaves on meadow every ~44 units; autumn leaves (`#e09a30 #d0602a #f2c040 #b8402a #e87a3a`) with a lead midrib on the carpet; 5-point gold stars on night glass; amber roundels on the path; seedy bubbles on quarries. Each decal piece is a `glassBlob` (gradient + 0.55–0.65 unit lead).
9. **Glints**: every ~24 units, 32 % chance, a diagonal white stroke (alpha 0.2, width 0.55, length 1.6–4) — sometimes doubled.
10. **Prop pools**: contact shadow `rgba(16,12,24,0.38)` ellipse, then additive coloured radial pools (e.g. arch window: red, blue, gold pools at alpha 0.26; candles warm `rgb(255,180,70)` 0.3; graves cold `rgb(150,200,255)` 0.12).

## Characters

**Hero** (reference: pumpkin-headed Jack, sprite box −14…14 × −38…3, drawn ×1.15):
- **Boots**: two capsules (`CAP`) r ≈ 2.1, `#4a2f22 / #5d3b29`, swinging ±2.2 units over 4 frames.
- **Cloak**: 7-point trapezoid (−8.8…8.8 wide at the hem, 4.6 at the shoulders, −17.2…−2.6 tall) BSP-cut into pieces ≤ 38 units² in 5 greens.
- **Golden hem**: zig-zag band split into 3 gold pieces (`#f2c040 #e0a830 #f2c040`) with thinner outline (0.5).
- **Clasp jewel**: a 1.5-unit glowing gold circle.
- **Scarf**: back tail piece + front band split diagonally into two reds.
- **Stem + leaf**: curved stem `#4f7c2c`, one leaf as two half pieces split on the midrib.
- **Head**: ellipse rx 10.6, ry 8.4 centred at y −24.6, divided into 5 vertical **rib lenses** (boundaries −1.05, −0.64, −0.22, 0.22, 0.64, 1.05) coloured dark-mid-light-mid-dark orange — this gives roundness without any shading pass.
- **Face**: triangle eyes, triangle nose and a 17-point jagged grin as **glow pieces** in `#ffd23a`, offset 1.5 units towards the facing side, plus two additive glows (warm halo r 16 × 1.25 at alpha ~0.32, gold r 10 × 0.55 flickering).
- 4 walk frames (feet offsets `[0, 2.2, 0, −2.2]`, back-foot lift `[0, .8, 0, .8]`); facing = horizontal flip.
- A warm additive light pool on the floor under the hero (r 20 × 0.4 squashed, ×1.6) pulsing 0.85 ± 0.15.

General construction rules for any new character:
- Big readable primitives first (ellipse, capsule, polygon), then cut them into glass with: `mosaic()` (BSP cuts with jittered angle ±0.6 rad until each piece ≤ maxArea), `ribCells()` for round fruit/heads, `leafCells()` for leaves/wings/ears, explicit polygon cells for faces and facets.
- Piece area roughly 30–80 units² on bodies, 3–15 units² on faces and details.
- One idea per colour family per part; jitter does the rest.

## Enemies and props

All enemies use the same Painter; their sprites are baked in 4 frames plus flash copies.

- **Small melee enemy** (turnip, box −14…14 × −34…4, drawn ×0.92): bulb = turnip bezier outline, cut into 3 coloured cap pieces (one of 3 jewel variants: amethyst, magenta, indigo) over 2 ivory pieces with a jagged seam; 3 leaves fanning out of the top swaying ±0.12 rad; two root-leg capsules; two angry quad eyes as ember glow pieces; a lead frown line. Hops with ±0.09 rad rock.
- **Fast enemy** (ghost, box −11…14 × −27…3): arched sheet with a 4-scallop animated hem, cut into opal mosaic pieces ≤ 70 units² with low jitter (0.06), hollow navy eye/mouth ellipses, a reaching arm capsule, cold pupils `rgba(160,220,255,.9)`. After baking, the bottom 9 units are erased with a `destination-out` gradient (0 → 0.85) so it dissolves. Drawn at alpha 0.86, floating 4 units up with a cold additive glow.
- **Brute** (colossus, box −31…31 × −64…3): egg body (bezier, ~44 wide × 40 tall) BSP-cut into pieces ≤ 78 units², violet above y −31 and brown below (with ±3 unit noise on the boundary); capsule legs and arms with their own mosaics; a leaf crown of 5 leaves; a 4-facet **ruby core** of glow pieces with a pulsing ruby glow (0.45 ± 0.25); amber glow eyes; a jagged dark maw. Ground contact: a dark ellipse 19 × 5.5 plus an additive ruby glow on the floor.
- **Pickups**: XP gem = a kite split into 4 facets around (0, −1.4), two of them glowing, aqua (big gem: gold with a ruby centre); bobs ±1.1 units, aqua additive halo, rare twinkle glint. Projectile = two-piece seed.
- **Props**: trees = BSP trunk + 5 foliage lobes (ellipse mosaic + 2–3 leaf pieces each) in autumn/summer/blossom families with glowing fruit jewels; bushes = 3 lobes + berry jewels; gothic arch = stone mosaic frame, jewel-mosaic window (pieces ≤ 11 units²), mullion, quatrefoil with ruby centre; candles = ivory pieces + layered flame glow pieces + flickering warm glow; graves = grey mosaic slabs with an inlaid pale-blue glowing cross; pumpkins = rib lenses, sometimes carved and glowing.

**Readability with many enemies**: every enemy has the same fat lead outline, so overlapping crowds read as stacked cut-outs; enemy colours (ivory, amethyst, opal) are deliberately absent from floor palettes; eyes glow; there are only 3 recurring silhouettes with distinct sizes (small 26 units, ghost 28, brute 64); and shadows are simple dark ellipses that anchor each one.

## Effects and particles

- **Shatter (kill)**: 8 shards for small enemies, 6 for ghosts, 16 for brutes, in the enemy's colours (e.g. cap colour, cream, green). Shards are baked leaded triangles/quads (outline 0.4). Physics: speed 55–75 × 0.5–1.2, vz 70, gravity 300, drag 1.4, life 0.9–1.4 s, spin ±8 rad/s, fake tumble via y-scale `0.25 + 0.75·|cos|`, glint flash when edge-on. Plus 2–5 glints and, for brutes, a ruby ring.
- **Death pop**: for 0.22 s the flash copy is drawn scaled 1 → 1.18 and fading.
- **Spawn**: 6–10 shards swirl in from radius 30–50 units (ease-out quad over 0.85 s), the body fades in from 60 %, the flash copy fades out, and a warm glow pulses.
- **Hit**: flash copy blitted at `min(0.62, flash × 0.9)` alpha, sprite squash (+12 % x, −8 % y), one glint star, 45 % chance of one shard.
- **Glint star**: baked 16 × 16-unit sprite: radial white core r 3 + 4 curved spikes 7.5 units, added with `lighter`, rotates slightly; tints warm, cold, rose, mint.
- **Projectile**: seed sprite rotated to heading, a 16-unit tapered additive trail, small gold glow at alpha 0.35.
- **Dash**: 3 additive flash-copy ghosts behind the hero at 7-unit spacing, alpha `0.32/i`.
- **Level-up**: gold ring, 12 coloured vertical light beams (gold, rose, blue, mint) and 10 glints.
- **Hurt**: one rose glint and 5 orange/gold shards from the hero; player death = 18 shards.

## Lighting, shadows and post-processing

- **No directional light.** The light comes *through* the glass: highlights are always at the upper-left of each piece's own centre, and glowing elements are brighter pieces plus additive glow sprites.
- **Glow sprites**: radial gradients with alpha stops `0: .9, .25: .45, .6: .12, 1: 0`, colours warm `rgb(255,190,80)` r 16, gold `rgb(255,210,90)` r 10, aqua `rgb(110,240,220)` r 10, cold `rgb(150,200,255)` r 14, ruby `rgb(255,60,80)` r 14. Always drawn with `globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter'`.
- **Shadows**: flat ellipses, `rgba(14,10,22,0.42)` (ghost 0.25), small enemy 8 × 2.6, ghost 5 × 1.7, brute 19 × 5.5, hero 7.5 × 2.4.
- **Coloured light pools** from props baked into the ground chunk with `lighter` (see Background).
- **Screen overlay** (baked per screen size, s = H/900):
  - Vignette like a deep window embrasure: radial from 0.28 H to 0.56 × diagonal, `rgba(14,8,26, 0 / .1 @ .55 / .36 @ .85)` → `rgba(10,6,20,.62)`.
  - Window frame: lead stroke 10 s at inset 5 s (`rgba(16,12,22,.85)`), gold fillet 2 s at inset 11 s (`rgba(214,170,80,.35)`), dark corner rosettes r 110 s.
  - 70 faint wavy ripple lines (white 2.8 % / navy 3 %), screen-anchored like real pane distortion.
  - **Light layer** at 55 % × 50 % resolution: warm centre `rgba(255,226,170,.16)` plus five diagonal coloured rays (rose, gold, blue, amber, lilac) at alpha 0.075 → 0.028 → 0, slanted 0.45 H; added with `lighter`, stretched to 110 % width and drifting.

## UI and HUD

- **Panels** are glass in lead: 3–5 px lead border, `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #d9ad4e, 0 0 0 6px #17131c` (gold fillet then outer lead), jewel radial-gradient fill, gothic arch radii (`70px 70px 16px 16px / 56px 56px 16px 16px`).
- **Bars**: dark glass trough; fill = repeating lead mullions every 40–46 px over a 3-stop vertical gradient (HP `#ffc0b4 → #ec3c52 → #9a1630`, XP `#c8fff0 → #4fdcbc → #149a80`), outer colour glow and a white 50 % highlight strip.
- **Level-up cards**: tall pointed-arch cards (`112px 112px 14px 14px / 128px 128px 14px 14px`) with a diamond lead quarry pattern (two 45° repeating gradients, lead 2.5 px every 22.5 px) over blue/ruby/green jewel gradients, double gold+lead inner and outer rings, a round glowing icon medallion and a parchment description plate.
- **Icons** are drawn with the same Painter (outline 2.0, inner 1.15 at 48 px icon size).

```css
.hud-panel {
```

## Motion and animation

- **4 baked frames** per animated actor; `frame = floor(phase × 4) & 3`. Hero phase = distance × 0.42, small enemy × 0.85, brute × 0.32, ghost = time × 6 fps.
- **Hero**: walk lift `|sin(phase·2π)| × 2.2` units, rock `0.05 × facing × sin`, y-squash ±2 %; idle breathing y +2.5 % / x −1.5 % at 3 rad/s; shooting squash −4 % y; level-up wobble `sin(levelT·4π) × levelT × 12 %`.
- **Small enemy**: hop `|sin| × 1.2` units, rock ±0.09 rad. **Ghost**: +4 units float, bob ±1.5 at 2.4 rad/s, tilt by velocity up to 0.14 rad. **Brute**: lift 1.8 units, landing squash `(1 − up)^4 × 5 %`.
- **Hit flash** decays 1 → 0; i-frames blink at 14 Hz between alpha 1 and 0.55.
- **Flicker**: candle flames `0.75 + 0.25·sin(11t)·sin(7.3t)`, face glow `0.28 + 0.12·sin(9t)·sin(5.3t)`, gem halos `0.55 + 0.15·sin(6t)`.
- **Sway**: trees/bushes skew 0.02 / 0.03 at 1.1 rad/s; light rays drift at 0.12 rad/s.
- **Numbers**: scale 0.4 → 1.25 in 12 % of life, settle to 1 by 26 %, shrink 50 % and fade in the last 20–25 %.

## Do and don't

Do:
- Draw every actor in two passes: lead outline pass, then glass pieces with inner lead.
- Give every piece its own off-centre radial gradient and ±6 % brightness jitter.
- Split shapes where a glazier would: ribs, midribs, folds, facets.
- Make faces, eyes, flames and jewels glow pieces plus an additive glow sprite.
- Anchor the floor tessellation in world space; separate regions with heavier lead.
- Cast coloured additive light pools from props.
- Pre-bake every sprite and its lit flash copy.
- Keep the overlay: vignette, lead frame with gold fillet, slow coloured rays.

Don't:
- Don't use flat fills without lead seams — it becomes generic vector art.
- Don't flash enemies pure white; the flash copy keeps the lead.
- Don't make floor pieces as small as actor pieces (floor 15–30 units, actors 2–8).
- Don't use thin or coloured outlines; lead is always `#17131c`.
- Don't add directional drop shadows or realistic lighting.
- Don't use actor colours that match the floor region they live on.
- Don't compute the per-pixel ground every frame.

## Implementation recipe

1. Set up a world of 360 units visible height; `S = canvasHeight / 360`. Choose `K = clamp(round(S × 1.5), 3, 5)` for sprite baking.
2. Implement the helpers: `mulberry32`, `hashInt`, colour `mix/mul`, `perlin/fbm`, `splitPoly`, `bsp`, `mosaic`, `ribCells`, `leafPts/leafShape/leafCells`, path helpers `ELL`, `CAP`, `PP`.
3. Implement the **Painter** with modes `outline`, `fill`, `flash` and methods `part(shape, cells, opts)`, `piece(shape, col, cx, cy, r, opts)`, `glass(cell)` exactly as in the Code section.
4. For each actor write `parts(P, frame)` declaring pieces back-to-front, with frame-dependent offsets for 4 frames. Bake `{n, f}` pairs per frame with `build(box, fn, mode, seed)`.
5. Write the ground: field nodes on a 4-unit grid, bilinear signed distances, material priority, Voronoi per material with `smin` edges, luminance curve, antialiased lead ramp. Render in chunks (256 units) into ImageData, time-sliced, cached.
6. Add decals per material with a seeded scatter, then glints, then prop contact shadows and additive light pools.
7. Bake glow sprites, glint star, shard sprites, projectile, trail; draw them with `lighter`.
8. Per frame: blit ground chunks, y-sort actors and props, blit sprites with flip/scale/rotation, glow blits, particles, numbers.
9. Bake and draw the overlay (vignette + frame + ripples, then the half-res light layer additively).
10. Build the HUD with the CSS recipes: lead border, gold fillet ring, jewel gradients, mullioned bars, Cinzel fonts with lead text-shadow.

## Code

The snippets below are cleaned-up ports from the reference module. `starter.js` contains all of them wired together (hero, small enemy, ghost, brute, gems, seed, shards, ground, overlay). The full reference module is `../../js/styles/stainedglass.js`.

Glass piece shading and the two-pass Painter:

```js
const LEAD = '#17131c', WARM = [255, 250, 232];
const hex = (h) => [1, 3, 5].map((i) => parseInt(h.slice(i, i + 2), 16));
const mix = (a, b, t) => a.map((v, i) => v + (b[i] - v) * t);
const mul = (c, f) => c.map((v) => Math.min(255, v * f));
const rgb = (c) => `rgb(${c[0] | 0},${c[1] | 0},${c[2] | 0})`;
function mulberry32(a) { return () => { a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) | 0; let t = Math.imul(a ^ (a >>> 15), 1 | a); t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t; return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296; }; }

function Painter(ctx, mode, seed) { this.ctx = ctx; this.mode = mode; this.ol = 0.95; this.il = 0.55; this.rnd = mulberry32(seed); }
Painter.prototype.part = function (shape, cells, o = {}) {
  const c = this.ctx;
  if (this.mode === 'outline') { // pass 1: one fat outer came for the whole figure
    c.beginPath(); shape(c); c.lineWidth = (o.ol ?? this.ol) * 2;
    c.strokeStyle = c.fillStyle = LEAD; c.stroke(); c.fill(); return;
  }
  c.save(); c.beginPath(); shape(c); c.clip();
  for (const cell of cells) this.glass(cell, o);
  c.restore();
  c.beginPath(); shape(c); c.lineWidth = this.il * 1.2; c.strokeStyle = LEAD; c.stroke();
};
Painter.prototype.glass = function (cell, o) {
  const c = this.ctx, glow = cell.glow || o.glow;
  let col = mul(hex(cell.col), 1 + (this.rnd() - 0.5) * 0.12);
  if (this.mode === 'flash') col = mix(col, WARM, glow ? 0.4 : 0.58); // lit glass, lead stays
  const r = Math.max(0.6, cell.r);
  const g = c.createRadialGradient(cell.cx - r * 0.25, cell.cy - r * 0.3, r * 0.05, cell.cx, cell.cy, r * 1.3);
  g.addColorStop(0, rgb(glow ? mix(col, [255, 255, 236], 0.78) : mix(col, [255, 255, 255], 0.3)));
  g.addColorStop(0.48, rgb(col));
  g.addColorStop(1, rgb(mul(col, glow ? 0.9 : 0.64)));
  c.beginPath(); cell.path(c); c.fillStyle = g; c.fill();
  if (!glow && r > 1.6 && this.rnd() < 0.5) { // glint
    c.fillStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,0.55)';
    c.beginPath(); c.ellipse(cell.cx - r * 0.38, cell.cy - r * 0.42, r * 0.26, r * 0.1, -0.7, 0, Math.PI * 2); c.fill();
    c.beginPath(); cell.path(c);
  }
  c.lineWidth = this.il; c.strokeStyle = LEAD; c.stroke();
};
/** Bake a figure: fn(P) declares parts; box = [x0,y0,x1,y1] in world units; K = px per unit. */
function build(box, fn, mode, seed, K) {
  const cv = document.createElement('canvas');
  cv.width = Math.ceil((box[2] - box[0]) * K); cv.height = Math.ceil((box[3] - box[1]) * K);
  const x = cv.getContext('2d'); x.lineJoin = x.lineCap = 'round'; x.scale(K, K); x.translate(-box[0], -box[1]);
  fn(new Painter(x, 'outline', seed)); fn(new Painter(x, mode, seed));
  return cv;
}
```

BSP mosaic — cut any convex polygon into glass pieces:

```js
function splitPoly(poly, px, py, nx, ny) {
  const a = [], b = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < poly.length; i++) {
    const p = poly[i], q = poly[(i + 1) % poly.length];
    const dp = (p[0] - px) * nx + (p[1] - py) * ny, dq = (q[0] - px) * nx + (q[1] - py) * ny;
    (dp >= 0 ? a : b).push(p);
    if ((dp >= 0) !== (dq >= 0)) { const t = dp / (dp - dq), m = [p[0] + (q[0] - p[0]) * t, p[1] + (q[1] - p[1]) * t]; a.push(m); b.push(m); }
  }
  return [a, b];
}
const area = (p) => Math.abs(p.reduce((s, a, i) => { const b = p[(i + 1) % p.length]; return s + a[0] * b[1] - b[0] * a[1]; }, 0)) / 2;
function bsp(poly, maxArea, rnd, out = [], depth = 0) {
  if (area(poly) <= maxArea || depth > 9) { out.push(poly); return out; }
  const xs = poly.map((q) => q[0]), ys = poly.map((q) => q[1]);
  const cx = xs.reduce((s, v) => s + v) / xs.length, cy = ys.reduce((s, v) => s + v) / ys.length;
  const w = Math.max(...xs) - Math.min(...xs), h = Math.max(...ys) - Math.min(...ys), ext = Math.max(w, h);
  const ang = (w > h ? 0 : Math.PI / 2) + (rnd() - 0.5) * 1.2, nx = Math.cos(ang), ny = Math.sin(ang);
  const [a, b] = splitPoly(poly, cx + nx * (rnd() - 0.5) * 0.35 * ext, cy + ny * (rnd() - 0.5) * 0.35 * ext, nx, ny);
  if (a.length < 3 || b.length < 3) { out.push(poly); return out; }
  bsp(a, maxArea, rnd, out, depth + 1); bsp(b, maxArea, rnd, out, depth + 1);
  return out;
}
// usage: cells = bsp(cloakPolygon, 38, mulberry32(7)).map((p) => ({ path: (c) => polyPath(c, p), col: pick(), cx, cy, r }))
```

Floor pixel: Voronoi edge distance + antialiased lead with metallic ridge:

```js
const smin = (a, b, k) => { const h = Math.max(k - Math.abs(a - b), 0) / k; return Math.min(a, b) - h * h * k * 0.25; };
/** sites: 3 nearest {sx, sy, col, C} sorted by squared distance d1<d2<d3; re = distance to region border. */
function glassPixel(x, y, s1, s2, s3, d1, d2, d3, re, res) {
  const e1 = (d2 - d1) / (2 * Math.hypot(s2.sx - s1.sx, s2.sy - s1.sy));
  const e2 = (d3 - d1) / (2 * Math.hypot(s3.sx - s1.sx, s3.sy - s1.sy));
  const eP = smin(e1, e2, 1.6), e = Math.min(eP, re);
  let t = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, e / (s1.C * 0.34)));
  const lum = 0.6 + 0.38 * t * t * (3 - 2 * t);           // dark rim -> bright core
  let [r, g, b] = s1.col.map((v) => v * lum);
  const cov = Math.max(0.78 - eP, 1.2 - re) * res + 0.5;   // piece lead 0.78, region lead 1.2 (half widths)
  if (cov > 0) {
    const k = Math.min(1, cov), tl = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, Math.max(1 - eP / 0.78, 1 - re / 1.2))), q = tl * tl * 0.85;
    r += (28 + 56 * q - r) * k; g += (24 + 54 * q - g) * k; b += (34 + 62 * q - b) * k; // ridge rgb(84,78,96)
  }
  return [r, g, b];
}
```

Pumpkin/fruit rib lenses (roundness without shading):

```js
function ribCells(cx, cy, rx, ry, fs, cols) { // fs e.g. [-1.05,-0.64,-0.22,0.22,0.64,1.05]
  const out = [], PI = Math.PI;
  for (let i = 0; i < fs.length - 1; i++) {
    const a = fs[i], b = fs[i + 1]; let path;
    if (a < 0 && b > 0) { const o = Math.max(-a, b); path = (c) => { c.moveTo(cx + rx * o, cy); c.ellipse(cx, cy, rx * o, ry, 0, 0, 2 * PI); }; }
    else if (b <= 0) { const o = -a, n = Math.max(0.01, -b); path = (c) => { c.moveTo(cx, cy - ry); c.ellipse(cx, cy, rx * o, ry, 0, -PI / 2, PI / 2, true); c.ellipse(cx, cy, rx * n, ry, 0, PI / 2, -PI / 2, false); c.closePath(); }; }
    else { const n = Math.max(0.01, a), o = b; path = (c) => { c.moveTo(cx, cy - ry); c.ellipse(cx, cy, rx * o, ry, 0, -PI / 2, PI / 2, false); c.ellipse(cx, cy, rx * n, ry, 0, PI / 2, -PI / 2, true); c.closePath(); }; }
    out.push({ path, col: cols[i % cols.length], cx: cx + rx * (Math.max(-1, a) + Math.min(1, b)) / 2, cy: cy - ry * 0.1, r: Math.max(rx * (b - a) * 0.75, ry * 0.95) });
  }
  return out;
}
```

## Adapting it to your game

Keep fixed (this *is* the style):
- Lead `#17131c`, outer came 1.9 units, inner 0.55, floor lead 0.78 / 1.2 half-widths with the metallic ridge.
- The per-piece radial gradient (30 % white core, ×0.64 rim) and brightness jitter.
- Two-pass Painter, flash copies that keep the lead, shatter-into-shards deaths.
- Glow pieces + additive glow sprites for every light source; coloured light pools; the window overlay.

May change:
- **Palette swap**: replace region families with other jewel families (e.g. sapphire sea + emerald islands + gold sand) — keep mid values (HSL lightness ~30–55 %) and 5–7 swatches per family; keep actors brighter/paler than their region.
- **New characters**: start from a silhouette, then cut along natural seams. Knights: helmet ribs + visor glow; animals: leaf-cells for ears and wings; robots work only if made of jewel colours.
- **Other genres**: side-scrollers can use a vertical window (pointed-arch frame around the viewport) and a parallax backdrop of large-piece mosaics; puzzle games can turn each tile into a leaded piece.
- **Resolution**: bake sprites at higher K for big screens; the floor can drop to 1–1.5 px per unit on mobile — the lead antialiasing keeps it clean.
- **Cell sizes** scale with your world: floor cells ≈ 0.6–1.2 × hero width.

## Performance notes

- Sprites: ~70 canvases baked at init (hero 4×2, small enemy 3 variants × 4 × 2, ghost 4×2, brute 4×2, 15 prop variants, 36 shards, glows). Baking takes tens of ms; never repaint glass per frame.
- Ground: the expensive part — per pixel a bilinear field lookup, a 3×3 Voronoi search and the lead ramp. Render it once per 256-unit chunk as a time-sliced generator (yield every 2 rows) at ≤ 2.5 px per unit, cache chunks, precompute site arrays per chunk and field nodes in a shared map (cleared above 60 000 entries). Classify 4-unit cells far from any border as a single material to skip the per-pixel region test.
- Per frame: 1–3 `drawImage` per actor + a few additive glows, so 300+ enemies stay cheap. Avoid `ctx.filter` and `shadowBlur`.
- Overlay: baked per screen size; the light layer is half resolution and only stretched.
- Damage numbers are cached as sprites by value + crit (cache cleared at 400 entries).

## Copy-paste prompt

```text
Build my game <X> in the "Cathedral Glass" stained-glass style (Canvas 2D, procedural, no image assets):
- Everything is backlit stained glass: jewel-tone pieces separated by near-black lead #17131c.
- Each glass piece: off-centre radial gradient (30% white core at upper-left, base colour at 48%, colour x0.64 rim), ±6% brightness jitter, two faint white streaks, a small elliptical glint on half the pieces.
- Draw every actor in two passes: (1) fill+stroke every part in lead with lineWidth 1.9 world units = one fat outer outline; (2) clip into each part, paint its glass cells, stroke inner lead 0.55.
- Cut shapes like a glazier: BSP mosaics for bodies/clothes, vertical rib lenses for round fruit/heads, leaves split on the midrib, faceted gems.
- Faces, eyes, flames, jewels are glow pieces (78% warm-white core) plus additive radial glow sprites ('lighter').
- Pre-bake each actor in 4 walk frames plus a "flash" copy (pieces mixed 58% to warm white, lead kept) for hits.
- Floor: per-pixel world-anchored Voronoi glass (cells 15-30 units), material regions from noise signed distances (meadow greens, crimson leaf carpet, amber 3-lane path, night blue, grey diamond quarries), lead 0.78 / 1.2 units with a metallic ridge rgb(84,78,96).
- Leaded decals (flowers, leaves, stars), white glint strokes, coloured additive light pools under props.
- Deaths shatter into tumbling leaded shards; hits add a four-point glint star.
- Overlay: dark-violet vignette, lead window frame with gold #d9ad4e fillet, slowly drifting coloured diagonal light rays.
- HUD: lead-bordered glass panels with gold fillet rings, gothic arch tops, mullioned bars; fonts Cinzel Decorative 900 + Cinzel with lead text-shadow outlines.
- Actors brighter/paler than the floor region; gold only for light sources. 360 world units visible vertically.
```


---

<!-- style: clay · https://miwale.com/styles/library/clay/STYLE.md -->

# Clay World — Game Art Style Spec

> Stop-motion plasticine miniature set: soft gradient-built clay figures with fingerprints, warm studio light and 12 fps boil.

Everything looks hand-rolled from modelling clay and filmed on a tabletop miniature set (think Aardman / Clay Jam). Characters are stacks of soft lumpy balls and sausages with **no outlines**: each part is lit by a warm top-left key light, darkened by inner ambient occlusion along its bottom edge, caught by a warm rim light along its top edge, covered in faint thumbprints and topped with a broad, soft specular. The ground is a set of flat clay sheets — meadow, soil, purple clay, ochre paths and sunken glossy ponds — with raised bevelled edges and a lumpy hand-pressed surface. All animation steps at 12 fps and every frame is a slightly different "boil" of the same model. The reference implementation is the top-down survivor game *Jack vs. the Turnip Ancestors* (hero = pumpkin-head Jack, enemies = turnip creepers, ghosts, a root colossus); everything below is written so you can apply it to any game.

## At a glance

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Family | Claymation · Stop-motion plasticine |
| Mood | cozy, handmade, playful, tactile, warm |
| Best for | top-down action/survivor, cozy adventure, puzzle/party, casual mobile |
| Renderer | Canvas 2D, fully procedural, no image assets |
| Pixel art | No — native resolution, sprites baked at 3–5 px per world unit |
| Difficulty | 5/10 — soft shapes are forgiving, but each figure needs a few passes to read as plasticine |
| Fonts | Chewy (titles, numbers), Baloo 2 500–800 (body) |
| Key colours | meadow `#76a454`, purple clay `#66507e`, ochre path `#d6a262`, pond `#7ebad2`, pumpkin `#ee7a22`, candle `#ffd458`, plum shadow `#401a34`, panel cream `#f5ddb8` |

## When to use it

- **Good fits:** top-down survivor/arena games, cozy adventures, farming and village sims, party and puzzle games, kids' games, casual mobile. The soft volumes read well at 15–60 world units per character and stay friendly even with "monsters".
- **Good fits:** games with chunky, toy-like characters and a limited cast (3–10 enemy types). Each type can be a distinct colour pair.
- **Bad fits:** grim, horror or realistic games — the warm studio light and rounded forms are inherently cute.
- **Bad fits:** pixel-precise retro games, games with tiny units (< 8 units tall: the shading turns to mush) or with hundreds of unit types (each needs hand-tuning).
- **Bad fits:** fast smooth-motion games where 12 fps stepping would feel laggy (e.g. competitive shooters).

## Color palette

| Swatch name | Hex | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Meadow clay | `#76a454` | Default ground (~40% of screen); canvas clear colour `#78a854` |
| Meadow light | `#8cac5a` | Second meadow tone blended in large noise patches |
| Purple clay | `#66507e` | Raised dark sheets, graveyard zones |
| Soil | `#986c4a` | Raised brown fields |
| Ochre path | `#d6a262` | Raised winding paths and clearings |
| Pond | `#7ebad2` | Sunken glossy water sheets |
| Pumpkin orange | `#ee7a22` | Hero head, main accent; HUD numbers `#f07a24` |
| Overall blue | `#3c62a6` | Hero body; pants `#344c80` |
| Scarf green | `#68ae48` | Hero scarf; leaves `#60a246`; foliage `#609e4a` |
| Skin cream | `#f8e0ba` | Hands; shoes `#6c422a` |
| Turnip purple | `#8650ac` | Small enemy top (variants `#b24c8e`, `#685cbe`) |
| Turnip cream | `#f4e8cc` | Small enemy body (variants `#f6e2ce`, `#eee8c6`) |
| Brow plum | `#4a2852` | Eyebrows, dark accents |
| Ghost white | `#eaf0fc` | Floating enemy; shaded to `#96a4ce` |
| Brute mauve | `#7e5a68` | Large brute; lumps `#6c4a5c`, `#946c76`; roots `#a07660` |
| Candle ramp | `#fff7c4` → `#ffd458` → `#ff8f22` | All glow: carved faces, cracks, cores, lanterns |
| Cavity | `#4e1606` | Inside of carved holes; cracks `#2c1218` + `#ff9a3a` |
| Plum shadow | `#401a34` | Shadow tint target; AO `rgba(58,20,40)`, contact `rgba(52,22,24)`, ground shadow `rgba(44,24,16)` |
| Warm white | `#fffbf0` | Highlight target; rim light `rgba(255,247,230)` |
| Panel cream | `#f5ddb8` | UI slabs (`#fff5e2` → `#f5ddb8` → `#e0b98a`), base `#b98654` |
| Seed gold | `#ffca40` | Small pickups; big pickups `#ff7c34` |

**Palette rules**

- Colours come in as RGB triples and are shaded with two helpers, never with grey:
  - `lighten(c, t) = mix(c, [255,251,240], t)` (warm white)
  - `darken(c, t) = mix(c * (1 - t), [64,26,52], t * 0.3)` (multiplied, then pulled 30%·t toward plum)
- Saturated-but-chalky toy colours. No neon, no pure `#000`, no pure `#fff` except tiny glossy dots and pupil catch-lights.
- Ground sheets stay mid-value so the glossier, brighter characters pop.
- Each enemy family is a two-tone pair (dark top layer smeared over a light body) — hordes read as colour clusters.
- Glow is reserved for the candle ramp, composited with `'lighter'`.
- Approx. ratio: 60% ground greens/purples, 25% character colours, 15% warm accents and cream UI.

## Typography

**Chewy** (400) — titles, HUD numbers, card names, damage numbers. <https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Chewy>
```css
font: 400 40px/1.1 'Chewy', 'Baloo 2', system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 2px; color: #f07a24;
text-shadow: 0 2px 0 #c85e1a, 0 4px 0 #a84a12, 0 5px 0 #8c3c0e, 0 9px 10px rgba(40,18,6,.45);
```

**Baloo 2** (500, 600, 700, 800) — labels, descriptions, hints. <https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Baloo+2>
```css
font: 800 12px/1.2 'Baloo 2', system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 2px; color: #9a6a44;
```

Text effects:
- **Extruded clay letters:** stack 3–5 hard `text-shadow`s 1–3 px apart in progressively darker versions of the text colour, then one soft drop shadow. Big titles (84 px) use `0 3px 0 #e08a26, 0 6px 0 #c06a1c, 0 9px 0 #9c5214, 0 11px 0 #7e4210, 0 20px 22px rgba(20,8,2,.55)` and are rotated `-2deg`.
- **Cream text on coloured clay:** `#fff6e6` with `0 1px 0 <dark>, 0 2px 0 <darker>, 0 3px 4px rgba(40,18,6,.6)`.
- **In-world damage numbers** are baked sprites: Chewy 9.5 units (13 for crits), a blurred dark copy 0.13 em lower, 3 stacked "side" copies (crit `#b24a16` → `#ffa82e`), a vertical gradient face (lighten 0.45 → base → darken 0.12) and a radial white highlight clipped to the upper half with `source-atop`.

## Rendering technique

1. **Init:** choose sprite resolution `K = clamp(round(screenPxPerUnit * 1.2), 3, 5)` px per world unit (the game shows 360 world units vertically).
2. **Build the fingerprint tile** (192×192 px, tileable via 9 offset draws): 7 thumbprints of 5–8 concentric partial ellipses (radius 9–18 px, aspect 1.25, sweep π–1.9π) plus 12 curved tool smears. Every stroke is drawn twice: dark `rgba(70,28,20,0.1)` (0.9 px), then light `rgba(255,246,232,0.09)` 0.9 px lower.
3. **Build the ground height texture** (256×256, 2 texels per unit, tileable fBm) and convert it to a lighting modulator `MOD = (h[x-1,y-1] - h[x+1,y+1]) * 2.4 + (h - 0.5) * 0.08 + hashNoise * 0.008` — a diagonal derivative = light from the top-left.
4. **Bake every sprite** into its own canvas at K px/unit: the hero (1 idle + 4 walk frames, normal + hurt face), each enemy type × 4 frames (× 3 colour variants), props (2–4 variants each), pickups, projectile, 14 crumb balls, 14 splats, the spawn mound. Each frame gets its own RNG seed (`100 + frame`, `200 + variant*10 + frame`, ...) so lumps and fingerprint offsets differ — this is the boil. A cream-tinted copy (`#fff8ec`, source-atop) and mirrored copies are stored next to each frame.
5. **Ground chunks** (256 units, ≤ 2.5 px/unit) are rendered lazily by a generator that yields every few rows: sample material fields on a 4-unit grid, per pixel compute signed distance + lit bevel/shadow, multiply by `MOD`, `putImageData`, then stamp decals with canvas paths.
6. **Per frame draw order:** ground chunks → ground overlay (additive hero light pool, pickup glows, splats, spawn mounds) → pickups → soft shadows of all actors/props → y-sorted props, enemies, hero (blits) → orbiting items → projectiles → particles → damage numbers → screen overlay (vignette + top light).
7. Sprites are drawn with `drawImage` at `1/K` scale, optionally under a rotation transform. Smoothing stays ON (this is not pixel art).

## Background and ground

The floor is a **tabletop of flat clay sheets** laid on top of each other.

- **Fields:** 4 domain-warped fBm fields (warp ±110 units at 1/900 frequency) decide soil (scale 760), purple (600), pond (420) and ochre (clearings at 650 + thin winding paths from `|perlin| < 0.019` at 1/1500). A field > 0 means "inside the sheet". Later layers sit on top: meadow < soil < purple < pond < path.
- **Signed distance:** fields are sampled on a 4-unit grid and bilinearly interpolated; `dist = value / |gradient|` gives a pixel distance to the sheet edge, `ld = -(grad · L) / |grad|` with `L = (-0.42, -0.907)` gives how much the edge faces the light.
- **Raised sheet (soil, purple, path):** outside within `SW = 3.4` units → cast shadow `k = 0.4 * sh² * (0.35 + 0.65 * max(0, -ld))`; inside within `BW = 3.0` units → bevel `f = 1 + ld * 0.42 * p² + 0.09 * exp(-((p - 0.55)/0.22)²) - 0.03 * p³` (p = 1 at the edge → 0 inside). The Gaussian term is a thin bright crest just inside the edge — the "rolled lip" of a clay sheet. 1-pixel anti-aliased coverage `cov = clamp(dist + 0.5)`.
- **Sunken sheet (pond):** a darker wet bank outside (`1 - 0.1q²` over 0.7·BW), an inverted bevel inside (`1 - max(ld,0)*0.34p² + max(-ld,0)*0.16p² - 0.05p²` over 1.3·BW), and a much smoother surface (`m = 0.35`).
- **Surface lumps:** `colour * (1 + MOD * m) * tint` with m = 1 (meadow), 1.1 (soil), 1 (purple), 0.35 (pond), 0.9 (path); `tint = 1 ± 4.5%` from very low-frequency noise. Meadow blends `#76a454` ↔ `#8cac5a` by smoothstep(0.3, 0.7, noise/420).
- **Decals** (jittered 10-unit grid, ~30% of points used, never within 6 units of a material border):
  - Meadow: "modelling-tool" grass imprints (fans of 3–5 curved strokes, 0.65 units, alpha 0.16), rolled green grass sprouts (sausage strokes 1.0 wide), 5-petal flowers (`#faf6ec`, `#f6a0b6`, `#fcd65a`, `#b096e2`, petals 0.82 units with darker under-copy 0.2 lower, yellow bump centre), grey pebbles.
  - Soil: pebbles (`#b28460`, `#7e583e`, `#a0968c`, `#c4a078`), pink worms (`#e28c96`, wavy sausage 1.5 wide), twigs.
  - Purple: spiral imprints, purple pebbles, tiny lilac mushrooms.
  - Pond: lily pads (`#58964a` / `#70ae56`, 4 × 2.6 units, notch line in pond colour), ripple rings, and **studio-light reflections**: a radial white blob squashed to 0.32 height, rotated -0.18, 9–16 units wide, plus a 0.55-alpha core ellipse.
  - Path: thumbprints (5 concentric partial ellipses, 0.85 units apart) and footprints.
- An **imprint** is a dark stroke `rgba(52,26,12,a)` plus a lighter stroke `rgba(255,246,222,0.95a)` at 0.6 width shifted 0.6w down; a **bump** (pebble) is a shadow ellipse offset (+0.22rx, +0.5ry), a radial gradient body and a small highlight ellipse at the upper left.

## Characters

The hero (reference: pumpkin-head boy, ~21 units wide, ~33 tall incl. stem, drawn at scale 1.06) is an assembly of ~20 clay parts painted back to front:

1. Scarf tail (two capsules r 1.5, swinging angle per frame 0.22–0.58 rad).
2. Back arm: capsule r 1.25 in body blue + cream hand ellipse 1.5 × 1.45.
3. Legs: capsules r 1.4 in `#344c80` + shoe ellipses 2.3 × 1.4 in `#6c422a`.
4. Body: lumpy blob 4.7 × 4.4 (`#3c62a6`, amt 0.08) with two pressed fold grooves; a yellow button 0.75.
5. Front arm, then the scarf ring (lump 6 × 2.3 with 4 vertical grooves).
6. Stem capsule (r 1.35, `#787434`) and a leaf (`#68a646`) with a curly tendril stroke.
7. **Head:** pumpkin superellipse 10.2 × 8.4 (exponents 0.85/0.92, dents at top and bottom), `spec 0.55`, `gloss 0.7`, `lit 0.24`, `ao 0.55`, highlight at (-5.0, -4.6) radius 4.4; 4 curved rib grooves (width 0.75, alpha 0.3); carved face (two triangle eyes, a zig-zag grin) with candle light.

Proportions: head ≈ 55–60% of height, body tiny, limbs stubby (r 1.25–1.4). Feet at y = 0, origin bottom-centre.

**Animation frames** (back foot x/y, front foot x/y, back arm, front arm, body lift):
`idle [-2.1,0, 2.3,0, 0.18,-0.18, 0]`, walk `[-3.5,0, 3.7,-0.2, 0.8,-0.75, 0]`, `[-0.8,-1.7, 1.0,0, 0.25,-0.2, 0.9]`, `[3.5,-0.2, -3.3,0, -0.7,0.8, 0]`, `[1.0,0, -0.8,-1.7, -0.2,0.25, 0.9]`.
A hurt variant swaps the carved face for squeezed slits and an "O" mouth. Facing = mirrored sprite.

**The clay() painter** — the material illusion, in order:

| Step | What | Numbers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contact shadow | the shape filled with `source-atop` + shadow, so it only darkens parts already painted behind it | `rgba(52,22,24,0.42)`, blur `min(0.4R, 2.4)` units, offset `(min(0.06R,0.45), min(0.2R,1.4))` |
| Base | flat fill in the base colour, then clip to the shape | — |
| Key light | radial gradient from `(cx-0.25rx, cy-0.5ry)` r `0.04R` to `(cx+0.05rx, cy+0.05ry)` r `1.22R` | stops `0: lighten(col, 0.2)`, `0.5: col`, `1: darken(col, 0.4)` |
| Fingerprints | the 192 px tile as pattern, random offset per part (seeded) | alpha 1 (0.5–0.6 on eyes/pickups, 0 on tiny glossy parts) |
| Inner AO | fill "big rect minus shape" (even-odd) 3000 units away; only its shadow falls back inside the clip | `rgba(58,20,40,0.5)`, blur `0.6R`, offset `(-0.1R, -0.3R)` → darkens the bottom inner edge |
| Rim light | same trick with a warm shadow | `rgba(255,247,230,0.42)`, blur `0.26R`, offset `(+0.04R, +0.12R)` → glows along the top inner edge |
| Detail | grooves, faces, carved holes, painted inside the clip | — |
| Soft specular | radial blob at `(cx-0.3rx, cy-0.52ry)` r `0.45R`, rotated -0.45 rad, scaled 1.4 × 0.8 | stops `0: rgba(255,255,252,spec)`, `0.45: spec*0.38`, `1: 0`; default spec 0.3 |
| Gloss dot (optional) | small ellipse inside the spec | `0.32 × 0.17` of spec radius, alpha `gloss` (0.4–0.85) |

Parameters per part: `lit` (key light strength), `dark` (override shadow colour), `ao`, `rim`, `spec`, `gloss`, `fp`, `cast`, `hi` (highlight position/radius).

## Enemies and props

All secondary actors use the same painter and the same back-to-front assembly.

- **Small melee enemy** (turnip creeper, ~21 × 22 units, scale 0.92): three leaf blades (leafPath, length 8–10, width 2.5–2.9, centre groove), two root legs (capsules r 1.5, `#e4caa0`), a turnip body (cream base, `spec 0.35`, `lit 0.12`) with a **second clay layer smeared on top** — a wavy-bottomed purple shape painted inside the body's clip with its own AO and contact shadow. Two googly eyes (white clay balls 2.5 × 2.8 with black pupils `#1e1420` and a white catch-light), angry brow capsules (`#4a2852`, r 0.75, `cast 0.5`), a pressed frown groove (width 0.7, alpha 0.55). Three colour variants: `#8650ac`, `#b24c8e`, `#685cbe` tops.
- **Fast floating enemy** (ghost, ~20 × 24): one custom silhouette with a 3-scallop animated hem and a wispy tail, colour `#eaf0fc` shaded with `dark: #96a4ce` (cool shadow for a cool material), `spec 0.55`, `gloss 0.5`, `lit 0.3`, `rim 0.3`. Sad dark sockets `#3a3c62`, tiny white catch-lights, an "O" mouth whose height pulses. Two stubby arm ellipses. Drawn at alpha 0.84, floating 5 units up.
- **Large brute** (root colossus, ~37 × 64): a 14-point lumpy body (amt 0.12, narrowing toward the top), extra lumps on shoulders and hips, capsule arms r 4.4 with three root-finger capsules, glowing **cracks** (3 strokes: `#2c1218` 1.5 → `#ff9a3a` 0.65 → `#ffe9a6` 0.25), a carved glowing core (cavity `#3a1410`, candle gradient offset +0.9 down), eyes as dark sockets with yellow `#ffc94a` irises, a jagged mouth, and an additive pulsing glow on the core. Four leaves on top.
- **Pickups:** a seed/drop shape 1.7 × 2.0 (`#ffca40`, big `#ff7c34` ×1.45) with `spec 0.7`, `gloss 0.85`, bobbing 3 ± 1 units with a tiny shadow and additive glow (r 5.5 / 9).
- **Props:** trees (capsule trunk r 3.4 `#865e40` with 3 grooves, 5 lumpy foliage balls r 8–11, alternating ±5% lightness, red berries or white blossoms), bushes (4 lumps + berries), mushrooms (dome + cream spots), fences (capsule posts and rails with grooves), pumpkins (with ribs), gravestones (grey slab `#9a96a4` with a pressed cross and a chipped corner groove), hay domes (90 straw strokes), rocks (1–2 grey lumps). Each prop has a fixed soft shadow ellipse (e.g. tree 17 × 5.5, bush 14 × 4.5).
- Readability: enemies are lighter/glossier than the ground and always carry eyes; small enemies sit at ~0.6× the hero's height, brutes ~2×.

## Effects and particles

- **Clay crumbs:** hits (55% chance, 1 crumb) and kills (5 / 3 / 12 crumbs) spawn baked clay balls (2 × 1.85 units, `spec 0.45`, `fp 0.6`) in the enemy's colours; velocity 40–85, upward 50–110, gravity 300, drag 1.6; on ground contact they squash to 1.25 × 0.72; shrink out in the last 18% of life.
- **Splats:** a flat lumpy pancake (4.6 × 2.4, amt 0.25, `rim 0.3`) plus 3 droplets, scaled 1.05 (2.1 for brutes), random ±0.3 rad, live 1.7–2.2 s; pop-in with outBack over 8%, fade and flatten to 50% height in the last 30%.
- **Death:** squash `sx × (1 + 0.7k)`, `sy × (1 - 0.8k)`, `k = outQuad(min(1, q/0.55))`, fade after 50%, cream flash copy at `0.5 × (1 - q)`.
- **Hit flash:** sprite squashes `1 + 0.16·flash` / `1 - 0.15·flash` and a cream copy is overlaid at `min(0.55, flash × 0.8)`; plus an additive white puff (`rgba(255,255,248,0.95)` → 0, size 6–9, 0.12 s).
- **Projectiles:** baked cream seed with a tapered soft streak (`rgba(255,244,214,0.75)` → 0, 11.5 units long, 3 units thick), fading in over 1/14 s, with a tiny ground shadow 6 units below; the seed "flips" with `sy = 0.6 + 0.4|cos(step)|`.
- **Pickup:** small additive flash on the hero; level-up: a 26-unit flash, 18 multi-coloured crumbs and 8 dust puffs in a ring.
- **Dash:** 3 ghost copies at alpha `0.32/i` 6 units apart along the dash, sprite stretched 1.18 × 0.9, plus beige dust puffs.
- **Spawn:** enemies rise out of a dark clay mound (lump 10.5 × 4.2 with a dark hole gradient `#2c160c → #6e4630`) revealed in 8 discrete rows-steps.

## Lighting, shadows and post-processing

- **Key light:** top-left everywhere — sprite gradients, highlights, ground bevels (`L = (-0.42, -0.907)`), pebbles, UI radial gradients at `30% 18%`.
- **Actor shadows:** a radial sprite `rgba(44,24,16,0.5)` → `0.34 @ 0.45` → 0, stretched to an ellipse (hero 10.2 × 3.6, small enemy 8.8 × 3.0, brute 21 × 6.6, floater 6.2 × 2.3 at alpha 0.6), shifted +8% of rx to the right.
- **Warm practical lights:** additive (`'lighter'`) glow sprite `rgba(255,214,120,0.85) → rgba(255,170,70,0.35) @ 0.35 → 0` for the hero's light pool on the ground (34 × 18, alpha 0.16), his carved face (11 × 10, alpha 0.3 ± 0.08), lanterns (12, alpha 0.45 ± 0.1), brute cores (11, alpha 0.32 ± 0.1) and pickups.
- **Screen overlay** (one 320 × 180 sprite stretched to the screen): elliptical vignette (scaled 1 × 0.62) `rgba(70,34,16,0)` at r 70 → `0.12` at 60% → `rgba(56,26,12,0.46)` at r 215; a warm top light band `rgba(255,232,206,0.24)` → 0 over the top 19%; a faint bottom band `rgba(255,226,196,0.2)`; a whole-screen warm wash `rgba(255,186,110,0.04)`.
- **Menus:** level-up backdrop `radial-gradient(rgba(255,206,140,.28), rgba(46,22,10,.7) 78%)` with `backdrop-filter: blur(3px) saturate(.75)`; game over adds `grayscale(.7) brightness(.7)`.

## UI and HUD

The HUD is made of the same clay: **slabs with thickness**. Panels use a cream radial gradient, an inner white top highlight, an inner brown bottom shadow, a solid 5–8 px darker base (`0 5px 0 #b98654`) for thickness and a soft drop shadow. Border radii are deliberately uneven (`26px 30px 24px 28px / 28px 24px 30px 26px`) so nothing is machine-perfect. Bars are pressed grooves (dark brown inset) with glossy pill fills and a blurred white highlight strip. A faint thumbprint sits in a corner of each panel. Upgrade cards come in cream, green (`#cde6ae`) and lilac (`#dcc6ee`) clay; their icons are drawn with the same clay() painter at 48-unit icon space.

```css
.clay-panel { position: relative; padding: 3px 30px 9px; border-radius: 26px 30px 24px 28px / 28px 24px 30px 26px;
  background: radial-gradient(120% 140% at 30% 18%, #fff5e2 0%, #f5ddb8 45%, #e0b98a 100%);
  box-shadow: inset 0 3px 3px rgba(255,255,255,.8), inset 0 -6px 10px rgba(150,88,40,.38),
    inset 4px 0 8px rgba(255,255,255,.25), 0 5px 0 #b98654, 0 13px 18px rgba(50,24,10,.38); }
.clay-panel::after { content: ''; position: absolute; right: 9px; bottom: 7px; width: 22px; height: 27px;
  border-radius: 50%; transform: rotate(-24deg); pointer-events: none;
  background: repeating-radial-gradient(ellipse at 50% 58%, rgba(120,66,26,.2) 0 1px, rgba(255,255,255,.22) 1px 2px, rgba(0,0,0,0) 2px 3.3px);
  -webkit-mask: radial-gradient(closest-side, #000 60%, transparent); mask: radial-gradient(closest-side, #000 60%, transparent); }
.clay-number { font-family: 'Chewy', 'Baloo 2', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 40px; letter-spacing: 2px; color: #f07a24;
  text-shadow: 0 2px 0 #c85e1a, 0 4px 0 #a84a12, 0 5px 0 #8c3c0e, 0 9px 10px rgba(40,18,6,.45); }
.clay-bar { position: relative; width: 250px; height: 30px; border-radius: 999px; overflow: hidden;

.clay-bar > .fill { height: 100%; border-radius: 999px;
  background: linear-gradient(180deg, #ffab8f 0%, #f2613f 36%, #d23e26 72%, #a92c18 100%);   /* XP: #fff0a8 #ffd055 #f0a52c #c97c18 */
  box-shadow: inset 0 -4px 5px rgba(90,18,4,.45), inset 0 2px 2px rgba(255,220,200,.6); }

  border-radius: 4px; background: rgba(255,255,255,.55); filter: blur(1px); }
.clay-button { border-radius: 999px; padding: 6px 26px 8px; color: #fff6e6; font-family: 'Chewy', sans-serif; font-size: 24px;
  background: radial-gradient(circle at 36% 30%, #ffc988, #f08a3a 60%, #c9621e); text-shadow: 0 2px 0 #9c4a16;
  box-shadow: inset 0 3px 3px rgba(255,255,255,.55), inset 0 -4px 6px rgba(120,40,0,.4), 0 5px 0 #9c4a16, 0 12px 16px rgba(20,8,2,.45); }
@keyframes clayWobble { 0%,100% { transform: none } 33% { transform: translate(-3px,1px) scale(1.04,.95) } 66% { transform: translate(3px,-1px) scale(.97,1.03) } }
@keyframes clayPop { 0% { transform: scale(.3,.1) rotate(-6deg); } 50% { transform: scale(1.15,.85) rotate(-1deg); }
  75% { transform: scale(.95,1.06) rotate(-3deg); } 100% { transform: scale(1) rotate(-2deg); } }
/* use with steps(): animation: clayPop .5s steps(6) backwards;  hurt: clayWobble .26s steps(3) */
```

## Motion and animation

- **12 fps everything:** `step = Math.floor(t * 12)`; positions of bobs/pulses use `Math.floor(t * 12) / 12`.
- **Boil:** per step, `bj = hash(step, seed) - 0.5` → `sx *= 1 + bj*0.02`, `sy *= 1 - bj*0.018`, `rot += bj2*0.025` (hero) / `0.035`, `0.03`, `0.04` (enemies). Combined with per-frame seeded bakes this makes the clay "breathe" like re-sculpted stop-motion.
- **Hero:** walk frame `1 + (floor(anim * 0.34 * 4) & 3)`; contact frames squash `1.04 × 0.96`, passing frames `0.98 × 1.03`; lean `0.035 × facing`. Idle breathes `sy = 1 + 0.025·sin(floor(t*6)/6 * 2.8)`. Shooting squashes up to 5%, level-up wobbles ±16% for a moment, hurt squashes 15% wide.
- **Small enemy:** 4-frame waddle, rock `[0, 0.07, 0, -0.07]` rad, odd frames hop 1.1 units and stretch 1.03, even frames squash 1.05 × 0.95. Per-instance size `0.94 + seed * 0.12`.
- **Brute:** 4-frame stomp, odd frames lift 1.2 units, even frames squash 1.06 × 0.94, rock ±0.03.
- **Floater:** frame rate 1.8 cycles/s, hover `5 + sin(q*2.4 + seed*12) * 1.6` units, tilt `clamp(vx/60) * 0.12`.
- **Pickups:** bob `3 + sin(q*4 + seed*20)` units; when collected they hop `sin(πt)·9` and pop with outBack.
- **Damage numbers:** pop 0.4 → 1.25 → 1 with an extra horizontal squash in the first 22% of life, shrink to 40% and fade at the end, rotated ±0.125 rad.
- UI animations use `steps()` timing; never ease smoothly.

## Do and don't

**Do**
- Paint every shape with the clay() painter (base → key-light radial → fingerprints → inner AO → rim → detail → soft spec).
- Assemble figures back to front so each part casts a soft contact shadow on what lies behind.
- Press details in as grooves (dark furrow + light lip 0.55w lower).
- Step all animation at 12 fps and bake each frame with its own seed.
- Keep the light top-left on sprites, ground bevels, pebbles and UI gradients alike.
- Use lumpy 11-point blobs for organic forms and keep proportions chunky and toy-like.
- Reserve the candle glow ramp for important/magical things and add it with `'lighter'`.

**Don't**
- Don't draw outlines or ink lines — it becomes cartoon vector art.
- Don't use hard cel bands or black/grey shadows; shadows are soft and plum.
- Don't tween smoothly at 60 fps.
- Don't use perfect geometric circles for bodies, foliage or rocks.
- Don't add strong grain/noise overlays; texture is faint fingerprints and lumps only.
- Don't use tiny hard highlights everywhere (that is plastic/candy); clay spec is broad, only heads and berries get a glossy dot.
- Don't use neon or fully saturated hues.

## Implementation recipe

1. Set a world unit scale: e.g. 360 units of screen height; hero ≈ 21 × 33 units with feet at the origin.
2. Implement `lighten`, `darken` (toward `#fffbf0` / `#401a34`), a seeded RNG and a 2D hash.
3. Build the fingerprint tile (192 px) once.
4. Implement the `clay(ctx, shapeFn, colour, opts)` painter exactly as in the table under *Characters*, with `PK` = px per unit of the target canvas.
5. Add primitives: ellipse, capsule, lumpy blob (`lumpPts` 11 points, amt 0.06–0.25 + `blobPath` Catmull-Rom), and custom silhouettes; wrap them as `cE`, `cCap`, `cLump`.
6. Add `groove`, `eye` and `carve` helpers.
7. Design each character as an ordered list of parts (back limbs → body → front limbs → head → face). Give the head the strongest spec + gloss. Define 4 walk frames as small tables of foot/arm positions.
8. Bake every frame of every actor to a canvas at `K = clamp(round(pxPerUnit*1.2), 3, 5)` with a unique seed; store mirrored and cream-flash copies.
9. Build the ground: define material fields (noise or level-design masks), compute SDF bevel/shadow per pixel, multiply by the lumpy height modulator, then stamp decals. Cache in chunks.
10. Per frame: ground → ground glows/splats → shadows → y-sorted sprites (with 12 fps boil transforms) → projectiles → particles → numbers → vignette overlay.
11. Implement juice: crumbs, splats, squash on hit/death, cream flash, additive glows.
12. Style the HTML UI with the clay-panel CSS, Chewy extruded numbers and `steps()` animations.

## Code

The snippets below are the core techniques, ported from the reference module and runnable on their own. `starter.js` (next to this file) contains all of them wired together, plus the ground baker and a full preview scene; the complete reference module is [`../../js/styles/clay.js`](../../js/styles/clay.js).

```js
// Shade helpers: highlights toward warm white, shadows toward plum.
const mix = (a, b, t) => [a[0] + (b[0] - a[0]) * t, a[1] + (b[1] - a[1]) * t, a[2] + (b[2] - a[2]) * t];
const rgbS = (a, al) => al === undefined ? `rgb(${a[0] | 0},${a[1] | 0},${a[2] | 0})` : `rgba(${a[0] | 0},${a[1] | 0},${a[2] | 0},${al})`;
const lighten = (c, t) => mix(c, [255, 251, 240], t);
const darken = (c, t) => mix(c.map((v) => v * (1 - t)), [64, 26, 52], t * 0.3);
```

```js
// The plasticine painter. PK = canvas px per world unit, FPC = fingerprint tile canvas, PR = seeded rng().
function clay(c, shape, col, o) {
  const [cx, cy, rx, ry] = o.b, R = Math.max(rx, ry), base = rgbS(col);
  if (o.cast !== 0) {                                   // soft contact shadow on parts already painted
    c.save(); c.globalCompositeOperation = 'source-atop';
    c.shadowColor = `rgba(52,22,24,${o.cast || 0.42})`; c.shadowBlur = Math.min(R * 0.4, 2.4) * PK;
    c.shadowOffsetX = Math.min(R * 0.06, 0.45) * PK; c.shadowOffsetY = Math.min(R * 0.2, 1.4) * PK;
    c.fillStyle = base; c.beginPath(); shape(c); c.fill(); c.restore();
  }
  c.save(); c.beginPath(); shape(c); c.fillStyle = base; c.fill(); c.clip();
  const g = c.createRadialGradient(cx - rx * 0.25, cy - ry * 0.5, R * 0.04, cx + rx * 0.05, cy + ry * 0.05, R * 1.22);
  g.addColorStop(0, rgbS(lighten(col, o.lit ?? 0.2))); g.addColorStop(0.5, base); g.addColorStop(1, rgbS(o.dark || darken(col, 0.4)));
  c.fillStyle = g; c.fillRect(cx - R * 2.5, cy - R * 2.5, R * 5, R * 5);
  if (o.fp !== 0 && FPC) {                              // fingerprints, random offset per part
    const pat = c.createPattern(FPC, 'repeat'); pat.setTransform(new DOMMatrix([1 / PK, 0, 0, 1 / PK, PR() * 60, PR() * 60]));
    c.globalAlpha = o.fp || 1; c.fillStyle = pat; c.fillRect(cx - R * 1.6, cy - R * 1.6, R * 3.2, R * 3.2); c.globalAlpha = 1;
  }
  const OFF = 3000;                                     // inner AO + rim: blurred shadows of the shape's OUTSIDE
  c.save(); c.beginPath(); c.rect(cx - R * 3 + OFF, cy - R * 3, R * 6, R * 6); c.translate(OFF, 0); shape(c); c.translate(-OFF, 0);
  c.fillStyle = '#000';
  c.shadowColor = `rgba(58,20,40,${o.ao ?? 0.5})`; c.shadowBlur = R * 0.6 * PK;
  c.shadowOffsetX = -OFF * PK - R * 0.1 * PK; c.shadowOffsetY = -R * 0.3 * PK; c.fill('evenodd');
  if (o.rim !== 0) {
    c.shadowColor = `rgba(255,247,230,${o.rim ?? 0.42})`; c.shadowBlur = R * 0.26 * PK;
    c.shadowOffsetX = -OFF * PK + R * 0.04 * PK; c.shadowOffsetY = R * 0.12 * PK; c.fill('evenodd');
  }
  c.restore();
  if (o.detail) { c.save(); o.detail(c); c.restore(); }
  const sp = o.spec ?? 0.3;
  if (sp > 0) {                                         // broad, tilted soft specular (+ optional gloss dot)
    const h = o.hi || [cx - rx * 0.3, cy - ry * 0.52, R * 0.45];
    c.save(); c.translate(h[0], h[1]); c.rotate(-0.45); c.scale(1.4, 0.8);
    const sg = c.createRadialGradient(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, h[2]);
    sg.addColorStop(0, `rgba(255,255,252,${sp})`); sg.addColorStop(0.45, `rgba(255,253,244,${sp * 0.38})`); sg.addColorStop(1, 'rgba(255,252,240,0)');
    c.fillStyle = sg; c.beginPath(); c.arc(0, 0, h[2], 0, Math.PI * 2); c.fill();
    if (o.gloss) { c.fillStyle = `rgba(255,255,255,${o.gloss})`; c.beginPath(); c.ellipse(-h[2] * 0.1, -h[2] * 0.06, h[2] * 0.32, h[2] * 0.17, 0, 0, Math.PI * 2); c.fill(); }
    c.restore();
  }
  c.restore();
}
```

```js
// Lumpy hand-rolled ball: 11 jittered points joined by a closed Catmull-Rom spline.
function lumpPts(cx, cy, rx, ry, n, amt, r) {
  const pts = [], ph = r() * Math.PI * 2;
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const a = (i / n) * Math.PI * 2, k = 1 + (r() - 0.5) * amt + Math.sin(a * 3 + ph) * amt * 0.25;
    pts.push([cx + Math.cos(a) * rx * k, cy + Math.sin(a) * ry * k]);
  }
  return pts;
}
function blobPath(c, pts) {
  const n = pts.length; c.moveTo(pts[0][0], pts[0][1]);
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const p0 = pts[(i - 1 + n) % n], p1 = pts[i], p2 = pts[(i + 1) % n], p3 = pts[(i + 2) % n];
    c.bezierCurveTo(p1[0] + (p2[0] - p0[0]) / 6, p1[1] + (p2[1] - p0[1]) / 6, p2[0] - (p3[0] - p1[0]) / 6, p2[1] - (p3[1] - p1[1]) / 6, p2[0], p2[1]);
  }
  c.closePath();
}
// Pressed groove (ribs, folds, wood grain): dark furrow + light lip below.
function groove(c, path, w, a) {
  c.lineCap = 'round'; c.strokeStyle = `rgba(58,22,18,${a})`; c.lineWidth = w; c.beginPath(); path(c); c.stroke();
  c.save(); c.translate(0, w * 0.55); c.strokeStyle = `rgba(255,240,220,${a * 0.75})`; c.lineWidth = w * 0.5;
  c.beginPath(); path(c); c.stroke(); c.restore();
}
// Carved hole with candle light shifted down (wall thickness).
function carve(c, path, glow) {
  c.save(); c.beginPath(); path(c); c.fillStyle = '#4e1606'; c.fill(); c.clip();
  c.translate(0.15, 0.8); c.beginPath(); path(c); c.fillStyle = glow; c.fill(); c.restore();
}
```

```js
// Raised clay sheet edge, per pixel. dist = signed distance in px (>0 inside), ld = edge facing light (-1..1),
// bwPx/swPx = bevel 3.0 and shadow 3.4 world units in px. Returns new [r,g,b] over the colour underneath.
function sheetPixel(under, layer, dist, ld, bwPx, swPx) {
  let [r, g, b] = under;
  if (dist < 0.5) {                                   // cast shadow just outside the sheet
    let sh = 1 + dist / swPx;
    if (sh > 0) { sh = Math.min(1, sh); const k = 0.4 * sh * sh * (0.35 + 0.65 * Math.max(0, -ld)); r *= 1 - k; g *= 1 - k; b *= 1 - k; }
  }
  if (dist > -0.5) {                                  // lit bevel + bright crest inside the edge
    const cov = Math.min(1, dist + 0.5), p = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, 1 - dist / bwPx)), cr = (p - 0.55) / 0.22;
    const f = 1 + ld * 0.42 * p * p + 0.09 * Math.exp(-cr * cr) - 0.03 * p * p * p;
    r += (layer[0] * f - r) * cov; g += (layer[1] * f - g) * cov; b += (layer[2] * f - b) * cov;
  }
  return [r, g, b];                                   // afterwards multiply by (1 + MOD * m) for the lumpy surface
}
```

## Adapting it to your game

- **Keep fixed:** the clay() painter and its numbers, no outlines, top-left warm light, plum shadows, 12 fps stepping with boil, fingerprints, grooves for detail, raised-sheet ground with bevels, the cream clay UI slabs.
- **May change:** all hues. Swap palettes per biome (e.g. snow world: sheets `#e8eef4` / `#b8c8dc`, ice pond, but keep shadows plum-blue and highlights warm), as long as sheets stay mid-value and characters stay brighter and glossier.
- **New characters:** compose from 8–25 primitives; give each type a unique silhouette and colour pair; eyes are the main readability cue. Brutes = more lumps + glowing cracks/core; flyers = single smooth silhouette, cool shading, floating shadow.
- **Other genres:** side-scrollers work well — turn the ground into stacked clay strata (same bevel maths along a horizontal edge) and keep the soft shadow under actors. Puzzle games: tiles become clay slabs with the UI panel recipe.
- **Other resolutions:** keep `K` between 3 and 5 px/unit; below 3 the AO/rim blur disappears, above 5 baking costs balloon. For tiny on-screen units (< 10 units) reduce to base + key light + spec.

## Performance notes

- Never call the clay() painter per frame — it uses several `shadowBlur` fills per part. Bake everything (hero 5 frames × 2 faces, enemies 4 frames × variants, props, particles, icons) at init; the reference bakes ~80 sprites in well under a second.
- Per frame cost is just `drawImage` blits + a handful of additive glow sprites + one full-screen overlay sprite (< 2 ms for hundreds of actors).
- Ground is the hot spot: per-pixel SDF + texture lookup. Render 256-unit chunks lazily with a generator (yield every 4 rows / per 128-pixel band), cap ground resolution at 2.5 px/unit, and skip per-pixel SDF work in grid cells that are fully inside or outside every sheet (classify each 4-unit cell first — the reference does this and only runs the full maths near edges).
- Cache damage-number sprites per value (clear above 400 entries); wait for the Chewy font before caching.
- Clay splats are capped at 150; crumbs are pooled particles.

## Copy-paste prompt

```text
Build my game <X> in the "Clay World" style (stop-motion plasticine miniature set):
- Canvas 2D, procedural, no image assets, no outlines anywhere.
- Every body part goes through one clay() painter: flat base, radial key-light gradient from the upper-left
  (lighten 0.2 toward #fffbf0 -> base at 0.5 -> darken 0.4 toward plum #401a34 at 1.22R), a tiled faint fingerprint
  pattern, inner ambient occlusion rgba(58,20,40,0.5) along the bottom and a warm rim rgba(255,247,230,0.42) along the
  top (both made with blurred offset shadows of the shape's outside), then a broad soft specular tilted -0.45 rad.
- Characters are chunky toy assemblies of lumpy balls, capsules and blobs painted back to front; each part casts a
  soft contact shadow onto parts behind it. Big glossy heads, googly white-clay eyes or carved glowing faces.
- Details are pressed grooves (dark furrow + light lip below), never drawn lines.
- Ground: flat clay sheets (meadow #76a454, purple #66507e, soil #986c4a, ochre path #d6a262, sunken pond #7ebad2)
  with raised bevelled edges (3 units), soft cast shadows (3.4 units), light from (-0.42,-0.907), a lumpy hand-pressed
  height texture, and imprinted decals (grass tool marks, flowers, pebbles, thumbprints, lily pads, glossy reflections).
- Warm studio lighting: soft plum-brown ellipse shadows under actors, additive candle glow (#fff7c4 -> #ffd458 -> #ff8f22),
  warm brown vignette.
- Bake all sprites once at 3-5 px per world unit, one seeded bake per animation frame (boil); animate at 12 fps steps
  with small hash jitter in scale/rotation; squash and stretch on steps, hits and deaths; clay crumb particles and splats.
- UI: cream clay slabs with inner highlight/shadow, a solid darker base for thickness, uneven border radii, Chewy
  extruded numbers (#f07a24 with stacked darker text-shadows), Baloo 2 body text, steps() animations.
```
