<!-- style: crossstitch · https://miwale.com/styles/library/crossstitch/STYLE.md -->

# Cross-Stitch Sampler — Game Art Style Spec

> The whole game is a living cross-stitch sampler on Aida cloth: every cell is a real thread X, contours are backstitched.

The world is a piece of beige Aida fabric with visible holes. Everything that is not bare cloth is embroidered on a 3.2-unit stitch grid: characters and props are small cell grids in which every cell is a two-stroke thread cross with its own shadow, sheen and ply twist, outlined with a dark backstitch. Flowers are French knots and lazy daisies, water is satin stitch, pickups are glass beads and sewing buttons, enemies are stitched into existence by a darting needle and unravel into loose threads when they die. It reads like grandma's Halloween sampler come to life — warm, cosy, tactile. The reference implementation is the game *Jack vs. the Turnip Ancestors* (pumpkin-head hero, turnip creepers, ghosts, a turnip colossus); everything below is written so you can use it for any game.

## At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Family | Textile · Cross-stitch embroidery |
| Mood | cozy, handmade, nostalgic, whimsical, autumnal |
| Best for | top-down survivors/arena games, cozy farming or adventure, grid puzzle/board games, seasonal games |
| Renderer | Canvas 2D, fully procedural, no image assets |
| Pixel art | No (`pixelArt: false`) — native resolution, but all art is quantised to a 3.2-unit stitch grid |
| Difficulty | 3/10 — works like pixel art on a coarse grid; new motifs are simple stitch patterns |
| Fonts | Grandstander (600–900) for numbers/titles, Mali (500–700) for text |
| Key colours | Aida `#dccaa5`, outline `#2b1d1d`, pumpkin `#e2701f`, leaf `#55843a`, turnip `#83479a`, pond `#43729e`, rust `#a24f2a` |

## When to use it

- **Good fits:** top-down games with small, iconic actors; anything cosy, seasonal, folk-tale or "made by grandma"; games on a grid (tactics, puzzles, roguelikes) where the stitch grid doubles as the game grid; crowds of enemies (each type is a strong colour block).
- **Also good:** menus and HUDs — fabric tags, embroidery hoops and stitched titles are very recognisable.
- **Bad fits:** smooth rotation or squash-and-stretch animation (motifs only snap and swap frames); realistic or gritty tone; perspective/3D cameras; bosses that need fine facial detail (a 15×17-cell brute is about the limit of readability); very fast games where the 3.2-unit steppy motion would feel jittery.

## Color palette

Every colour is a named thread with a one-letter code (used directly in the motif strings). The real hex values:

| Swatch | Code | Hex | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Aida cloth | — | `#dccaa5` | Fabric base (renderer clear colour `#d9c8a4`), ~50 % of the screen |
| Backstitch black | K | `#2b1d1d` | Outline thread of characters and props |
| Pumpkin dark / rust / orange / light | Q q O o | `#6c2817` `#a4401b` `#e2701f` `#f59b40` | Hero head, pumpkins, autumn trees |
| Candle yellow / pale | y Y | `#ffd23c` `#fff2a6` | Carved faces, eyes, glowing bits |
| Greens dark→light | G g l L | `#2d5230` `#55843a` `#8daf55` `#b3c07c` | Meadow stitches, stems, pines, crowns |
| Browns | B b k | `#45291c` `#7c4a2b` `#c79a66` | Trunks, roots, feet, path border |
| Purples | P p m | `#4f2560` `#83479a` `#bc8ac7` | Small enemy body |
| Creams | c C w | `#f3e6bf` `#d8bc7f` `#fbf8f0` | Enemy faces, seeds, highlights |
| Ghost blues | i I j | `#d5e6f2` `#97b6d4` `#3c5078` | Fast spirit enemy (j = its outline + eyes) |
| Reds | r R E | `#c3312b` `#7a1c24` `#e65f3e` | Scarf, hearts, mushrooms, crits |
| Greys | a A e | `#9f9a93` `#5f5a58` `#d0cbc2` | Gravestones, metal |
| Cloak | d D | `#1d3f55` `#2e6479` | Hero body |
| Field ochre | f F h t | `#c99a3e` `#a6782e` `#e3b24d` `#f2d37c` | Crop rows, gold trees, gold accents |
| Rust forest | x X z | `#a24f2a` `#84391f` `#6b3b24` | Forest floor fill |
| Pond | N n u W | `#2b4b70` `#43729e` `#7faacf` `#bcd6ea` | Satin water, deep → shallow |
| Flowers | s v V | `#e58ca2` `#7b59a8` `#a98bd0` | French knots, daisies |
| Shadow | — | `#28160c` / `rgba(40,22,10,a)` | Every shadow |

**Palette rules**

- Shading never invents colours: a darker area switches to the next thread in the ramp (e.g. `Q → q → O → o`).
- Each stitch derives four tones from its thread: underlay `colour × 0.64`, underside `colour × 0.7`, top ply `colour`, sheen `mix(colour, white, 0.5)` at α 0.75. Hit flash = `mix(colour, white, 0.6)`.
- Bare fabric dominates. Meadow is stitched at only 3–40 % density; forests and ponds are dense but bounded by backstitch.
- Shadows are always warm brown `rgba(40,22,10,a)`; never black, never grey.
- One hue family per actor type (hero orange + navy, small enemy purple + cream, spirit pale blue, brute purple over brown) so crowds stay readable on the beige cloth.
- Gradients only on round "hardware": French knots, beads, buttons, sequins, needles, glows. Never inside stitched areas.

## Typography

- **Grandstander** — weights 600, 700, 800, 900. Chunky rounded display face for the timer, numbers, card names and big titles. <https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Grandstander>
- **Mali** — weights 500, 600, 700. Friendly handwriting for labels, descriptions, hints. <https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Mali>

Google Fonts families as loaded by the module: `Grandstander:wght@600;700;800;900`, `Mali:wght@500;600;700`.

```css
body { font-family: 'Mali', 'Grandstander', sans-serif; color: #4a2c1e; }
.timer { font: 900 35px/1 'Grandstander', sans-serif; letter-spacing: 1px; color: #a3302a;
  text-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(255,250,235,.9), 0 2px 0 rgba(90,30,15,.25); }
.value { font: 800 17px 'Grandstander', sans-serif; color: #7a1c24; text-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.6); }
.label { font: 700 11px 'Mali', sans-serif; color: #6a3a1e; }
```

Text effects: a 1 px cream "embossed" highlight shadow below dark text on fabric; big titles ("Level up!", "Game over", "Pause") are filled with a tiled cross-stitch texture using `background-clip: text; color: transparent` plus `filter: drop-shadow(0 3px 0 #3a1a0c)`. In-world damage numbers are not a font at all: they are 3×5-cell stitched digit motifs.

## Rendering technique

World units: the camera shows 360 units vertically. One stitch cell `C = 3.2` units; motif sprites are baked at `CP = 8` px per cell (so `K = C / CP = 0.4` units per sprite px), with a 2 px margin around each stitch sprite (`SM`) and 5 px around each motif (`MP`).

1. **Init — fabric:** bake a 16×16-hole Aida tile (128 px). Per pixel: hole corners ×0.74, hole edges ×0.93, inner 2×2 weave checker ×1.03 / ×0.985, plus ±3.5 % row and column slub noise and ±3 % grain on base `#dccaa5`. Add 22 long 1-px slub threads (`rgba(255,250,235,0.16)` or `rgba(110,80,40,0.08)`), wrapped so the tile stays seamless.
2. **Init — stitches:** for every thread colour bake 3 jittered variants of a full cross (`makeStitch`): two diagonal strokes (`/` first, then `\` on top), each drawn as shadow (`rgba(40,22,10,.36)`, width 3.1, offset +0.45/+0.85), dark body (×0.7, width 2.9), top ply (width 2.0, nudged −0.22 up), sheen (mix white 0.5, α 0.75, width 0.7, from 18 % to 78 % of the stroke) and three twist ticks (×0.62, α 0.45, width 0.55). Endpoints jitter ±0.25 px. Half stitches use only the `/` stroke.
3. **Init — motifs:** every character frame, prop, icon and digit is a cell grid → `renderMotif`: blurred shadow (`blur(1.1px)`, α 0.42, offset 1.4/2.4 px) → underlay rect per cell (`colour × 0.64`, inset 0.6 px, so fabric barely shows) → one stitch variant per cell (`hash(x, y) % 3`) → backstitch outline along every silhouette edge (2.2 px) → inner contours (1.7 px) → free backstitch segments (stems, brows, mouths, 1.4–2.4 px).
4. **Per chunk (256 units = 80×80 cells), built incrementally as a generator:** fabric pattern fill → classify every cell (meadow / forest / field / pond / path) → lighten path cells → merge stitched cells into per-colour row runs in a `Path2D` and fill each with a seamless 4×4-stitch pattern (`createPattern` with `setTransform(DOMMatrix([K,0,0,K,0,0]))`) → satin-stitch pond → decals → backstitched region borders → soft cloth-fold overlay.
5. **Per frame, world space:** ground chunks → hero light pool (additive) → gems → shadows → y-sorted props/enemies/hero (all snapped to the cell grid via `blitCell`) → orbiting lanterns → projectiles → particles → stitched damage numbers.
6. **Screen space:** brown radial vignette sprite stretched over the screen; with run progress a `multiply` tint of `#2a2050` up to α 0.16.
7. **Grid snapping:** sprite origins are always whole cells: `gx = round(x / C − w / 2)`, `gy = round(y / C) − h`, drawn at `(gx·C − MP·K, gy·C − MP·K)`. Only particles, beads and projectiles move freely.

## Background and ground

The ground is an endless sampler. Noise fields (domain-warped fbm) decide the material per cell:

- **Path** (winding, half-width 7.5–12.5 units, from the zero line of warped Perlin noise): no stitches at all, just the cloth lightened with `rgba(255,250,236,0.42)`, edged on both sides with a `#7c4a2b` backstitch — the classic "unstitched linen road".
- **Meadow** (default): sparse full crosses in `L`/`l`/`g` (dry patches: `t`/`L`/`l`). Density `0.03 + 0.24·smoothstep(0.36, 0.78, fbm)` plus up to `+0.36` near forests; a cell is stitched when `bayer8·0.55 + hash·0.45 < density`, so stitches cluster organically.
- **Forest** (warped fbm > 0.58): every cell stitched in rust `z`/`X`/`x` (tone from fbm + Bayer), 1.8 % gold `h` and 1.6 % orange `o` accents, plus leaf motifs, mushrooms and brown knot pairs. Border: `#45291c` backstitch.
- **Fields** (cell-aligned rectangles, 160–320 × 110–220 units): rows of half stitches `/` in crop colours; every 4th row empty; rutabaga fields get purple knots; optional fences and a scarecrow.
- **Pond** (warped fbm > 0.66): satin stitch — blocks of up to 3 cells in a brick pattern (block start offset `j % 3`), each block 3 slanted parallel threads; tone `W/u/n/N` by depth; lily pads and white ripple threads. Border: navy `#2b4b70` backstitch.
- **Decals** on a 21-unit jittered grid (only on cells whose 4 neighbours share the material): French-knot flower clusters (3–5 knots in `s w h V m E` with a yellow centre and two green stem threads), lazy daisies (5 looped petals + tack stitches), three-stitch grass tufts from one hole, sequins, rows of three beads, mushrooms.
- **Cloth light**: one RGBA value per cell, smoothed: folds `(perlin(u/1100, (v−7)/260) − perlin(u/1100, (v+7)/260))·1.3` on a rotated axis, warm white `(255,248,228)` for positive, brown `(62,38,22)` for negative, α ≤ 0.15.

## Characters

The hero is a **9 × 11-cell** grid (28.8 × 35.2 units), facing right; left is a mirrored grid (free backstitch segments are mirrored too):

```
....gG...    leaf stem (g/G) + a curly backstitch stem segment
..qoOOq..
.qoOOOOq.    pumpkin head: ramp q/o/O, lit upper-left
qoOYyOYyq    carved eyes Y/y
qoOOOOOOq
qOyYyYyYq    carved grin
.qOyOyOq.
..RrrrR..    red scarf
.rdDDDdk.    navy cloak d/D, scarf end r, hand k   (frame 0)
..dDDDd..
..BB.BB..    boots
```

- Frames 1 and 2 only change the last three rows (hand swings, legs apart/together). Walk sequence `1,0,2,0`.
- Outline `K #2b1d1d` at 2.2 px; inner contour `Q #6c2817` at 1.7 px around the yellow carving (`inner: { keys: 'yY', k: 'Q' }`) so the face reads as cut into the shell.
- Extras: a white-flash copy per frame (`mix(c, white, 0.6)`, no shadow) for hurt; an additive candle glow (`rgb(255,150,60)` radial, 24×18 units, α `0.22 + 0.07 sin 9t + 0.05 sin 23t`) over the face; a 26-unit soft brown ellipse shadow under the feet; a large warm light pool (80×52 units, α ~0.5) on the ground.
- Rules: big head, 2–3-row body, 1-row feet; at most 4 threads per material; the brightest thread (yellow) is reserved for the face.

## Enemies and props

- **Small melee enemy** (turnip creeper, 7 × 8 cells): rows 0–1 leaf crown (3 frames: leaves wiggle), purple body `P/p/m` with yellow eyes, cream face `C/c`, row 7 legs `k` (3 frames). Backstitch brows (`K`, 1.6) and a zig-zag mouth (`R`). A second variant is made by **remapping** threads (`p→#a8487a, P→#6c2550, m→#d888b0`) — cheap variety.
- **Fast enemy** (ghost, 8 × 8): `i/w/I` body with `j #3c5078` eyes and outline (no black outline → lighter, airy), drawn at α 0.9, hovers 1–2 cells above its shadow, 3 tail frames at 5 fps, half-strength shadow.
- **Brute** (colossus, 15 × 17, procedural): a sphere lit by `l = −0.5nx − 0.55ny + 0.62nz + bayer4 jitter`, purple ramp `P/p/m` on the upper part and brown `z/b/k` below a wavy line, leaf crown, 2-cell yellow eyes, a yellow/red tooth row, root arms that rise per frame, backstitch brows, cracks and a smile. Additive glow over the face.
- **Spawn/death:** 6 partial masks per actor (cells sorted bottom-up with random jitter), rendered without outline and with shadow α 0.25. Spawn shows them in order while a silver needle with red thread darts across the current row; death plays them in reverse while fading.
- **Props** (y-sorted, snapped to cells, sort key = foot row): round autumn trees 13 × 16 (lit-sphere crown with 4-thread ramps `Q q O o`, `R r E o`, `F f h t`, `X q O h`; stitched trunk `k/b/z`), pines 11 × 17 (tiered, `l/g/G` by side), bare trees (pure backstitch branches 2.4 px + a crow), pumpkin pairs, gravestones 5 × 7, scarecrows, a little house, fences (rails as 2.6-px backstitch). Trees turn 55 % transparent when the hero walks behind them.
- Readability: every actor and prop has the dark outline + blurred drop shadow; ground has neither, so actors always pop off the cloth.

## Effects and particles

Everything is an embroidery material:

- **Projectile:** a cream seed (quadratic shape, gradient `#fffaf0 → #f3e6bf → #c9a86a`, outline `#8a6a3a`, 4 rib lines) with a 3-dash running-stitch trail in `rgba(255,214,120,0.35–0.75)`; sprite 56×20 px drawn at 14×5 units, rotated to velocity.
- **Hit:** cream French knot pop (life 0.18 s) + 60 % chance of one loose thread snippet; white-flash overlay on the sprite.
- **Loose thread snippet:** a 6-point random curl drawn with `quadraticCurveTo` in 4 passes (shadow 2.6, dark 2.4, body 1.4, sheen 0.5 px), 8 units, spinning, gravity 120–160.
- **Kill:** 7 threads (brute 16) in the enemy's colours, 2 beads (ghost 1, brute 5), brute drops a 4-hole button, and a dashed ring (`setLineDash([1.6, 1.2])`, width 0.9, cream or `#97b6d4`) expands 3→11 units (brute 6→22) with ease-out-quad over 0.3 s.
- **Pickups:** small = orange glass bead `#f39a2e` (radial gradient, dark hole, white glint), 5.4 units, additive glow 13 units, bob 0.8; big = gold sewing button `#e3b24d` with cream cross thread, 9 units, rocking ±0.3 rad. Pickup = 1–5 cross-stitch sparks (a stitch sprite at 2.4 units).
- **Orbiting weapon:** a 5×5-cell stitched lantern with a 28-unit additive glow.
- **Dash:** 2 ghost copies of the hero at α 0.22/k + soft fluff glows.
- **Level-up:** two dashed ellipses (gold `#e3b24d`, red `#c3312b`, dash 2.4/1.6) growing from 8 to 54 units, 16 sparks in a ring, 4 buttons.
- **Hurt / death of hero:** orange threads (`#e2701f`, `#f59b40`), red dashed ring; on death 20 threads in orange/navy/red.
- **Damage numbers:** stitched 3×5 digits (white `w` + black outline; crits `y` + `R` outline), cell size 1.3 units (crit 1.8), pop ×1.4 at spawn.

## Lighting, shadows and post-processing

- Light comes from the **upper left** everywhere: stitch shadows fall down-right, sheen lines sit up-left, sphere-shaded motifs use `(−0.5, −0.6, 0.62)`.
- **Motif drop shadow:** silhouette in `#28160c`, `blur(1.1px)`, α 0.42, offset (1.4, 2.4) px — the motif looks slightly raised off the cloth.
- **Ground shadows** under actors: a pre-baked radial ellipse (`rgba(50,28,12,.55 → .25 → 0)`), width 26 (hero), 20 (small), 16 at α 0.5 (ghost), 46 (brute), 26–34 under trees.
- **Coloured light:** additive (`lighter`) radial glow sprites in warm orange/yellow: hero pool `rgb(255,170,70)` α 0.32, face/brute glow `rgb(255,150,60)` α 0.5, gem/lantern glows `rgb(255,190–205,80–110)`. All flicker with summed sines.
- **Vignette:** 320×180 radial gradient `rgba(60,30,12,0) → 0.10 at 70 % → rgba(40,18,8,0.42)`, stretched over the screen.
- **Night grading:** `multiply` fill `#2a2050` at α `min(0.16, progress × 0.2)` — the cloth gets dusky towards the end, but stays readable.

## UI and HUD

HUD elements are sewn objects: fabric tags with a satin-stitched border and a dashed running-stitch line, bars filled with cross-stitch tiles, the timer is a wooden embroidery hoop with a metal clasp. Backgrounds use the same Aida generator rendered to data URLs (`#efe3c4` light, `#ddcba4` darker), and 8×8 px stitch tiles (one stitch on fabric) for bar fills. Icons are 12×12-cell stitched motifs. Tag border colours: red `#c0442c/#8c2a1c/#e0704c` (health), purple `#6e3a80/#4c2160/#9a62ac` (score), green `#5c8a3c/#3a6028/#86b45a` (info); level-up cards in orange, purple and green, tilting −1.5° on hover.

```css
.tag { border: 5px solid transparent; border-radius: 12px; padding: 7px 16px 7px 10px;
  background: url(aida.png) padding-box,
    repeating-linear-gradient(-52deg, #c0442c 0 2px, #8c2a1c 2px 3px, #e0704c 3px 4.5px) border-box;
  outline: 2px dashed rgba(124,29,36,.55); outline-offset: -10px;
  box-shadow: 0 4px 0 rgba(50,26,10,.35), 0 6px 14px rgba(20,10,4,.35);
  font-family: 'Mali', 'Grandstander', sans-serif; color: #4a2c1e; }
.bar { width: 216px; height: 18px; border-radius: 3px; background: url(aida-dark.png) 0 0/32px 32px;
  box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(110,70,30,.45), inset 0 2px 3px rgba(60,30,10,.25); }
.bar-fill { height: 100%; background: url(stitch-red.png) 0 1px/8px 8px; }
.hoop { width: 138px; height: 138px; border-radius: 50%; border: 10px solid transparent;
  background: radial-gradient(circle, rgba(255,250,235,.5) 0 40%, rgba(120,80,40,.18) 100%) padding-box,
    url(aida.png) padding-box,
    repeating-radial-gradient(circle, #c98f55 0 2px, #b47842 2px 3.5px, #d9a46a 3.5px 5px) border-box;
  box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px #7a4c26, inset 0 5px 10px rgba(70,40,15,.35), 0 0 0 2px #6b4221,
    0 0 0 5px #d39c60, 0 0 0 7px #6b4221, 0 7px 0 rgba(40,20,8,.3), 0 8px 18px rgba(20,10,4,.4); }
.hoop::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 4px; border-radius: 50%; border: 2px dashed rgba(124,29,36,.5); }
.stitched-title { font: 900 70px 'Grandstander', sans-serif; letter-spacing: 2px;
  background: url(stitch-orange.png) 0 0/8px 8px; -webkit-background-clip: text; background-clip: text;
  color: transparent; filter: drop-shadow(0 3px 0 #3a1a0c) drop-shadow(0 0 1px #3a1a0c); }
.overlay { background: radial-gradient(ellipse at 50% 45%, rgba(80,45,20,.3), rgba(28,14,8,.82)); }
```

Generate `aida.png` with the fabric generator (4×4 holes of 8 px, base `#efe3c4`) and `stitch-*.png` as an 8×8 canvas with a darkened underlay and one `makeStitch` sprite.

## Motion and animation

- **Steppy by design:** actors snap to the 3.2-unit grid; they move in whole stitches.
- **Hero:** 3 frames, sequence `1,0,2,0`, frame = `floor(distanceWalked / 5) & 3`; idle frame 0. Only the bottom rows change.
- **Small enemy:** sequence `0,1,0,2`, frame = `floor(anim·1.6 + seed·4) & 3` with `anim = distance / 10`. **Spirit:** `floor(t·5 + seed·7) % 3`, hover 1–2 cells toggled by `sin(2.2t + seed·9) > 0.3`.
- **Spawn:** 6 stitching steps (about 1 s), needle oscillates `sin(30t)` across the motif width. **Death:** reverse steps, α `min(1, progress·3)`.
- **Hit flash:** white-flash copy overlaid at α `min(1, flash·1.3)·0.9`. **I-frames:** blink at 18 Hz to α 0.45.
- **Idle life:** glows flicker (`0.5 + 0.06 sin 7.3t + 0.04 sin 13.1t`), gems bob 0.8 units at 3 rad/s, lanterns bob 0.8 at 4 rad/s, big buttons rock `0.3 sin 2t`.
- **Particles** obey gravity (120–220) and drag (1.2–3), threads spin (`vr` ±4–5 rad/s), lifetimes 0.2–1.6 s, alpha `min(1, life·2.2)`.

## Do and don't

**Do**

- Build every sprite from a cell grid of thread codes; render each cell as a real thread X with underside, top ply, sheen and twist.
- Keep the Aida holes visible everywhere and aligned with the stitch grid (cells at multiples of 3.2 units).
- Outline silhouettes and region borders with backstitch segments that stop just short of each hole.
- Use embroidery vocabulary for every effect: French knots, beads, buttons, sequins, satin stitch, running stitch, loose threads, needles, hoops.
- Leave lots of bare fabric; suggest meadow and transitions with dithered stitch density.
- Bake stitch variants and ground chunks once; fill large areas with seamless stitch patterns.

**Don't**

- Don't use flat filled squares — it reads as pixel art, not embroidery.
- Don't rotate, scale or sub-cell-offset stitched motifs (only round hardware and projectiles rotate).
- Don't use black/grey shadows, vector ink outlines or neon colours.
- Don't stitch the whole ground densely; the fabric must breathe.
- Don't fade enemies out; unravel them stitch by stitch and leave threads.
- Don't exceed 3–4 threads per material or invent intermediate colours.

## Implementation recipe

1. Set up world units: 360 visible vertically; constants `C = 3.2`, `CP = 8`, `K = 0.4`, `SM = 2`, `MP = 5`. Smoothing stays on.
2. Define the thread palette as a map of single letters → hex (table above). Add new threads in ramps of 3–4.
3. Write the fabric generator (hole grid + weave + slubs) and bake a 16×16-hole tile.
4. Write `makeStitch(rgb, variant)` (two strokes × 5 passes) and cache 3 variants per colour; write `stitchPattern(code)` (seamless 4×4 tile).
5. Write `threadSegs(ctx, segs, rgb, width, gap)` — the 4-pass backstitch used for every line in the game.
6. Write `motif(rows, outline, segs)` + `renderMotif(m, opts)` (shadow, underlay, stitches, outline, inner contour, free segments) + `mirror(m)` + `blitCell(ctx, sprite, gx, gy)`.
7. Design actors as string grids (hero 9×11, small enemy ~7×8, fast enemy ~8×8, brute ~15×17); 3 frames that only change legs/crown/tail; bake right, left, flash and 5 partial spawn masks.
8. Build the ground per chunk: fabric fill → classify cells → bare path → per-colour run paths filled with stitch patterns → satin water → knot/daisy/tuft decals → backstitched borders → cloth folds. Spread it over frames (generator) if the world is infinite.
9. Props: more string grids or procedural lit-sphere crowns quantised to thread ramps; y-sort them with actors; snap to cells.
10. Effects: knots, beads, buttons, thread curls, dashed rings, needle, seed — all baked as small sprites at init.
11. Light: warm additive glow sprites (hero pool, faces, pickups), soft brown ellipse shadows, brown vignette, optional multiply night tint.
12. HUD: fabric tags with satin borders and dashed stitch lines, stitched bar fills, embroidery-hoop timer, Grandstander + Mali, stitched-texture titles.

## Code

The core techniques, standalone. The full working kit is [`starter.js`](starter.js) (palette, fabric, stitches, backstitch, motif renderer, hero, enemies, stitched ground, beads, glows, preview scene); the complete reference module is [`../../js/styles/crossstitch.js`](../../js/styles/crossstitch.js).

Shared helpers used below:

```js
const C = 3.2, CP = 8, K = C / CP, SM = 2, MP = 5, WHITE = [255, 255, 255];
const lerp = (a, b, t) => a + (b - a) * t;
const mul = (c, f) => c.map((v) => Math.min(255, v * f));
const mix = (a, b, t) => a.map((v, i) => v + (b[i] - v) * t);
const rgb = (c, a) => (a === undefined ? `rgb(${c[0] | 0},${c[1] | 0},${c[2] | 0})` : `rgba(${c[0] | 0},${c[1] | 0},${c[2] | 0},${a})`);
function rng(seed) { let a = seed >>> 0; return { next() { a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) | 0; let t = Math.imul(a ^ (a >>> 15), 1 | a);
  t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t; return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296; } }; }
function hashInt(x, y, s) { let h = (Math.imul(x, 374761393) + Math.imul(y, 668265263) + Math.imul(s, 1442695041)) | 0;
  h = Math.imul(h ^ (h >>> 13), 1274126177); h ^= h >>> 16; return h >>> 0; }
```

**1. One cross stitch** — the atom of the style (bake 3 variants per colour):

```js
function makeStitch(c3, v) {
  const c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width = c.height = CP + SM * 2;
  const ctx = c.getContext('2d'), r = rng(v * 977 + c3[0] * 3 + c3[1] * 7 + c3[2] * 11), j = () => (r.next() - 0.5) * 0.5;
  const a = SM + 0.85, b = SM + CP - 0.85, base = mul(c3, 0.95 + r.next() * 0.1);
  const line = (x0, y0, x1, y1) => { ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(x0, y0); ctx.lineTo(x1, y1); ctx.stroke(); };
  ctx.lineCap = 'round';
  [[a + j(), b + j(), b + j(), a + j(), -1], [a + j(), a + j(), b + j(), b + j(), 1]].forEach(([x0, y0, x1, y1, dir], n) => {
    ctx.strokeStyle = n ? 'rgba(40,22,10,0.30)' : 'rgba(40,22,10,0.36)'; ctx.lineWidth = 3.1;
    line(x0 + 0.45, y0 + 0.85, x1 + 0.45, y1 + 0.85);                          // shadow
    ctx.strokeStyle = rgb(mul(base, 0.7)); ctx.lineWidth = 2.9; line(x0, y0, x1, y1); // underside
    const px = dir < 0 ? -0.18 : 0.18;
    ctx.strokeStyle = rgb(base); ctx.lineWidth = 2.0; line(x0 + px, y0 - 0.22, x1 + px, y1 - 0.22); // top ply
    const hx = dir < 0 ? -0.55 : 0.5;
    ctx.strokeStyle = rgb(mix(base, WHITE, 0.5), 0.75); ctx.lineWidth = 0.7;    // sheen
    line(lerp(x0, x1, 0.18) + hx, lerp(y0, y1, 0.18) - 0.6, lerp(x0, x1, 0.78) + hx, lerp(y0, y1, 0.78) - 0.6);
    ctx.strokeStyle = rgb(mul(base, 0.62), 0.45); ctx.lineWidth = 0.55;         // two-ply twist ticks
    const dx = x1 - x0, dy = y1 - y0, L = Math.hypot(dx, dy), ux = dx / L, uy = dy / L;
    for (const t of [0.3, 0.52, 0.74]) {
      const cx = x0 + dx * t, cy = y0 + dy * t;
      line(cx + uy * 0.9 - ux * 0.5, cy - ux * 0.9 - uy * 0.5, cx - uy * 0.9 + ux * 0.5, cy + ux * 0.9 + uy * 0.5);
    }
  });
  return c;
}
```

**2. Backstitch** — every outline, stem, border and fence rail:

```js
// segs = flat [x0,y0,x1,y1, ...]; w = thread width; gap = shortening at each hole
function threadSegs(ctx, segs, c3, w, gap) {
  const path = (dx, dy) => {
    ctx.beginPath();
    for (let k = 0; k < segs.length; k += 4) {
      const x0 = segs[k], y0 = segs[k + 1], x1 = segs[k + 2], y1 = segs[k + 3];
      const L = Math.hypot(x1 - x0, y1 - y0) || 1, g = Math.min(gap, L * 0.3), gx = (x1 - x0) / L * g, gy = (y1 - y0) / L * g;
      ctx.moveTo(x0 + gx + dx, y0 + gy + dy); ctx.lineTo(x1 - gx + dx, y1 - gy + dy);
    }
  };
  ctx.lineCap = 'round';
  path(w * 0.28, w * 0.42); ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(35,20,10,0.36)'; ctx.lineWidth = w * 1.12; ctx.stroke();
  path(0, 0); ctx.strokeStyle = rgb(mul(c3, 0.72)); ctx.lineWidth = w; ctx.stroke();
  path(-w * 0.06, -w * 0.08); ctx.strokeStyle = rgb(c3); ctx.lineWidth = w * 0.62; ctx.stroke();
  path(-w * 0.16, -w * 0.22); ctx.strokeStyle = rgb(mix(c3, WHITE, 0.45), 0.7); ctx.lineWidth = w * 0.26; ctx.stroke();
}
```

**3. Motif renderer** — cell grid → embroidered sprite, drawn snapped to the world grid:

```js
// m = { w, h, cell: [code|null], outline: code }; col(code) -> [r,g,b]; stitchSet(rgb) -> 3 makeStitch variants
function renderMotif(m, col, stitchSet) {
  const c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width = m.w * CP + MP * 2; c.height = m.h * CP + MP * 2;
  const ctx = c.getContext('2d'), has = (x, y) => x >= 0 && y >= 0 && x < m.w && y < m.h && !!m.cell[y * m.w + x];
  const sh = document.createElement('canvas'); sh.width = c.width; sh.height = c.height;
  const sx = sh.getContext('2d'); sx.fillStyle = '#28160c';
  for (let y = 0; y < m.h; y++) for (let x = 0; x < m.w; x++) if (has(x, y)) sx.fillRect(MP + x * CP, MP + y * CP, CP, CP);
  ctx.save(); ctx.filter = 'blur(1.1px)'; ctx.globalAlpha = 0.42; ctx.drawImage(sh, 1.4, 2.4); ctx.restore();
  for (let y = 0; y < m.h; y++) for (let x = 0; x < m.w; x++) if (has(x, y)) {           // dense underlay
    ctx.fillStyle = rgb(mul(col(m.cell[y * m.w + x]), 0.64)); ctx.fillRect(MP + x * CP + 0.6, MP + y * CP + 0.6, CP - 1.2, CP - 1.2);
  }
  for (let y = 0; y < m.h; y++) for (let x = 0; x < m.w; x++) if (has(x, y))
    ctx.drawImage(stitchSet(col(m.cell[y * m.w + x]))[hashInt(x, y, 77) % 3], MP + x * CP - SM, MP + y * CP - SM);
  const segs = [];
  for (let y = 0; y < m.h; y++) for (let x = 0; x < m.w; x++) {
    if (!has(x, y)) continue;
    const X0 = MP + x * CP, Y0 = MP + y * CP, X1 = X0 + CP, Y1 = Y0 + CP;
    if (!has(x, y - 1)) segs.push(X0, Y0, X1, Y0); if (!has(x, y + 1)) segs.push(X0, Y1, X1, Y1);
    if (!has(x - 1, y)) segs.push(X0, Y0, X0, Y1); if (!has(x + 1, y)) segs.push(X1, Y0, X1, Y1);
  }
  threadSegs(ctx, segs, col(m.outline), 2.2, 0.55);
  return c;
}
// feet at world (x, y): snap to whole cells, then draw at 0.4 units per sprite px
function drawActor(ctx, spr, cellsW, cellsH, x, y) {
  const gx = Math.round(x / C - cellsW / 2), gy = Math.round(y / C) - cellsH;
  ctx.drawImage(spr, gx * C - MP * K, gy * C - MP * K, spr.width * K, spr.height * K);
}
```

**4. Big stitched areas in a few fills** — merge cells into row runs per colour, fill with a seamless stitch pattern:

```js
// stitchPattern(code): 32x32 canvas, 4x4 stitches drawn with 9 wrap offsets so it tiles
function fillStitchRuns(ctx, cellsX, cellsY, keyAt, stitchPattern) {
  const paths = new Map();
  for (let j = 0; j < cellsY; j++) {
    let run = null, r0 = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i <= cellsX; i++) {
      const k = i < cellsX ? keyAt(i, j) : null;        // thread code or null (bare cloth)
      if (k === run) continue;
      if (run) { if (!paths.has(run)) paths.set(run, new Path2D()); paths.get(run).rect(r0 * C, j * C, (i - r0) * C, C); }
      run = k; r0 = i;
    }
  }
  for (const [k, p] of paths) {
    const pat = ctx.createPattern(stitchPattern(k), 'repeat');
    pat.setTransform(new DOMMatrix([K, 0, 0, K, 0, 0]));  // pattern px -> world units, aligned to the cell grid
    ctx.fillStyle = pat; ctx.fill(p);
  }
}
// meadow density: sparse, clustered by Bayer + hash
// stitched = bayer8(i, j) * 0.55 + hash2(i, j) * 0.45 < 0.03 + 0.24 * smoothstep(0.36, 0.78, fbm(x / 190, y / 190))
```

## Adapting it to your game

- **Keep fixed:** the 3.2-unit grid (or any fixed cell size ≈ 1/110 of screen height), the stitch construction (5 passes per stroke, 3 variants), dark backstitch outlines, blurred warm drop shadows, visible Aida holes, bare-fabric dominance, warm brown shadows, embroidery-only effect vocabulary, Grandstander + Mali.
- **May change:** the thread palette (swap the whole set to a winter, spring or sci-fi floss set — keep ramps of 3–4 and keep a dark outline thread), the fabric colour (white, black or navy Aida all work; recompute contrast so motifs still pop), ground materials (snow = sparse white crosses, sand = half stitches, lava = satin stitch in reds), actor designs.
- **New actors:** draw them as string grids; for round shapes use the lit-sphere quantiser (`l = −0.5nx − 0.55ny + 0.62nz` + Bayer jitter → pick thread from ramp). Make variants by thread remapping, not new art.
- **Other genres:** for platformers use a side view but keep the cell grid and snapping; for puzzle/board games let one stitch cell or a 4×4 block be the game tile; for card games make cards fabric tags with satin borders.
- **Other resolutions:** the look is resolution-independent because sprites are baked at 8 px per cell and drawn scaled with smoothing; for very large screens bake at 12–16 px per cell.

## Performance notes

- Bake at init: 3 stitch variants per thread (~45 threads → ~135 tiny canvases), seamless patterns for the ground colours, knots in 5 sizes, all actor frames (right, left, flash) and 5 spawn masks per actor, props, icons, digits, glows.
- `ctx.filter = 'blur()'` is only used during baking (motif shadows); never per frame.
- Ground chunks of 80×80 cells are built as generators within a ~5 ms per-frame budget; the per-colour run + pattern fill keeps a chunk at roughly a dozen `fill()` calls instead of up to 6400 `drawImage` calls. Noise per cell (warped fbm, path distance) is the main cost.
- Per frame: one `drawImage` per actor/prop, plus 1–2 additive glows per glowing object; hundreds of enemies are fine. Particles are cached sprites (thread curls are cached per colour × shape).
- The starter kit bakes its whole ground once per canvas size and draws a frame in well under 2 ms.

## Copy-paste prompt

```text
Build my game <X> in the "Cross-Stitch Sampler" style (miwale Game Style Library):
- The whole world is beige Aida cloth (#dccaa5) with a visible hole grid; Canvas 2D, procedural, no image assets.
- Everything drawn is embroidery on a fixed stitch grid: 1 cell = 3.2 world units (360 units = screen height), baked at 8 px per cell.
- Every cell is a real cross stitch: two diagonal thread strokes, each = warm shadow, dark underside (x0.7), top ply, white sheen line, twist ticks; 3 jittered variants per colour.
- Sprites are string grids of single-letter thread codes (hero 9x11 cells, small enemy ~7x8, brute ~15x17), outlined with a dark #2b1d1d backstitch (4-pass thread line that stops short of each hole), with a blurred warm-brown drop shadow.
- Use a DMC-like palette in ramps of 3-4 threads; never invent in-between colours; shadows are always rgba(40,22,10,a).
- Actors snap to whole cells; 3 animation frames that only change legs/crown/tail; spawn = stitched in row by row with a needle, death = unravel into loose curly threads + beads.
- Ground: bare linen paths with brown backstitch borders, sparse dithered green meadow stitches, dense rust forest, satin-stitch ponds, French-knot flowers, grass tufts; every region border is backstitched. Leave lots of bare fabric.
- Effects use embroidery materials only: French knots, glass beads (small pickups), sewing buttons (big pickups), sequins, running-stitch trails, dashed thread rings.
- Light from the upper left; warm additive candle glows; brown radial vignette.
- HUD: fabric tags with satin-stitch borders and dashed running-stitch lines, cross-stitch-tile bar fills, an embroidery-hoop timer; fonts Grandstander (numbers/titles) and Mali (text).
- Bake stitches, motifs and ground chunks once; fill large stitched areas with seamless stitch patterns.
```


---

<!-- style: popart · https://miwale.com/styles/library/popart/STYLE.md -->

# Pop-Art Comic — Game Art Style Spec

> A printed 1960s comic book come alive: brush-ink outlines, flat process colours, Ben-Day dots and slipped colour plates.

Everything on screen looks like cheap four-colour newsprint. Sprites are flat process colours with thick, slightly
lopsided black brush outlines; volume comes only from halftone dots (bigger dots = darker) in a crescent on the
shadow side plus a solid spot-black rim; a cyan or magenta colour plate peeks out from behind each figure because the
"printing press" is out of register. The ground is warm paper divided into big organic regions, each with its own
rotated dot screen and separated by inked contour lines. Kills explode into jagged yellow starbursts with POW!/ZONK!
balloons. The reference implementation is the game *Jack vs. the Turnip Ancestors* (pumpkin-head hero vs. turnip
hordes), but nothing in the technique is specific to it.

## At a glance

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Family | Comic · Pop-Art print |
| Mood | loud, playful, punchy, retro, spooky-fun |
| Best for | arena survivors, brawlers, top-down action with hordes, superhero/Halloween party games |
| Renderer | Canvas 2D, fully procedural, no image assets |
| Pixel art | No — native resolution, sprites baked at 3–5 px per world unit |
| Difficulty | 5/10 — every new object needs outline, dots and plate offset individually; the ground is expensive |
| Fonts | Bangers (shouts, numbers, titles), Comic Neue 700 (body text) |
| Key colours | ink `#1b1620`, paper `#f4ecd4`, yellow `#ffe23a`, red `#e8262c`, cyan `#2ec4ef`, magenta `#e0338f` |

## When to use it

Good fits:
- **Horde/arena games** — saturated actors on pale dotted paper stay readable even with 200 enemies on screen.
- **Action with lots of feedback** — hits, kills and level-ups map naturally to comic bursts and sound words.
- **Halloween, superhero, B-movie, pulp themes** — the 60s horror-comic print language is instantly recognisable.
- **UI-heavy games** (upgrade cards, shops) — comic panels with hard shadows make crisp, characterful UI.

Bad fits:
- **Atmospheric or realistic horror** — there are no soft lights, no darkness, no gradients.
- **Calm cozy games** — the style shouts; it is hard to make it quiet.
- **Strict retro pixel games** — this is vector-smooth with anti-aliasing, not a pixel grid.
- **Mostly-dark scenes** — paper is light by definition; a "night" region is pale blue paper with blue dots, not black.

## Color palette

| Swatch | Hex | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ink | `#1b1620` | All outlines, spot blacks, shadow dots, text strokes, panel frame (rgb 30,24,36 for ground ink) |
| Newsprint | `#f4ecd4` | Paper, panel gutter, UI bar backgrounds |
| Meadow paper | `#ede9c7` | Base ground (~50 %) under green dots `#68b062` |
| Autumn paper | `#fad880` | Field region under orange-red dots `#e8623e` |
| Night paper | `#c8d2e8` | Night region under blue dots `#5668b2` |
| Graveyard paper | `#e0d3de` | Graveyard region under violet dots `#8660a0` |
| Path paper | `#f9e9aa` | Paths: no dots, diagonal ink hatching along the edges |
| Process Yellow | `#ffe23a` | Bursts, glow dots, carved faces, clock panel, LEVEL UP |
| Process Red | `#e8262c` | HP bar, burst dots, sound-word text |
| Process Cyan | `#2ec4ef` | Misregistered plate, XP bar, gems, ghost eyes (dot sister `#1aa0d8`) |
| Process Magenta | `#e0338f` | Second plate, enemy dots, big gems |
| Pumpkin Orange | `#ff8a1c` | Hero head (shade dots `#e0301e`, rib lines `#d8561a`) |
| Cape Blue | `#2c6ad0` | Hero cape and sleeves (dots `#0f2f80`) |
| Scarf Red | `#ea2a33` | Hero scarf (dots `#8a0c22`) |
| Pants | `#2b2846` | Hero legs (back leg `#1f1c36`), glove `#fffaf0` |
| Leaf Green | `#3fae49` | Leaf crowns (dots `#1a6a2c`), stems `#4c8a2a` |
| Turnip Magenta | `#d4308c` | Small enemy A top (cyan dots, shade `#5a0c48`), bottom `#fdeabb` with `#f08a3c` dots |
| Turnip Violet | `#8a3cc0` | Small enemy B top (magenta dots, shade `#2a0a50`), bottom `#f8e6a6` |
| Ghost White | `#fcfbf4` | Ghost body, dust puffs (shade dots `#1aa0d8`) |
| Brute Plum / Clay | `#8a3a86` / `#c98545` | Brute top / bottom, shade `#3a1030`, limbs `#9a5a30` |
| Flash Yellow | `#ffe94a` | Hit/impact frame fill with `#ff7a1a` shade dots |

Palette rules:
- Every fill has a **darker dot sister** used only for halftone shade. Never shade by darkening the fill.
- Black is always warm ink `#1b1620`, never `#000`.
- Ground = pale paper tints with mid-saturation dots. Actors = full-saturation process colours. This value gap is
  what keeps hordes readable.
- Plates are only cyan `#2ec4ef` (solid actors, bursts) or magenta `#e0338f` (ghosts, gems, projectiles) at 60–65 %
  alpha; props use pink `#ff3d6e` at 45 %.
- Complementary dot overlays: cyan dots on magenta, magenta on violet, yellow on magenta, red on yellow.
- No gradients, no blur, no glow — tone is dot size or dot density.

## Typography

**Bangers** 400 — https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Bangers — sound words, damage numbers, HUD numbers, titles, card
names. Fallback stack: `"Bangers", "Luckiest Guy", Impact, "Arial Black", sans-serif` (use bold when falling back).

```css
.clock-time { font: 400 38px/1 'Bangers', Impact, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 2px; color: #1b1620; text-shadow: 2px 2px 0 #e8262c; }
.lu-title   { font: 400 92px/1 'Bangers', Impact, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 4px; color: #ffe23a; transform: rotate(-4deg); }
```

**Comic Neue** 700 — https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Comic+Neue — labels, descriptions, hints; often uppercase with
1 px letter-spacing.

```css
.hint { font: 700 16px/1.25 'Comic Neue', 'Comic Sans MS', sans-serif; letter-spacing: 1px; text-transform: uppercase; color: #1b1620; }
```

Text effects:
- **Ink outline in CSS**: 16 hard `text-shadow`s around a circle (`cos/sin × w px, 0 blur, #1b1620`) plus one drop
  shadow `8px 8px 0 #1b1620` for big titles (w = 4 for titles, 2 for HP text, 1.5 for small labels).
- **On canvas**: draw a colour-plate copy offset (−0.7, +0.6) units at 85 % alpha (magenta, or cyan for crits), then
  `strokeText` with lineWidth = 0.22 × font size in ink, then `fillText` in white/yellow.
- **Crit numbers**: yellow fill with red halftone dots clipped to the lower half of the letters (`source-atop`).
- **Sound words** get a hard drop shadow of ink offset (+0.9, +0.9) units before the stroke.

## Rendering technique

1. **Choose bake resolution** `K = clamp(round(screenHeightPx / 360 × 1.4), 3, 5)` pixels per world unit. The camera
   shows 360 world units vertically.
2. **Bake every sprite** once with the *part painter* (see Code). For each part, in order:
   1. `clip()` to the part shape;
   2. flat fill (or a two-tone fill function);
   3. optional Ben-Day overlay `dots: [colour, rf, spacing, rotationDeg]` across the whole part;
   4. **shade crescent**: clip to "everything minus the shape shifted by `sh`" (even-odd) and fill with dots in the
      dark sister colour (`rf` 0.45–0.62). `sh` points toward the light (negative x/y), so the crescent appears on the
      bottom-right;
   5. **spot-black crescent**: same trick with a smaller offset `spot` (≈ 40 % of `sh`), filled solid ink;
   6. details (ribs, patterns) and white shine ellipses at top-left;
   7. `restore()` and stroke the outline **twice**: width `w`, then `0.85 w` translated by (`0.3 w`, `0.36 w`). The
      result is a brush line that swells on the bottom-right.
   8. optional interior ink lines at `0.55 × ol` (≈ 0.55 units).
3. **Halftone tile**: a T×T canvas (T = round(spacing × K), min 3 px) with circles at the 4 corners and the centre
   (a 45° diamond lattice), radius = `rf × T / 2`; used as a repeating pattern with
   `pattern.setTransform(DOMMatrix().rotate(deg).scale(1/K))` so the dots live in world units. Sprite dot spacing is
   1.3 units (`DSP`).
4. **Misregistration**: after painting, tint a silhouette copy of the sprite with the plate colour and draw it
   `destination-over` at alpha 0.65, offset (−0.5 K, +0.375 K) px — i.e. 0.5 units left, 0.375 down.
5. **Variants per actor**: 4 animation frames × {normal, flash} × {right, left (mirrored canvas)}. The flash frame is
   painted with the same code but every fill becomes `#ffe94a` and shade dots `#ff7a1a`, dots/details are skipped.
6. **Per frame**: ground chunks (cached) → ground overlay (spawn bursts, hero glow) → pickups → shadows → y-sorted
   props/enemies/hero → orbitals → projectiles → particles → numbers → screen overlay (vignette dots + panel frame).
   Everything except the ground is `drawImage` of baked canvases with scale/rotation.
7. Sprites are drawn with smoothing on (the style is anti-aliased vector print, not pixel art).

## Background and ground

The floor is computed **per pixel** in world space so dots never swim or seam between chunks (256-unit chunks, at most
2.5 px/unit):

- **Region fields**: four domain-warped fBm fields (warp: Perlin at 1/900 × 110 units; field scales 1/1000, 1/1250,
  1/820) minus thresholds (0.55, 0.635, 0.625) decide autumn, night and graveyard regions; a fourth field
  `(0.02 − |perlin(x/1500)|) × 3.2` makes winding paths. The topmost positive layer wins (path > graveyard > night >
  autumn > meadow).
- **Grid + signed distance**: fields are sampled on a 4-unit grid and bilinearly interpolated; the bilinear gradient
  gives a signed distance `field / |∇field|`. Cells far inside/outside are flagged so most pixels skip the work.
- **Ink contours**: ink coverage `(hw − |dist|) × res + 0.5`, clamped 0..1, where half-width `hw = 0.42 + 0.62 ×
  noise(x/36)` — a 0.84–2.08-unit brush line that thickens and thins.
- **Dot screens** (one per material, multiply-blended into the paper colour):

| Region | Paper rgb | Dot ink rgb | Spacing | Angle | Radius (× spacing) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Meadow | 237,233,199 | 104,176,98 | 3.3 | 45° | 0.17–0.33 |
| Autumn | 250,216,128 | 232,98,62 | 3.0 | 15° | 0.15–0.31 |
| Night | 200,210,232 | 86,104,178 | 3.0 | 45° | 0.22–0.36 |
| Graveyard | 224,211,222 | 134,96,160 | 2.8 | 60° | 0.20–0.36 |
| Path | 249,233,170 | — | — | — | hatching |

  Dot radius is interpolated by a tone field `0.5 + perlin(x/240)·0.42 + perlin(x/1300)·0.3`, so the print gets
  denser and lighter in patches like a worn screen. Coverage is anti-aliased: `(radius − d) × res + 0.5`.
- **Path hatching**: within 14 units of a path edge, diagonal lines `(x − y)·0.7071 / 1.7` of half-width
  `0.34 × taper` that fade over a noise-varying length 1.5–10.5 units — the comic "speed hatching" along a road.
- **Paper**: × yellowing `1 ± 0.04` (noise/1700), × grain `0.985 + (hash − 0.5)·0.045 + fibre·0.025`.
- **Decals** (scatter every ~15 units, skipped within 5 units of a region edge): meadow — 3-blade ink grass tufts
  (30 %), 5-petal white/pink flowers with yellow centre (6 %); autumn — red/yellow leaves, stubble strokes; night —
  white 4-point glints; graveyard — branching cracks, pebbles; path — pebbles with a black crescent, ink specks;
  1.5 % rare ink splats anywhere.

## Characters

The hero (reference: pumpkin-head boy) is ~21 × 34 units at 1.12× scale, feet at y = 0:

- **Head**: superellipse pumpkin (`|cos|^0.85`, `|sin|^0.92`, dented 15 % at the top, 7 % at the bottom) centred at
  (0.4, −22.6), rx 8.4, ry 6.9, orange `#ff8a1c`, outline 1.15, shade crescent `[-2.3, -1.9]` with `#e0301e` dots
  rf 0.55, spot `[-0.85, -0.75]`, four curved rib lines `#d8561a` 0.55 wide, two white shine ellipses top-left.
  Green stem capsule. Face = carved triangles and a zig-zag grin: black hole, yellow `#ffe23a` interior shifted
  (+0.3, +0.55) inside, leaving a black rim on the top-left.
- **Body**: blue cape quad-curve shape (shade `[1.7, -1.3]`, spot `[0.75, -0.55]`, two fold lines 0.5), red scarf knot
  ellipse and a waving scarf tail polygon behind everything.
- **Limbs**: capsules (`CAP`) — legs r 1.35 in `#2b2846` (back leg darker `#1f1c36`), black ellipse shoes with a
  white shine; arms r 1.25 in cape blue with Ben-Day overlay, white glove ellipses with cyan-dot shade.
- **Paint order**: scarf tail → back leg → back arm → front leg → cape → front arm → scarf knot → stem → head → face.
- **Frames**: 0 idle, 1 contact A, 2 passing (front foot lifted 1.9), 3 contact B; each frame is a row of numbers
  (back foot x/y, front foot x/y, back/front arm angle, cape flare). Cape flare also swings the hem and scarf tail.
- **Facing**: bake once facing right, mirror the canvas for left (the face is offset +1.4 units toward the facing).
- **Plate**: cyan behind the hero.

## Enemies and props

All actors use the same painter so they share outline weight, dot spacing and light direction. Readability with large
hordes comes from: saturated colours vs. pale ground, distinct silhouettes per type, big yellow eyes, the cyan
fringe separating overlapping sprites, and the halftone shadow anchoring each one.

- **Small melee enemy** (turnip, ~17 × 28 units at 0.92×): teardrop turnip body (bezier, top −20.6, bottom −2.6,
  half-width 8.5), *two-tone*: magenta/violet top with complementary dots (rf 0.42) above a wavy ink line at y −12.2
  (amplitude 0.9), cream bottom with sparse orange dots (rf 0.22, rotated 30°). Three dotted leaves on top, stubby
  capsule legs. Face: yellow eye ellipses with ink pupils, angular ink brows, ink frown with a pink tongue and white
  fangs. Two colour variants chosen by seed.
- **Fast/floating enemy** (ghost, ~25 × 26): white sheet with a 7-unit dome and a wavy tail whose control points move
  with frame phase; strong cyan-dot shade `[-2.6, -1.6]` rf 0.62; cyan dots over the bottom 12 units; the bottom 28 %
  is erased with a `destination-out` gradient to 75 % so it hovers. Ink oval eyes with cyan catchlights, gaping
  ink mouth. Magenta plate (not cyan) so it reads as a different "ink".
- **Brute** (colossus, ~48 × 66): giant turnip (half-width 17.8, outline 1.45), plum top/clay bottom, five dark
  leaves, capsule arms r 3.0 with blob fists, zig-zag crack lines, a yellow star-shaped glowing core in the chest with
  ink rays, angular glowing eyes and a mouth with yellow teeth. Plays slower, has a smaller hit-flash cap (0.6).
- **Pickups**: cyan teardrop gem (big: magenta 5-point star with yellow dots), bobbing ±1 unit above a tiny dot shadow;
  magenta plate.
- **Props**: trees (circle-union crown, green or orange, hatched leaf strokes, sway via skew ±0.02), dead trees,
  berry bushes, rocks, wooden fences/signs, pumpkins (one lit), scarecrow with red/blue-dot shirt, hay bales,
  gravestones. Circle unions are converted to **one** polygon (ray-cast outline, 144 samples) so the even-odd shade
  crescent works. Props use a pink `#ff3d6e` plate at 45 % — weaker than actors, so actors pop.

## Effects and particles

- **Hit impact** (0.16 s): 8-point yellow star r 6.5/2.4 with red dots and a white inner star, scale 0.5 → 1.2 → 0.3;
  45 % chance of 7 black tapered speed-line wedges radiating from r 4.5 outward. Enemy overdrawn with its flash frame.
- **Kill burst** (0.34 s, brute 0.5 s ×1.9): 12-point jagged star r 10/5.6 in yellow/white/orange/yellow with red,
  cyan, dark-red or purple dot rings; pops with outBack in the first 16 %, grows +35 %/life, fades last 40 %.
- **Chunks**: 4 (small), 2 (ghost), 9 (brute) five-sided polygons in the enemy's colours with spot-black crescent,
  thrown with gravity 280; plus 2–6 ink droplets (ghosts: cyan).
- **Sound words**: POW! ZACK! KRACH! PENG! ZONK! PLOPP! for normal kills (30 %, ≥ 1.3 s apart), bigger WUMMS!/RUMMS!
  for brutes (always) with a 16-wedge ring shockwave, AUTSCH! when the hero is hurt (≥ 2.2 s apart). Max 3 alive.
  Colour sets `[fill, text, plate]`: yellow/red/orange-dot, red/yellow/dark-red, cyan/white/dark-blue, white/red/cyan.
- **Damage numbers**: see Typography; scale 0.3 → 1.35 → 1.0 over the first 24 % of life, random tilt ±0.15 rad.
- **Dash**: cyan and magenta silhouettes at 6 and 12 units behind, 60 % alpha, plus 4 ink speed lines; 3 white puffs.
- **Footstep / shot puffs**: white circle-union cloud with cyan-dot shade, outBack pop, quadratic shrink.
- **Level-up**: yellow ring of 16 wedges + 8 white 4-point twinkles with cyan shade flying out.
- **Spawn**: flattened yellow star with red dots and a black hole on the ground; enemy grows with outElastic; ink
  droplets fly out.

## Lighting, shadows and post-processing

- **Light** is always top-left; it exists only as crescent placement and white shine ellipses.
- **Contact shadows** are two concentric ellipses of ink dots (outer 9.6 × 3.5 units, rf 0.5, spacing 1.15; inner
  6.4 × 2.3, rf 0.95), drawn at 55 % alpha (hero 65 %, ghost 35 %) and scaled per type (brute 19, small 8.4, ghost 6).
- **Hero light**: a hex grid of yellow `#ffe23a` dots (spacing 1.6) within radius 15, dot radius `(1 − d)^0.7 × 0.88`,
  squashed to 1.5 × 0.62 on the floor at 80 % alpha. Orbiting lanterns get the same glow at 0.8 × flickering alpha.
- **No blur, no bloom, no colour grading.**
- **Screen overlay** (baked once per resolution): a hex grid of ink dots (spacing max(7, H/100) px) whose radius grows
  with `smoothstep(0.9, 1.42, distance from centre)` at 42 % alpha — a halftone vignette; a paper gutter of
  max(4, 0.6 % H) px; and a black panel frame of the same width drawn as jittered 24-segment strokes (width
  ×0.9–1.2) so it looks hand-inked. Only tiles that contain pixels are blitted.

## UI and HUD

Comic panels: zero radius, 3 px ink borders, **solid offset shadows** (4–8 px, no blur), slight rotations (±1–4°),
skewed bars, dotted fills via `radial-gradient` patterns. Kill counter is a white oval speech bubble with a tail;
level-up title sits in a 16-point red starburst with yellow dots; upgrade cards are cream with dotted colour headers
(cyan, yellow, pink), rotated −1.5°/1°/−0.5° and popping in with an overshoot cubic-bezier. Icons are painted with the
same part painter on a 48-unit grid (outline 2.4, dot spacing 3.6) with a 1.4 px misregistered plate.

```css
.hud-panel { background: #ffe23a; border: 3px solid #1b1620; border-radius: 0; box-shadow: 5px 5px 0 #1b1620;
  padding: 4px 18px 5px; transform: rotate(-1deg); font-family: 'Bangers', Impact, sans-serif; font-size: 38px;
  letter-spacing: 2px; color: #1b1620; text-shadow: 2px 2px 0 #e8262c; }
.hp-bar { width: 250px; height: 28px; overflow: hidden; transform: skewX(-10deg);
  background: radial-gradient(circle, rgba(27,22,32,.22) 1.1px, transparent 1.6px) 0 0/6px 6px, #f4ecd4;
  border: 3px solid #1b1620; border-radius: 0; box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 #1b1620; }
.hp-fill { height: 100%; border-right: 3px solid #1b1620;
  background: radial-gradient(circle, #8a0c22 1.8px, transparent 2.3px) 0 0/6px 6px, #e8262c; }
.xp-fill { height: 100%; border-right: 3px solid #1b1620;
  background: radial-gradient(circle, #1474b8 1.7px, transparent 2.2px) 0 0/6px 6px, #2ec4ef; }
.kills { padding: 4px 26px 4px 12px; background: #fff; border: 3px solid #1b1620; border-radius: 50%;
  box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 #1b1620; font: 400 30px 'Bangers', Impact, sans-serif; }
.card { background: #fbf5e2; border: 4px solid #1b1620; box-shadow: 8px 8px 0 #1b1620; transform: rotate(-1.5deg);
  animation: popCard .45s cubic-bezier(.3,1.5,.5,1) backwards; }
@keyframes popCard { from { transform: translateY(70px) scale(.6) rotate(8deg); opacity: 0; } }
.hurt .hp { animation: popShake .22s steps(3) 1; }
@keyframes popShake { 33% { transform: translate(-4px,2px) rotate(-1.5deg) } 66% { transform: translate(4px,-2px) rotate(1.5deg) } }
```

Overlays: level-up backdrop = radial dark vignette + red dots (2.2 px / 11 px) + yellow sunburst
`repeating-conic-gradient` (7° rays at 15 %) over `rgba(27,22,32,.62)`; game-over = ink dots over dark red.

## Motion and animation

- **Hero walk**: frame sequence 1, 2, 3, 2 at `anim × 0.4`; lift `sin(f·π) × 1.8` units, tilt `0.05 × facing ×
  sin(f·π)`; a dust puff on every other step (50 %).
- **Hero idle**: `sy = 1 + 0.025 sin(3.2t)`, `sx = 1 − 0.018 sin(3.2t)`. Shooting squashes 5 %; level-up wobbles
  `sin(levelT·4π)` ±16 %; hurt overlays the yellow flash and squashes 14/12 %. I-frames blink at 16 Hz to 45 % alpha.
- **Small enemy**: 4 frames at `anim × 0.85`, rotation `sin × 0.09`, hop 1.2 units, 5 % squash at contact, random
  scale 0.94–1.06.
- **Ghost**: 4 tail frames at 7 fps, hover 4.5 units up, bob ±1.6 at 2.6 rad/s, lean `vx/64 × 0.14`, alpha 0.94.
- **Brute**: 4 frames at `anim × 0.32`, contact squash `(1 − up)^3 × 7 %`, rotation ±0.03, hop 2 units.
- **Spawn**: solid enemies grow vertically with outElastic (width compensates `1/√p`), ghosts fade + outBack.
- **Hit**: flash frame alpha `min(cap, flash × 1.4)`, squash sx +18 %, sy −14 %.
- **Death**: 0–0.2 s inflate to 1.25× in the yellow frame (outQuad), 0.2–0.42 s shrink to 0 (inQuad) while rotating
  +0.6 rad; the kill burst covers it.
- **Pops everywhere use overshoot** (outBack, outElastic, CSS `cubic-bezier(.3,1.8,.5,1)`).

## Do and don't

Do:
- Route every shape through one part painter (fill → dots → shade crescent → spot black → double outline).
- Bake sprites once: 4 frames × normal/flash × both facings; blit at runtime.
- Shade with dot size in the colour's darker sister; keep the light top-left.
- Slip a cyan/magenta plate 0.5 units behind every sprite.
- Keep actors saturated and the ground pale.
- Use jagged star balloons + Bangers for loud events, rate-limited to 3 on screen.
- Give every UI panel a hard offset ink shadow and zero radius.

Don't:
- Use gradients, `shadowBlur`, filters or soft glows.
- Use pure `#000` or hairline outlines (< 0.4 units).
- Give two ground regions the same dot angle and spacing.
- Spam sound words — more than 3 turns into noise.
- Let enemies share the dominant colour of the ground region they walk on.
- Round UI corners or use translucent glass panels.
- Compute halftone per frame for sprites.

## Implementation recipe

1. Set up a camera that shows 360 world units vertically; compute `S = screenPx / 360` and `K = clamp(round(S × 1.4), 3, 5)`.
2. Copy the palette; for every new colour define a darker dot sister.
3. Implement `dotPattern(colour, rf, T)` (cached diamond-lattice tile) and the `Painter` with `dots`, `crescent`,
   `part`, `detail` (see Code / `starter.js`).
4. Implement shape helpers: ellipse `E`, capsule `CAP`, polygon `POLY`, bezier blob, circle union → polygon, star
   points with seeded jitter, plus any signature shapes (pumpkin superellipse, turnip bezier).
5. Model each actor as a function `parts(P, frame)` painting back-to-front. Store walk poses as small number tables.
6. `build(box, fn, mode, plate)` each frame into a canvas at K px/unit with 1.9 units margin, then add the plate
   silhouette `destination-over` at 65 % alpha offset (−0.5, +0.375) units. Build `mode = 'flash'` too. Mirror for
   left-facing.
7. Bake shadows (two dot ellipses), the hero glow (hex dot grid), bursts, impact star, chunks, puffs, twinkles.
8. Ground: noise fields on a 4-unit grid → bilinear signed distance → per-pixel region, ink contour of varying
   half-width, one rotated AA dot screen per region, grain, path hatching; render in chunks (generator/worker); then
   scatter ink decals.
9. Per frame: ground → spawn bursts + glow → pickups → shadows → y-sorted actors/props → projectiles → particles →
   numbers → baked screen overlay.
10. Hook game events: hit → impact + flash; kill → burst + chunks + ink + maybe a sound word; dash → plate smear.
11. Build the HUD in HTML/CSS with the panel rules above, fonts Bangers + Comic Neue 700.
12. Check readability with 200 enemies: if they mush together, raise saturation contrast to the floor, not outline width.

## Code

The core techniques, standalone. A complete runnable kit (hero, small enemy, ground, overlay, bursts, sound words) is
in [`starter.js`](starter.js); the full reference module is [`../../js/styles/popart.js`](../../js/styles/popart.js).

**1. Halftone tile + part painter** (the heart of the style):

```js
const INK = '#1b1620', TAU = Math.PI * 2;
const PAT = new Map();
function dotPattern(ctx, col, rf, T) {           // T px tile, dots at corners + centre (45° lattice)
  const key = col + '|' + rf + '|' + T;
  if (PAT.has(key)) return PAT.get(key);
  const cv = document.createElement('canvas'); cv.width = cv.height = T;
  const c = cv.getContext('2d'), r = rf * T * 0.5;
  c.fillStyle = col; c.beginPath();
  for (const q of [[0, 0], [T, 0], [0, T], [T, T], [T / 2, T / 2]]) { c.moveTo(q[0] + r, q[1]); c.arc(q[0], q[1], r, 0, TAU); }
  c.fill();
  const p = ctx.createPattern(cv, 'repeat'); PAT.set(key, p); return p;
}
function Painter(c, k) { this.c = c; this.k = k; this.ol = 1.0; this.dsp = 1.3; }
Painter.prototype.dots = function (col, rf, sp, rot) {
  const T = Math.max(3, Math.round((sp || this.dsp) * this.k)), p = dotPattern(this.c, col, rf, T);
  let m = new DOMMatrix(); if (rot) m = m.rotate(rot);
  p.setTransform(m.scale(1 / this.k));            // dots measured in world units
  this.c.fillStyle = p; this.c.fillRect(-999, -999, 1999, 1999);
};
Painter.prototype.crescent = function (shape, sh, fn) { // area of shape NOT covered by shape shifted by sh
  const c = this.c; c.save(); c.beginPath(); c.rect(-999, -999, 1999, 1999);
  c.translate(sh[0], sh[1]); shape(c); c.translate(-sh[0], -sh[1]); c.clip('evenodd'); fn(); c.restore();
};
Painter.prototype.part = function (shape, fill, o = {}) {
  const c = this.c;
  c.save(); c.beginPath(); shape(c); c.clip();
  c.fillStyle = fill; c.fillRect(-999, -999, 1999, 1999);
  if (o.dots) this.dots(...o.dots);
  if (o.sh) this.crescent(shape, o.sh, () => this.dots(...(o.shade || [INK, 0.45])));
  if (o.spot) this.crescent(shape, o.spot, () => { c.fillStyle = INK; c.fillRect(-999, -999, 1999, 1999); });
  if (o.hi) { c.fillStyle = '#fff'; for (const h of o.hi) { c.beginPath(); c.ellipse(h[0], h[1], h[2], h[3], h[4] || 0, 0, TAU); c.fill(); } }
  c.restore();
  const w = o.ol != null ? o.ol : this.ol;      // brush outline: heavier bottom-right
  c.strokeStyle = INK; c.lineWidth = w; c.beginPath(); shape(c); c.stroke();
  c.save(); c.translate(w * 0.3, w * 0.36); c.lineWidth = w * 0.85; c.beginPath(); shape(c); c.stroke(); c.restore();
};
// usage (world units, light top-left):
// P.part(E(0,-22.6,8.4,6.9), '#ff8a1c', { ol: 1.15, sh: [-2.3,-1.9], shade: ['#e0301e', 0.55], spot: [-0.85,-0.75], hi: [[-4,-26.2,2.1,0.85,-0.6]] });
```

**2. Bake with a misregistered colour plate:**

```js
function bakeSprite(box, paint, K, plate) {      // box = [l, t, r, b] in world units, feet at y = 0
  const m = 1.9, l = box[0] - m, t = box[1] - m;
  const cv = document.createElement('canvas');
  cv.width = Math.ceil((box[2] + m - l) * K); cv.height = Math.ceil((box[3] + m - t) * K);
  const ctx = cv.getContext('2d');
  ctx.scale(K, K); ctx.translate(-l, -t); ctx.lineJoin = ctx.lineCap = 'round';
  paint(new Painter(ctx, K));
  if (plate) {
    const tn = document.createElement('canvas'); tn.width = cv.width; tn.height = cv.height;
    const tc = tn.getContext('2d'); tc.drawImage(cv, 0, 0);
    tc.globalCompositeOperation = 'source-atop'; tc.fillStyle = plate; tc.fillRect(0, 0, tn.width, tn.height);
    ctx.setTransform(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0);
    ctx.globalCompositeOperation = 'destination-over'; ctx.globalAlpha = 0.65;
    ctx.drawImage(tn, -0.5 * K, 0.375 * K);       // plate slips 0.5 units left, 0.375 down
  }
  return { c: cv, ox: -l * K, oy: -t * K };       // draw at (x - ox/K, y - oy/K), size / K
}
```

**3. Ground pixel: rotated anti-aliased dot screen + brush contour:**

```js
// x, y world units; res = px per unit; tone 0..1; dist = signed distance to region edge (units); lw = noise 0..1
function groundPixel(x, y, res, paper, scr, tone, dist, lw) {
  let r = paper[0], g = paper[1], b = paper[2];
  if (scr) {
    const ca = Math.cos(scr.a), sa = Math.sin(scr.a);
    const su = (x * ca + y * sa) / scr.sp, sv = (y * ca - x * sa) / scr.sp;
    const fu = su - Math.floor(su) - 0.5, fv = sv - Math.floor(sv) - 0.5;
    const d = Math.hypot(fu, fv) * scr.sp, rad = scr.sp * (scr.r0 + (scr.r1 - scr.r0) * tone);
    const cov = Math.min(1, (rad - d) * res + 0.5);                 // 1-pixel AA edge
    if (cov > 0) { r *= 1 - cov * (1 - scr.ink[0] / 255); g *= 1 - cov * (1 - scr.ink[1] / 255); b *= 1 - cov * (1 - scr.ink[2] / 255); }
  }
  const hw = 0.42 + 0.62 * lw;                                      // contour half-width 0.42..1.04
  const ink = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (hw - Math.abs(dist)) * res + 0.5));
  return [r + (30 - r) * ink, g + (24 - g) * ink, b + (36 - b) * ink];
}
// meadow: groundPixel(x, y, 2.5, [237,233,199], { ink: [104,176,98], sp: 3.3, a: 0.785, r0: 0.17, r1: 0.33 }, tone, dist, lw)
```

**4. Halftone contact shadow and dot glow (no blur anywhere):**

```js
function bakeShadow(P) {                          // paint into a Painter-backed canvas, box [-10,-4,10,4]
  const c = P.c;
  c.save(); c.beginPath(); c.ellipse(0, 0, 9.6, 3.5, 0, 0, TAU); c.clip(); P.dots(INK, 0.5, 1.15); c.restore();
  c.save(); c.beginPath(); c.ellipse(0, 0, 6.4, 2.3, 0, 0, TAU); c.clip(); P.dots(INK, 0.95, 1.15); c.restore();
}
function bakeGlow(c) {                            // box [-16,-16,16,16]; draw at 1.5 x 0.62 under the hero, alpha 0.8
  const sp = 1.6; c.fillStyle = '#ffe23a'; c.beginPath();
  for (let j = -10; j <= 10; j++) for (let i = -10; i <= 10; i++) {
    const x = i * sp + (j & 1 ? sp / 2 : 0), y = j * sp * 0.866, d = Math.hypot(x, y) / 15;
    if (d >= 1) continue;
    const r = Math.pow(1 - d, 0.7) * sp * 0.55; c.moveTo(x + r, y); c.arc(x, y, r, 0, TAU);
  }
  c.fill();
}
```

## Adapting it to your game

Keep fixed: the painter pipeline and its order, ink `#1b1620`, outline ~1 unit with the doubled offset stroke, top-left
light, dot spacing ~1.3 units on sprites and ~3 units on the ground, misregistered cyan/magenta plates, no blur, comic
bursts + Bangers, hard-shadow UI.

May change:
- **Palette**: swap process colours freely, but each new fill needs a darker dot sister and must stay more saturated
  than the floor. Keep plates to two colours (cyan + magenta or a pair from your palette).
- **Theme**: sci-fi → chrome blue robots with cyan-dot shade and a magenta plate; western → leather browns with red
  dot overlays. The ground regions become desert/rock/water with their own screen angles.
- **New actors**: build from ellipses/capsules/polygons, give each type its own silhouette and dominant colour, carved
  or ink faces with big yellow eyes. Bosses: thicker outline (1.4–1.6) and a glowing core detail.
- **Genres**: side-scrollers work well (keep the shade on the bottom-right); for platformers, turn region fields into
  horizontal bands and keep the contour lines.
- **Resolution**: everything is in world units; only K changes. At very low resolutions raise dot spacing so dots stay
  ≥ 3 px.
- **Sound words**: localise the word lists; keep them short, uppercase, with "!".

## Performance notes

- Bake cost: ~40 actor canvases (4 frames × 2 modes × 2 facings per type) plus props and FX at 3–5 px/unit — a few
  hundred ms once at start. Runtime per actor is one `drawImage` (+1 for the flash), so 300+ enemies are fine.
- The ground is the hot spot: up to 4 region distances, a rotated dot screen, grain and hatching per pixel. Mitigations
  used by the reference: 4-unit noise grid with bilinear interpolation, per-cell "deep inside / far outside" flags that
  skip distance work, 256-unit chunks rendered as a generator yielding every 2 rows, resolution capped at 2.5 px/unit,
  `putImageData` in 128-row strips.
- Text sprites (numbers, sound words) are cached by value and colour; clear the cache above ~600 entries. Rebuild
  them once the web font has loaded (check `document.fonts` every 0.5 s).
- The screen overlay is baked once per resolution and only non-empty tiles are redrawn.
- `starter.js` bakes the ground once per canvas size and then draws a frame in well under 1 ms.

## Copy-paste prompt

```text
Build my game <X> in the "Pop-Art Comic" style (1960s printed comic book):
- Canvas 2D, procedural, no images. Camera shows 360 world units vertically; bake sprites at 3–5 px per unit.
- Paint every shape with one part painter: clip -> flat process colour -> optional Ben-Day dots -> halftone shade
  crescent (shape minus itself shifted toward the top-left light, filled with darker-sister dots) -> smaller solid
  black crescent -> white shine ellipses -> ink outline #1b1620 ~1 unit stroked twice (2nd at 0.85 width shifted +0.3,+0.36).
- Dots live in world units: diamond-lattice pattern, spacing 1.3 on sprites, radius factor 0.3–0.62.
- Behind every sprite draw a cyan #2ec4ef (or magenta #e0338f) silhouette at 65 % alpha offset 0.5 units left/0.375 down.
- Bake 4 walk frames + a yellow #ffe94a flash frame, both facings; runtime = drawImage only.
- Ground: pale newsprint regions (meadow #ede9c7 + green dots, autumn #fad880 + red dots, etc.), each with its own
  rotated anti-aliased dot screen whose dot size follows a tone noise, separated by brush ink contours 0.8–2 units wide.
- Shadows = ellipses of ink dots; glows = grids of yellow dots. No gradients, no blur, no #000.
- Saturated actors on pale ground; distinct silhouette + colour per enemy type; big yellow eyes.
- Kills: jagged 12-point yellow star with red dot rings + flying chunks + ink drops; sometimes a POW!/ZONK! balloon
  (Bangers, ink stroke, offset plate), max 3 on screen.
- HUD: Bangers + Comic Neue 700, zero-radius panels, 3 px ink borders, hard 4–8 px offset shadows, skewed dotted bars.
- Screen: ink-dot vignette in the corners and a hand-inked black panel frame around the view.
```
