<!-- style: vangogh · https://miwale.com/styles/library/vangogh/STYLE.md -->

# Starry Night — Game Art Style Spec

> A living Van Gogh night painting: every surface is thick, swirling impasto brush strokes in ultramarine, viridian and cadmium yellow.

The whole game looks like a freshly painted post-impressionist canvas at night (think *The Starry Night* and *Café Terrace at Night*). Meadows, wheat fields, paths and ponds are made of thousands of short, thick, directional dabs that follow swirling flow fields; characters are painted stroke by stroke with dark prussian-blue contours; every light source radiates concentric rings of glowing yellow strokes. The HUD is a museum: gilded frames, brush-stroke bars and little framed paintings as cards. The reference implementation is the game *Jack vs. the Turnip Ancestors* (a top-down survivor game: pumpkin-headed hero, turnip enemies, orbiting lanterns, seed projectiles) — use it as an example, not as a template.

## At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Family | Traditional media · Impasto oil painting |
| Mood | dreamy, vibrant, nocturnal, restless, artful |
| Best for | top-down action / survivor games, atmospheric adventure, art/museum themes, night exploration |
| Renderer | Canvas 2D, fully procedural, no image assets |
| Pixel art | No – smooth, native resolution; sprites baked at 3 px per world unit |
| Difficulty | 8/10 – every asset is built from many brush strokes; readability against the moving ground is hard |
| Fonts | Cinzel (600/800), Caveat Brush (400), Alegreya italic (500) |
| Key colours | `#141c30` night under-painting, `#2e5944` viridian meadow, `#866c2a` wheat ochre, `#3d4180` violet path, `#26409a` ultramarine, `#ffd040` cadmium, `#fff6c8` star white, `#111733` prussian contour |

## When to use it

- **Good fits:** top-down games with a free-roaming camera (the infinite painted landscape shines), atmospheric night adventures, art-themed games, slow to mid-paced action where the player has time to enjoy the canvas.
- **Works with care:** survivor-style hordes – at 100+ enemies the screen becomes a carpet of strokes; strong contours and ground-contrasting enemy colours are mandatory.
- **Bad fits:** competitive shooters and precision platformers (stroke-broken silhouettes blur hitboxes), UI-heavy strategy (the busy ground fights with dense UI), games that need hundreds of distinct tiny units, very low-end devices (long bake times).
- **Why:** the look comes from visual *texture density*. Everything is busy by design; gameplay must tolerate a high-frequency background.

## Color palette

| Swatch | Hex | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Night under-painting | `#141c30` | Clear colour, dark base behind ground strokes |
| Prussian contour | `#111733` | Outline strokes of hero and many props |
| Meadow viridian | `#2e5944` | Meadow mid tone – the dominant ground colour |
| Meadow light | `#70944e` | Brightest meadow strokes |
| Forest black-green | `#142a20` | Forest / dark grass |
| Wheat ochre | `#866c2a` | Wheat field mid tone |
| Wheat light | `#bc9a3e` | Brightest wheat strokes |
| Path violet | `#3d4180` | Roads and paths |
| Pond blue | `#26579c` | Water |
| Ultramarine coat | `#26409a` | Hero clothing |
| Cobalt light | `#4a76cc` | Cloth highlights, dash smear |
| Pumpkin orange | `#d86c1e` | Hero head mid tone |
| Scarlet | `#c8341e` | Scarf, HP bar, hurt vignette |
| Cadmium yellow | `#ffd040` | Eyes, hit dabs |
| Chrome yellow | `#ffe070` | Halo rings, stars, timer (`#ffe27a`) |
| Star white | `#fff6c8` | Hottest light centres |
| Turnip violet | `#763896` | Small enemy, top half |
| Turnip cream | `#e2d09a` | Small enemy, bottom half |
| Ghost turquoise | `#a2d0d2` | Fast floating enemy |
| Frame gold | `#d8aa48` | Gilded UI frames |

**Ground material ramps** (6 steps dark → light, from the module's `MATS`):

| Material | Ramp | Accents (12–14 % of pass-2 strokes) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wheat | `#3c2e18 #54421e #6c5624 #866c2a #a08232 #bc9a3e` | `#2e3e70 #a65e28 #4e5a28` |
| Meadow | `#1a3430 #23463c #2e5944 #3c6a48 #527e4a #70944e` | `#2e4a86 #8a8a3a #3a6a7a` |
| Path | `#1c1e44 #262a5a #31356c #3d4180 #4c4f94 #6264a8` | `#6a4f8e #2c4f72 #7a6a5a` |
| Forest | `#08120f #0e1d18 #142a20 #1b3828 #24462f #305639` | `#1a2650 #3a4a24 #0e2a36` |
| Pond | `#10244e #163268 #1d4384 #26579c #3270ae #4a8fbc` | `#78c0c0 #c6d2a0 #e8c850` |

**Character ramps:** coat `#141d52 #1d2c78 #26409a #3157b4 #4a76cc #7aa0e0`; pumpkin `#8e3a12 #b8521a #d86c1e #ec8a28 #f6aa3c #fcd06a`; leaf `#163a2a #1f5a3a #2f7a4a #4a9a52 #80bc5c`; turnip violet `#34124c #55206f #763896 #985ab6 #c28cd8`; cream `#9c8656 #c4ad78 #e2d09a #f4e9c2 #fffbe8`; ghost `#3d64a6 #6e9ec8 #a2d0d2 #cbece4 #f2fbf4`; brute plum `#1c1220 … #a27aa4`, umber `#22160e … #a07c52`; carved glow `#4a1206 #ffb52e #ffe070 #fff6c8`.

**Rules**

- Cool colours (blues, violets, greens) own ~85 % of the screen. Warm yellows/oranges are *light*: hero, lanterns, windows, pickups, eyes, hits.
- Never a flat colour: neighbouring strokes mix 2–4 steps of the same ramp; a macro fbm (scale 250 units) shifts the ramp index by up to ±1.6 so fields have large lighter and darker patches.
- Complementary accent dabs (blue in wheat, ochre in meadow) are essential for the Van Gogh vibration.
- Outlines are never `#000`: `#111733`, `#1d1036`, `#0c0812`, `#1f3a78` (ghost), `#04080a` (cypress).
- Hit flash tint is warm `#ffc84a` drawn additively, never white.

## Typography

- **Cinzel** 600/800 — titles, timer digits, card names. <https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Cinzel> — gold `#ffe27a`, embossed: `text-shadow: 0 2px 0 #3a2408, 0 0 14px rgba(255,200,80,.45)`, `letter-spacing: 2px`.
- **Caveat Brush** 400 — labels, HP and level text, kill counter, damage numbers. <https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Caveat+Brush> — cream `#fff0c8` / pale blue `#cfe4ff`, `text-shadow: 0 2px 0 #0a0e24, 0 0 6px rgba(6,8,26,.9)`.
- **Alegreya** italic 500 — descriptions. <https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Alegreya> — `#e6eefa`, `text-shadow: 0 1px 3px #000`.

```css
@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Cinzel:wght@600;800&family=Caveat+Brush&family=Alegreya:ital,wght@1,500&display=swap');
.timer { font: 800 36px/1 'Cinzel', 'Trajan Pro', Georgia, serif; color: #ffe27a; letter-spacing: 2px; text-shadow: 0 2px 0 #3a2408, 0 0 14px rgba(255,200,80,.45); }
.label { font: 400 23px 'Caveat Brush', 'Segoe Print', cursive; color: #fff0c8; text-shadow: 0 2px 0 #0a0e24, 0 0 6px rgba(6,8,26,.9); }
.desc  { font: italic 500 18px 'Alegreya', Georgia, serif; color: #e6eefa; text-shadow: 0 1px 3px #000; }
```

In-world damage numbers (canvas): `400 12px "Caveat Brush"` (crit 17 px), fill `#f6c43a` (crit `#f6602a`), outline `strokeText` `#121838` with lineWidth 2.8 (crit 3.6), then a highlight pass in `#fff4c0` (crit `#ffd27a`) at 75 % alpha offset by (−0.35, −0.45) units, rotated ±0.15 rad.

## Rendering technique

The look rests on **one primitive**, `stroke(ctx, x, y, angle, len, wid, col, rng, opts)`: an impasto dab drawn in local space as

1. a filled body: blunt rounded start (`quadraticCurveTo` bulge of 1.15 × half-width behind the start), slightly bent sides (random bend ±0.18 × length), a pointed tip at `len/2 + 0.35·halfWidth`;
2. a **light ridge**: a curve along the upper third, lineWidth 0.48 × half-width, colour mixed 30 % toward `#fff6dc` (`opts.hi`), alpha 0.8;
3. a **shadow edge**: a curve along the lower side, lineWidth 0.32 × half-width, colour × 0.58, alpha 0.75;
4. a **bristle groove**: a thin line (0.08 × width) at a random lateral offset, colour × 0.7, alpha 0.55.

Pipeline:

1. **Init (bake once):**
   - Ground stroke atlas: for each of 5 materials, 6 ramp colours + 3 accents × 3 variants, plus gold and flower dabs, painted onto one 1024 × 320 sheet at 3 px/unit, each trimmed to its painted bounding box, read back once with `getImageData`.
   - Characters: every animation frame is a separate painting (hero 3 idle + 4 walk, small enemy 2 colour variants × 4, ghost 3, brute 4) via `paint()` into CPU canvases (`willReadFrequently: true` – thousands of tiny anti-aliased paths raster faster there), then copied into a normal canvas for fast blitting; mirrored copies prebuilt.
   - Props (cypress ×3 heights, olive ×2, hay ×2, house ×2 with light positions, lamp, sunflowers ×2), FX sprites (halos, glow, pool, swirls, dabs, shadow, star, smear, trail), HUD textures (async, one per `setTimeout` task).
2. **Ground chunks (256 × 256 world units, generated incrementally):** sample materials and flow vectors on a 5-unit grid, fill an `ImageData` with the bilinear under-painting × canvas weave, then splat ~6 000 atlas strokes in pure JS (rotated nearest-neighbour sampling with alpha-over), then decals, then `putImageData` in 160-px bands. The generator yields every 30 strokes so no frame hitches.
3. **Per frame, draw order:** ground chunks → ground overlay (additive light pools, spawn swirls) → pickups → shadows → y-sorted props/enemies/hero → orbitals → projectiles → particles → damage numbers → fireflies (additive) → screen varnish vignette → HUD (DOM).
4. **Resolution:** not pixel art; ground at up to 2.5 px/unit (`groundResMax`), sprites at 3 px/unit (pickups 6 px/unit) and scaled with smoothing.

## Background and ground

- **Materials** from noise (world units): forest where `warped(x/760, y/760) > 0.6`, pond where another warped field `< 0.31` (kept ≥150 units from spawn), wheat where `fbm(x/470, y/470)` crosses 0.5, meadow elsewhere. Paths are the 0.5 iso-line of a large fbm (scale 980): distance to the line = `|p − 0.5| / |∇p|`, path where distance < 9–15 units (≈24 units wide), with the tangent of the iso-line as its flow.
- **Flow fields** (`fieldAt`): curl of fbm at scale 120 (`v0,v1`) and 52 (`v2,v3`) – rotate the gradient by 90° (`(-gy, gx)/|g|`) so strokes swirl around noise blobs, producing the Starry-Night whorls.
  - wheat: `(v0·0.5, −1 + v1·0.5)` – mostly vertical stalks;
  - meadow: `(v0, v1)` – big swirls;
  - path: path tangent + 0.22 · `(v0, v1)` – flowing along the road;
  - forest: `(v2, v3)` – tight small swirls;
  - pond: `0.85·(v2,v3) + 0.3·(v0,v1)`.
  Every stroke adds ±0.15 rad jitter.
- **Stroke sizes per material** (length L × width W, bend): wheat 9 × 2.5 (0.55), meadow 8 × 2.7 (0.45), path 11 × 2.5 (0.22), forest 6.5 × 2.6 (0.45), pond 10 × 2.5 (0.62).
- **Two passes:** pass 1 on a jittered grid of 4.3 units, one stroke per cell, ramp index `floor(rand·4 + bias − 0.4)` at scale 1.12 × (0.8–1.2); pass 2 on 6.2 units, kept with probability `pB` (wheat 0.75, meadow 0.62, path 0.55, forest 0.4, pond 0.72), index `2 + floor(rand·3 + bias)`, `acP` 12–14 % accent strokes. `bias = (macro − 0.5) · 3.2`, macro = `fbm(x/250, y/250)`.
- **Material per stroke** is chosen randomly by the interpolated weights, so borders dissolve into interleaved strokes instead of hard edges.
- **Under-painting:** per-material dark colours (wheat `rgb(46,34,20)`, meadow `rgb(17,32,28)`, path `rgb(17,17,40)`, forest `rgb(6,11,10)`, pond `rgb(10,21,50)`) × (0.8 + 0.45 · macro), with a 4-pixel canvas weave: alternate 4 × 4 cells darken their edge rows or columns to 0.87.
- **Decals:** path lamp reflections (cell 26, 32 %: 2–4 gold dabs side by side across the path), meadow wildflowers (cell 12, 20 %: 2–3 tiny 3 × 2 dabs in `#f4efd8`, `#ffd84a`, `#7aa8e8`), wheat ears (cell 9, 14 %: vertical gold dabs), poppies (cell 34, `#e0582a`), pond whorls (cell 70: 18–26 strokes on a 1.6–2.4-turn spiral, radius 12–20, squashed 0.62, gold in the centre), star reflections (cell 40: 5 gold dabs in a ring).
- All randomness is seeded per world cell (`hashInt(cx, cy, seed)`), so neighbouring chunks agree and borders are seamless.

## Characters

**Hero** (34 × 42 unit canvas, anchor (17, 37) = feet; ≈18 wide × 30 tall):

- Legs: two `seg()` strokes 2.5 wide in `#2b2238`, boots 3.6 × 2.0 strokes in `#1e130e`; walk pose swings feet ±1.9 units and lifts the forward one 1.3.
- Coat: a Catmull-Rom spline polygon from shoulders (y −16) widening to a hem at y −4, painted with `sp 1.55, len 4.2, wid 1.5`, vertical strokes (`−π/2 + x·0.07`), coat ramp picked by `2.2 − x·0.28 ± 0.8` (lit from the left), prussian contour 1.0 × 3. Two yellow button dabs `#f0c040`.
- Scarf: four alternating `#c8341e`/`#e8502a` dabs at the neck plus a fluttering tail behind (two segs).
- Head: 44-point ellipse rx 8.8, ry 7.4 centred at (0.6, −22.6) with 3.5-lobe ribbing, strokes follow the **meridians** of the sphere (`merid()` computes the slope of the meridian through each point), pumpkin ramp by `2.6 − dx·1.5 − dy·1.3`; four darker rib lines (`polyStroke`, 0.75 wide); contour 1.1 × 3.2; green stem and leaf.
- Face looks to +x: carved triangles for eyes (size 1.7, tall 1.25) and nose, a zig-zag 13-point mouth. `carved()` = dark rim offset (0.35, 0.4) `#4a1206`, fill `#ffb52e`, 62 % inset `#ffe070`, 30 % inset `#fff6c8`.
- Facing: mirror the sprite; frames re-painted with new seeds so the strokes "boil" gently between frames.

## Enemies and props

- **Small melee enemy** (turnip, 30 × 34): a 40-point bulb, narrower at the bottom; strokes run around the bulb (`atan2(dx/rx², −dy/ry²)·0.7`). The top half is violet, the bottom cream, with a wavy split line `0.5 + 0.08·sin(x·0.9)`. Four leaf strokes on top (6.4 × 2.5, `#1f5a3a`/`#2f7a4a`), contour `#1d1036` 0.95. Angry eyes: yellow dabs `#ffcf40` 2.4 × 1.6 with dark pupils and slanted brows `#1d0f2a`. Two colour variants (violet/cream and magenta/gold).
- **Fast floating enemy** (ghost, 30 × 32): a spline body with a wavy tail whose control points move with the phase; strokes swirl around the head centre (`atan2 + π/2 + 0.35`); ghost ramp brightest in the centre; contour `#1f3a78` 0.8; flat dark ellipses for eyes and an "O" mouth (`#0d1430`) – the only non-stroke details, for instant readability. Drawn at alpha 0.9, hovering ±1.2 units.
- **Brute** (colossus, 66 × 64): a 44-point blob rx 17.5, ry 16.5 painted with bigger strokes (`sp 2.0, len 5.4, wid 2.05`): plum above, umber below, turquoise rim light `#6fa4b0`/`#b4d0c4` on the upper-left edge. Glowing cracks: three passes of `polyStroke` per crack (dark 2.0 `#1a0c08`, orange 1.15, white-hot 0.45 `#fff2b0`) plus a 7-stroke glowing core; additive `glow` sprite pulses on the core. Root arms (2 segs + 3 finger strokes), crown of 5 leaves, thick legs.
- **Props** (all y-sorted sprites with painted shadows):
  - Cypress – the signature flame-shaped tree: 60–82 units tall, width `7.6·sin(π·(0.16+0.86t))^0.75`, a wobbling centre line; strokes 7.5 × 2.0 nearly vertical, swaying `0.6·sin(t·11 + x·0.35)`; ramp `#081210 … #3f6e40` with 8 % `#22355f` blue dabs. Becomes 45 % transparent when the hero walks behind it.
  - Olive tree: twisted trunk segs + 3 foliage blobs with radial strokes in sage greens and 10 % `#4a6a8c` dabs; contour skipped on the lit side.
  - Haystack, sunflowers (13 petals in `#e8a020/#f6c030/#ffd84a` around a dark seed head), houses (cream walls, blue side, red tiled roof, lit windows `#ffc93a` with cross bars), street lamps. Houses and lamps return light positions that get additive halos (radius 13 × size, flicker `0.85 + 0.1 sin(7t) + 0.05 sin(17t)`) and ground light pools.
- **Pickups:** XP gems are small teardrop paintings (gold ramp; big ones turquoise) baked at 6 px/unit, bobbing ±0.5–1 unit, each inside a rotating small halo (additive, alpha 0.55 ± 0.15).
- **Readability against the busy ground:** every actor gets (1) a dark painted contour, (2) a painted shadow, (3) a colour family the ground does not use (violet, cream, pale turquoise, plum), (4) yellow eyes. The hero additionally carries his own light halo, so he is always the brightest point on screen.

## Effects and particles

- **Seed projectile:** cream seed (7 × 5 units, contour `#3a2410`) rotated to its flight angle, preceded by a 16 × 4 unit trail made of an orange 15 × 2.2 stroke and a yellow 12 × 0.9 stroke, faded by a `destination-in` linear gradient.
- **Hit:** 3 paint dabs (one yellow/orange, two in the enemy's colour set) with velocity 30–80, `vz` 20–60, gravity 240; when they land they lie squashed (scale y 0.6) and fade. Plus a 4-stroke additive star (8 units; 12 for brutes) for 0.18 s.
- **Kill:** 9 dabs (22 for brutes, speed 75/110, size 1.8/2.6) and a paint swirl particle (3 spiral arms × 16 strokes in the enemy colours) expanding with outQuad and turning 3 rad over its life.
- **Pickup:** 1 (big: 5) star sprites rising.
- **Dash:** a smear of 6 long parallel strokes (blue/turquoise/orange), plus 4 blue dabs flung backwards; 2 ghost copies of the hero at alpha 0.25/0.125.
- **Level-up:** gold swirl 44 units + 14 stars bursting radially; also a growing gold swirl under the hero.
- **Hurt:** dab burst in red/orange/yellow/blue, an 18-unit star, the hero sprite flashed with additive warm tint, and the scarlet vignette.
- **Death (enemy):** sprite rises 3 units, scales to 1.2, alpha (1 − d)², additive flash for the first 40 %.

## Lighting, shadows and post-processing

- **Halos:** `haloSprite(px, colours, rings)` = radial gradient core (55 % → 0) + rings `[radius, alpha, strokeLen, strokeWidth]` (fractions of the radius) of tangential strokes. Gold halo (160 px, 5 rings) for hero/lamps/lanterns, cool halo (128 px) for big gems, small halo (64 px) for gems and fireflies. Always `globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter'`, slowly rotating.
- **Hero light:** two gold halos 44 and 72 units around the face, alpha 0.6 / 0.34 × pulse (0.85–1.0), plus a flickering 16 × 14 glow at the carved face and a 36 × 14 warm pool on the ground.
- **Ground light pools:** `pool` radial sprite (rgba(255,200,90,0.5) → 0) 60 × 30 units per lamp/window at alpha 0.45, additive.
- **Shadows:** a baked sprite of 16 dark ultramarine strokes (`#0c1030`, `#141a44`) in an ellipse, drawn at alpha 0.62 (ghost 0.35), sized per actor (hero 16 × 5.6, brute ~35 × 12).
- **Varnish vignette:** a rounded-rectangle band 13 % of the screen height, colour rgb(12,10,30), alpha `t² · 0.62`, plus loose dark edge strokes (22 × 6 units, alpha ≤ 0.5). Hurt version in rgb(200,52,24) with scarlet strokes, faded by `hurtT`. Baked once per screen size; only the 4 border strips are drawn.
- **Fireflies:** on a 130-unit world grid, 3 of 4 cells host a small halo drifting ±14/±10 units and twinkling.

## UI and HUD

- **Gold frame** (`goldFrame`): 9 concentric `strokeRect` bands across the thickness t – `#2a1c06 8 %, #7a5414 12 %, #d8aa48 14 %, #fbe7a0 6 %, #b8862c 16 %, #6a4610 8 %, #e6c068 14 %, #8a6018 12 %, #3a2808 10 %` – plus gold beads (radial gradient `#fff4c0 → #d8aa48 → #5a3a0c`) every 0.22 t along the middle and 8-petal corner rosettes. Used as a CSS `border-image` (slice 30).
- **Bars:** textures of horizontal brush strokes (`strokeBar`: 16–30 px long, 5–8 px wide) – track `#0e1638 #16224e #1d2c6a #26408a`, XP `#c88a1c … #fff0a8`, HP `#a8281a … #ffb060`; the fill has a ragged painted right edge (mask of 9 random-length strokes).
- **Timer:** a small night painting (swirling blue strokes + 2 stars) in a 22-px gold frame; "22:09" in Cinzel 800 36 px `#ffe27a`, label in Caveat Brush 18 px `#cfe4ff`.
- **Level-up cards:** 232 × 304 px framed night paintings (strokes swirling around a centre, darkened lower half), icon 112 px painted with the same strokes inside a gold halo, title Cinzel 19 px gold, description Alegreya italic 18 px. Overlay: `radial-gradient(ellipse at 50% 45%, rgba(20,28,70,.35), rgba(6,6,20,.82) 75%)`.
- **Icons:** painted at 100 × 100 with the same `paint()`/`stroke()` (heart, turnip, seed, basket…), stroke sizes 3–6 px.

```css
.panel { background: #121a44; color: #f6e6b0; font-family: 'Cinzel', Georgia, serif;
  border: 9px solid #d8aa48; border-image: linear-gradient(#fbe7a0, #b8862c 40%, #6a4610 60%, #e6c068) 9;
  box-shadow: 0 6px 16px rgba(0,0,0,.5); }
.bar { position: relative; height: 20px; outline: 4px solid #d8aa48; box-shadow: 0 3px 10px rgba(0,0,0,.55);
  background: repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, #16224e 0 18px, #1d2c6a 18px 30px, #0e1638 30px 44px); }
.bar > .fill { height: 100%; transition: width .15s;
  background: repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, #d0401e 0 16px, #ea6028 16px 28px, #f6883a 28px 38px, #a8281a 38px 50px);
  clip-path: polygon(0 0, 100% 0, calc(100% - 6px) 30%, 100% 55%, calc(100% - 5px) 100%, 0 100%); }
.timer { font: 800 36px/1 'Cinzel', serif; color: #ffe27a; letter-spacing: 2px; text-shadow: 0 2px 0 #3a2408, 0 0 14px rgba(255,200,80,.45); }
.label { font: 400 23px 'Caveat Brush', cursive; color: #fff0c8; text-shadow: 0 2px 0 #0a0e24, 0 0 6px rgba(6,8,26,.9); }
.card  { width: 232px; min-height: 304px; padding: 36px 26px 30px; color: #f6e6b0; box-shadow: 0 12px 26px rgba(0,0,0,.65); }
.card:hover { transform: translateY(-8px) scale(1.02); }
```

For the real look, bake `goldFrame()` and `strokeBar()` into canvases at startup and use `canvas.toDataURL()` as `border-image` / `background` (that is what the reference does).

## Motion and animation

- **Hero:** 4 walk frames (phase `p/4·2π`: leg = sin, bob = −|cos|·0.7, arm = −sin, scarf flutter = cos), switched by distance walked; 3 idle frames at 3.5 fps plus a sine bob of 0.4 units (2.4 rad/s).
- **Small enemy:** 4 frames (legs ±1.7, bob −0.8, body tilt ±0.07 rad, leaves ±0.12 rad). **Ghost:** 3 frames at 5 fps, hover `sin(3t)·1.2`. **Brute:** 4 frames at a slower rate (lift ±2.4, arm swing ±1.2).
- **Spawn:** stretch from 35 % to 100 % height (outQuad), width 1.25 → 1, alpha `smoothstep(0.2, 0.9)`, with a paint swirl beneath spinning −5 rad/s.
- **Hit flash:** additive warm tint copy, alpha `min(0.55, flash·0.9)`.
- **Lights:** halos rotate 0.35–1.2 rad/s; face glow flickers `0.32 + 0.08 sin(11t) + 0.05 sin(23t)`; gems pulse with `sin(5t)`.
- **Damage numbers:** pop 0.55 → 1.2 in the first 12 % of life, shrink to 1.0, rise 6 units, fade at `life·2.6`.
- The painting itself is static; motion comes from actors, rotating halos and drifting fireflies. Never animate the ground strokes (too expensive and visually exhausting).

## Do and don't

**Do**

- Build *everything* from the same stroke primitive – ground, characters, halos, HUD bars, icons.
- Give every ground material its own flow field and stroke size so regions read by direction, not only by colour.
- Outline actors with dark contour strokes, 30–55 % thicker on the shadow side.
- Make light warm, additive and slowly rotating – the only saturated yellow on screen.
- Bake strokes into offscreen canvases (atlas, sprites, chunks); only blit per frame.
- Seed all randomness per world cell / per sprite so repaints are identical.
- Frame UI elements like paintings in a gallery.

**Don't**

- Don't leave flat fills or smooth gradients as visible surfaces – base fills must be covered by strokes.
- Don't use thin vector outlines or pure black.
- Don't call thousands of `stroke()` per frame.
- Don't give enemies colours that exist in the ground beneath them (no green enemy on the meadow).
- Don't use white hit flashes or clean sans-serif fonts.
- Don't orient all strokes the same way or make ground strokes thinner than ~2 world units.
- Don't animate the ground.

## Implementation recipe

1. Set up a camera where the screen shows 360 world units vertically; scale = `canvasHeight / 360`.
2. Implement `stroke()` exactly as in the Code section; test it on a dark canvas – it must look like a thick oil dab with a ridge.
3. Implement `paint(polygon, opts)` (base fill → clipped jittered grid of strokes → `contour()`), `seg()` and `polyStroke()`.
4. Define 6-step ramps for each material and character; write `rampPick(ramp, value)`.
5. Paint each character frame into an offscreen canvas at 3 px/unit: limbs as `seg()`, bodies as `paint()` with a form-following angle function and a light term (`base − dx·1.5 − dy·1.3`), eyes as yellow dabs or `carved()` holes. Bake 3–4 frames per actor with different seeds.
6. Build a ground stroke atlas (per material: 6 ramp colours + 3 accents × 2–3 variants).
7. Write `fieldAt(x, y)` returning material weights and flow vectors (curl of fbm at 120 and 52 units, path tangent, macro brightness).
8. For each ground chunk (or, for a fixed-size level, once): fill the under-painting, run pass 1 (cell 4.3) and pass 2 (cell 6.2) of atlas strokes along the material's flow, then decals. Do it in a generator spread across frames.
9. Bake halo, glow, pool, shadow, star, dab, trail and swirl sprites.
10. Per frame: blit ground, light pools, shadows, y-sorted actors and props, then additive halos for every light, projectiles, particles, numbers, fireflies, vignette.
11. Build the HUD: bake `goldFrame()` and `strokeBar()` to data URLs and use them in CSS; Cinzel for numbers, Caveat Brush for labels.
12. Verify readability with a full horde on every ground material; boost contours or enemy brightness where they sink in.

## Code

The core techniques below are ported from the reference module and run stand-alone (Canvas 2D only). The complete runnable starter with hero, enemies, ground, halos and HUD is [`starter.js`](starter.js); the full reference implementation is [`../../js/styles/vangogh.js`](../../js/styles/vangogh.js).

```js
// Helpers
const TAU = Math.PI * 2;
const rng = (seed) => { let a = seed >>> 0; return { next() { a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) | 0; let t = Math.imul(a ^ (a >>> 15), 1 | a); t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t; return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296; } }; };
const H = (h) => { const n = parseInt(h.slice(1), 16); return [(n >> 16) & 255, (n >> 8) & 255, n & 255]; };
const rgb = (c, a) => (a === undefined ? `rgb(${c[0] | 0},${c[1] | 0},${c[2] | 0})` : `rgba(${c[0] | 0},${c[1] | 0},${c[2] | 0},${a})`);
const mix = (a, b, t) => a.map((v, i) => v + (b[i] - v) * t);
const mul = (c, f) => c.map((v) => Math.min(255, v * f));

/** One impasto dab: body, light ridge, shadow edge, bristle groove. */
function stroke(ctx, x, y, ang, len, wid, col, r, o = {}) {
  const hl = len * 0.5, hw = wid * 0.5, b = (o.bend ?? (r.next() - 0.5) * 0.36) * len;
  ctx.save(); ctx.translate(x, y); ctx.rotate(ang);
  if (o.a !== undefined) ctx.globalAlpha = o.a;
  ctx.beginPath();
  ctx.moveTo(-hl, -hw * 0.85);
  ctx.quadraticCurveTo(0, -hw * 1.25 + b, hl, b * 0.12 - hw * 0.14);
  ctx.lineTo(hl + hw * 0.35, b * 0.12); ctx.lineTo(hl, b * 0.12 + hw * 0.14);
  ctx.quadraticCurveTo(0, hw * 1.25 + b, -hl, hw * 0.85);
  ctx.quadraticCurveTo(-hl - hw * 1.15, 0, -hl, -hw * 0.85);
  ctx.fillStyle = rgb(col); ctx.fill();
  ctx.lineCap = 'round';
  ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(-hl * 0.88, -hw * 0.32); ctx.quadraticCurveTo(0, -hw * 0.5 + b, hl * 0.72, b * 0.12 - hw * 0.08);
  ctx.lineWidth = hw * 0.48; ctx.strokeStyle = rgb(mix(col, [255, 246, 220], o.hi ?? 0.3), 0.8); ctx.stroke();
  ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(-hl * 0.95, hw * 0.6); ctx.quadraticCurveTo(0, hw * 0.86 + b, hl * 0.85, b * 0.12 + hw * 0.1);
  ctx.lineWidth = hw * 0.32; ctx.strokeStyle = rgb(mul(col, 0.58), 0.75); ctx.stroke();
  const v1 = (r.next() - 0.5) * hw * 0.9;
  ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(-hl * 0.55, v1); ctx.quadraticCurveTo(hl * 0.2, v1 * 0.8 + b * 0.9, hl * 0.95, b * 0.12 + v1 * 0.3);
  ctx.lineWidth = Math.max(0.05, wid * 0.08); ctx.lineCap = 'butt'; ctx.strokeStyle = rgb(mul(col, 0.7), 0.55); ctx.stroke();
  ctx.restore();
}
```

```js
// Painting a region: base fill, clipped jittered grid of strokes, painted contour.
const pathOf = (P) => { const p = new Path2D(); p.moveTo(...P[0]); for (const q of P.slice(1)) p.lineTo(...q); p.closePath(); return p; };
function inPoly(P, x, y) { let ins = false; for (let i = 0, j = P.length - 1; i < P.length; j = i++) { const a = P[i], b = P[j]; if ((a[1] > y) !== (b[1] > y) && x < ((b[0] - a[0]) * (y - a[1])) / (b[1] - a[1]) + a[0]) ins = !ins; } return ins; }
const rampPick = (pal, v) => pal[Math.max(0, Math.min(pal.length - 1, Math.round(v)))];

function paint(ctx, P, r, o) { // o = { base, sp, len, wid, jit, col(x,y,r), ang(x,y,r), edge:{col,w,l} }
  const xs = P.map((p) => p[0]), ys = P.map((p) => p[1]);
  const path = pathOf(P), sp = o.sp, sy = sp * 0.75, jit = o.jit ?? 0.25;
  ctx.fillStyle = rgb(o.base); ctx.fill(path);
  ctx.save(); ctx.clip(path);
  for (let y = Math.min(...ys); y <= Math.max(...ys) + sy / 2; y += sy)
    for (let x = Math.min(...xs); x <= Math.max(...xs) + sp / 2; x += sp) {
      const px = x + (r.next() - 0.5) * sp, py = y + (r.next() - 0.5) * sy;
      if (!inPoly(P, px, py)) continue;
      stroke(ctx, px, py, o.ang(px, py, r) + (r.next() - 0.5) * jit * 2,
        o.len * (0.75 + r.next() * 0.5), o.wid * (0.8 + r.next() * 0.4), o.col(px, py, r), r);
    }
  ctx.restore();
  if (o.edge) contour(ctx, P, r, o.edge);
}
function contour(ctx, P, r, e) { // strokes along the edge, thicker on the down-right shadow side
  const cx = P.reduce((s, p) => s + p[0], 0) / P.length, cy = P.reduce((s, p) => s + p[1], 0) / P.length;
  const step = e.l * 0.6; let carry = r.next() * step;
  for (let i = 0; i < P.length; i++) {
    const a = P[i], b = P[(i + 1) % P.length], dx = b[0] - a[0], dy = b[1] - a[1], L = Math.hypot(dx, dy);
    if (L < 1e-6) continue;
    let d = carry;
    for (; d < L; d += step) {
      const x = a[0] + dx * d / L, y = a[1] + dy * d / L, ol = Math.hypot(x - cx, y - cy) || 1;
      const sh = ((x - cx) / ol) * 0.55 + ((y - cy) / ol) * 0.83;
      stroke(ctx, x, y, Math.atan2(dy, dx) + (r.next() - 0.5) * 0.2, e.l * (0.8 + r.next() * 0.4),
        e.w * (0.7 + 0.55 * Math.min(1, Math.max(0, sh * 0.5 + 0.5))), e.col, r, { hi: 0.16 });
    }
    carry = d - L;
  }
}

// Example: a round head with strokes following the sphere's meridians, lit from the upper left.
function paintHead(ctx, seed) {
  const r = rng(seed), cx = 0, cy = -22.6, rx = 8.8, ry = 7.4, head = [];
  const ORANGE = ['#8e3a12', '#b8521a', '#d86c1e', '#ec8a28', '#f6aa3c', '#fcd06a'].map(H);
  for (let i = 0; i < 44; i++) { const a = (i / 44) * TAU, k = 1 + 0.035 * Math.abs(Math.sin(a * 3.5)); head.push([cx + Math.cos(a) * rx * k, cy + Math.sin(a) * ry * k]); }
  const merid = (x, y) => { const dy = y - cy, q = Math.sqrt(Math.max(0.06, 1 - (dy / ry) ** 2)), kk = (x - cx) / (rx * q); return Math.atan2(1, (-kk * rx * dy) / (ry * ry * q)); };
  paint(ctx, head, r, { base: ORANGE[2], sp: 1.3, len: 3.6, wid: 1.45, jit: 0.12, ang: merid,
    col: (x, y, q) => rampPick(ORANGE, 2.6 - (x - cx) / rx * 1.5 - (y - cy) / ry * 1.3 + (q.next() - 0.5) * 1.3),
    edge: { col: H('#111733'), w: 1.1, l: 3.2 } });
}
```

```js
// Ground: flow field from the curl of fbm + stamping pre-rendered stroke sprites along it (bake once).
const hashInt = (x, y, s) => { let h = (Math.imul(x | 0, 374761393) + Math.imul(y | 0, 668265263) + Math.imul(s | 0, 1442695041)) | 0; h = Math.imul(h ^ (h >>> 13), 1274126177); return (h ^ (h >>> 16)) >>> 0; };
function perlin(x, y, s) {
  const x0 = Math.floor(x), y0 = Math.floor(y), fx = x - x0, fy = y - y0, f = (t) => t * t * t * (t * (t * 6 - 15) + 10);
  const g = (ix, iy, dx, dy) => { const a = ((hashInt(ix, iy, s) & 15) / 16) * TAU; return Math.cos(a) * dx + Math.sin(a) * dy; };
  const u = f(fx), v = f(fy), a = g(x0, y0, fx, fy), b = g(x0 + 1, y0, fx - 1, fy), c = g(x0, y0 + 1, fx, fy - 1), d = g(x0 + 1, y0 + 1, fx - 1, fy - 1);
  return (a + u * (b - a) + v * (c + u * (d - c) - a - u * (b - a))) * 1.414;
}
function fbm(x, y, seed, oct) { let a = 1, f = 1, t = 0, n = 0; for (let i = 0; i < oct; i++) { t += a * perlin(x * f, y * f, seed + i * 101); n += a; a *= 0.5; f *= 2; } return Math.min(1, Math.max(0, (t / n) * 0.5 + 0.5)); }
function curl(x, y, scale, seed) {
  const s = 1 / scale, n = fbm(x * s, y * s, seed, 2);
  const gx = fbm((x + 2) * s, y * s, seed, 2) - n, gy = fbm(x * s, (y + 2) * s, seed, 2) - n, m = Math.hypot(gx, gy) + 1e-9;
  return [-gy / m, gx / m]; // gradient rotated 90°: strokes circle around noise blobs -> swirls
}
function strokeSprite(L, W, bend, hex, seed, k = 3) { // one dab baked at k px per world unit
  const r = rng(seed), w = (L + W * 2) * k, h = (W * 2.2 + L * bend * 0.5 + 1) * k;
  const c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width = Math.ceil(w); c.height = Math.ceil(h);
  const g = c.getContext('2d'); g.translate(w / 2, h / 2); g.scale(k, k);
  stroke(g, 0, 0, 0, L, W, H(hex), r, { bend: (r.next() - 0.5) * bend });
  return c;
}
// Meadow: L 8, W 2.7, bend 0.45, ramp #1a3430 #23463c #2e5944 #3c6a48 #527e4a #70944e
function paintMeadow(g, wWorld, hWorld, s /* px per unit */) {
  const pal = ['#1a3430', '#23463c', '#2e5944', '#3c6a48', '#527e4a', '#70944e'];
  const SPR = pal.map((c, i) => [0, 1].map((v) => strokeSprite(8, 2.7, 0.45, c, 100 + i * 2 + v)));
  g.fillStyle = 'rgb(17,32,28)'; g.fillRect(0, 0, wWorld * s, hWorld * s); // under-painting
  for (const [cell, base, span, sc, keep] of [[4.3, -0.4, 4, 1.12, 1], [6.2, 2, 3, 1, 0.62]]) {
    for (let cy = 0; cy < hWorld / cell; cy++) for (let cx = 0; cx < wWorld / cell; cx++) {
      const r = rng((cx * 73856093) ^ (cy * 19349663) ^ (cell * 1000));
      const x = (cx + r.next()) * cell, y = (cy + r.next()) * cell;
      if (r.next() > keep) continue;
      const bias = (fbm(x / 250, y / 250, 61, 2) - 0.5) * 3.2;          // macro light/dark patches
      const idx = Math.max(0, Math.min(5, Math.floor(base + r.next() * span + bias)));
      const [vx, vy] = curl(x, y, 120, 51), ang = Math.atan2(vy, vx) + (r.next() - 0.5) * 0.3;
      const spr = SPR[idx][(r.next() * 2) | 0], k = (s / 3) * sc * (0.8 + r.next() * 0.4);
      const co = Math.cos(ang) * k, si = Math.sin(ang) * k;
      g.setTransform(co, si, -si, co, x * s, y * s);
      g.drawImage(spr, -spr.width / 2, -spr.height / 2);
    }
  }
  g.setTransform(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0);
}
```

```js
// Light halo: concentric rings of tangential strokes; draw additively and rotate slowly every frame.
function haloSprite(px, cols, rings) { // rings: [radius, alpha, strokeLen, strokeWidth] as fractions of R
  const c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width = c.height = px;
  const ctx = c.getContext('2d'), R = px / 2, r = rng(px * 7 + cols.length);
  const g = ctx.createRadialGradient(R, R, 0, R, R, R * 0.5);
  g.addColorStop(0, rgb(H(cols[0]), 0.55)); g.addColorStop(0.5, rgb(H(cols[1]), 0.18)); g.addColorStop(1, rgb(H(cols[1]), 0));
  ctx.fillStyle = g; ctx.fillRect(0, 0, px, px);
  rings.forEach(([rad, al, len, wid], i) => {
    const rr = rad * R, n = Math.max(6, Math.round((TAU * rr) / (len * R * 0.85))), off = r.next() * TAU;
    for (let k = 0; k < n; k++) {
      const a = off + (k / n) * TAU + (r.next() - 0.5) * 0.12;
      stroke(ctx, R + Math.cos(a) * rr, R + Math.sin(a) * rr, a + Math.PI / 2 + 0.12, len * R * (0.8 + r.next() * 0.4), wid * R,
        H(cols[Math.min(cols.length - 1, i + (r.next() < 0.3 ? 1 : 0))]), r, { a: al * (0.7 + r.next() * 0.3), bend: 0.12 });
    }
  });
  return c;
}
const GOLD_HALO = haloSprite(160, ['#fff6c8', '#ffe070', '#ffc83a', '#f0a030', '#d08a26'],
  [[0.2, 0.9, 0.14, 0.07], [0.34, 0.75, 0.15, 0.065], [0.5, 0.55, 0.15, 0.06], [0.66, 0.38, 0.15, 0.055], [0.84, 0.22, 0.14, 0.05]]);
function drawHeroLight(ctx, x, y, t) { // ctx in world units
  const pulse = 0.85 + 0.15 * Math.sin(t * 2.2);
  ctx.globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter';
  for (const [size, alpha, spin] of [[44, 0.6, 0.6], [72, 0.34, -0.4]]) {
    ctx.save(); ctx.translate(x, y); ctx.rotate(t * spin); ctx.globalAlpha = alpha * pulse;
    ctx.drawImage(GOLD_HALO, -size / 2, -size / 2, size, size); ctx.restore();
  }
  ctx.globalCompositeOperation = 'source-over'; ctx.globalAlpha = 1;
}
```

## Adapting it to your game

- **Keep fixed:** the stroke primitive and its proportions, painting by ramp picking, dark contour strokes, flow-field ground with per-material direction, additive rotating stroke halos for light, gold-framed museum UI, the night base with warm lights.
- **May change:** the landscape materials (e.g. snow `#c8d4e8` ramp with blue accents, sand, cobblestones painted as short curved arcs), the colour ramps (keep 6 steps, dark → light, and a complementary accent set), the characters (any shape: build a polygon, choose an angle function that describes its form – radial for blobs, vertical for cloth, meridians for spheres).
- **Daytime variant:** lift the under-painting and ramps (sky blues `#6a9ad0`, warmer yellows) but keep contours dark and keep halos for the sun/pickups; reduce vignette alpha to ~0.35.
- **Other genres:** side-scrollers can paint backgrounds as large flow-field panels (sky whorls with curl at scale 200) and keep actors as sprites; card games can use the framed-painting card and painted icons directly.
- **Other resolutions:** keep stroke sizes in world units (ground width ≥ 2 units). For a camera showing more of the world, scale the stroke size up with it, or the canvas turns into noise.
- **New enemy types:** pick a colour family absent from the ground, give it yellow eyes, a 0.8–1.6 contour, and a matching dab-burst colour set.

## Performance notes

- **Bake budget:** the reference spends ~0.5–1.5 s at init (atlas, ~25 character frames, ~10 props, FX). HUD textures are created asynchronously, one per `setTimeout`.
- **Chunks:** 256 × 256 units at ≤ 2.5 px/unit. Each chunk: ~4 000 grid samples (several fbm calls each) + ~6 000 stroke splats + decals. The reference splats atlas strokes in pure JS into an `ImageData` (exact span solving per row, no per-pixel bounds tests) and yields every 30 strokes / 16 rows inside a generator, building chunks within a 5 ms per-frame budget. Buffers are pooled to avoid GC pauses.
- **CPU vs GPU canvases:** paint with many small paths on `willReadFrequently: true` canvases (software rasteriser, faster for this), then copy into a normal canvas before blitting every frame.
- **Per frame:** one `drawImage` per actor, ~2–5 additive rotated halos per light, cached vignette strips. 2–4 ms in the reference with hundreds of enemies; the starter scene takes ~3 ms.
- **Hot spots:** large hordes (sprite count, not strokes), too many lights (each is 1–2 additive draws), re-baking anything per frame. Never call `stroke()` inside the frame loop except for a handful of particles – use baked dab sprites instead.
- **Static levels:** if your world is finite, bake the whole ground once into a few large canvases instead of chunking.

## Copy-paste prompt

```text
Build my game <X> in the "Starry Night" (Van Gogh impasto oil painting) style:
- Everything is made of one brush-stroke primitive: a thick dab with blunt start, tapered tip,
  a light ridge (colour mixed 30% to #fff6dc), a shadow edge (colour x0.58) and a bristle groove.
- Night palette: under-painting #141c30, meadow ramp #1a3430..#70944e, wheat #3c2e18..#bc9a3e,
  paths #1c1e44..#6264a8 (violet), ponds #10244e..#4a8fbc; warm light #ffd040/#ffe070/#fff6c8 only for light,
  hero and pickups. Outlines are dark strokes (#111733), never black lines.
- Ground: two passes of 8x2.7-unit strokes (cells 4.3 and 6.2 world units) stamped from pre-baked sprites
  along per-material flow fields (curl of fbm at 120 and 52 units = swirls; wheat vertical; paths along tangent),
  12-14% complementary accent dabs, macro fbm (250 units) shifting ramp index. Bake it, never per frame.
- Characters: paint each frame offscreen at 3 px/unit: polygon base fill, clipped jittered grid of strokes
  (spacing ~1.3, length ~3.6, width ~1.45) oriented by the form, ramp-picked with light from the upper left,
  dark contour strokes thicker on the shadow side, yellow eyes / glowing carved faces. 3-4 frames per actor.
- Enemies use colours absent from the ground (violet/cream, pale turquoise, plum with glowing cracks).
- Light: additive halos of concentric tangential yellow strokes, slowly rotating, warm light pools on the ground.
- Effects are paint dabs, 4-stroke stars and 3-arm paint swirls; hit flash is warm #ffc84a, never white.
- Screen: dark varnish vignette band (13% of height). UI: gilded 9-band gold frames, brush-stroke bars,
  Cinzel 800 gold numbers, Caveat Brush labels, Alegreya italic descriptions.
- Performance: bake strokes into canvases at init/chunk build; per frame only drawImage + a few additive halos.
```

<!-- style: shadow · https://miwale.com/styles/library/shadow/STYLE.md -->

# Shadow Theatre — Game Art Style Spec

> Backlit paper shadow-puppet theatre: indigo-black cut-paper silhouettes over glowing teal, violet, crimson and amber light fields.

The screen is a lit puppet stage seen from above. The **floor is the light**: big organic colour fields (moonlit teal, dusk violet, crimson, amber) glow like a backlit paper screen. They are joined by thin ink seams threaded with lace beads and covered in flat ink cut-outs: grass tufts, leaves, filigree scrolls, dandelion clocks and stars. **Everything that stands is a flat silhouette** in indigo-black ink `#0b0510`, built from tapered strokes, lens leaves and spiral curls in the tradition of Lotte Reiniger and *Limbo*. The only colour on a silhouette is **emissive**: the hero's carved pumpkin face, the small enemies' acid-green eyes, the brute's magenta cracks. There is also a soft baked rim of light. Ghosts invert the rule and are pale glowing veils. Velvet curtains, a scalloped valance and a vignette frame the scene as a theatre. The reference game is *Jack vs. the Turnip Ancestors* (a top-down survivor-like). Treat it only as an example.

## At a glance

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Family | Silhouette · Paper Shadow Puppets |
| Mood | fairy-tale gothic, warm, mysterious, theatrical, cosy-spooky |
| Best for | survivor-likes / hordes, halloween & folklore action, silhouette puzzle-platformers, storybook adventures |
| Renderer | Canvas 2D, fully procedural (no image assets) |
| Pixel art | No – smooth, anti-aliased, sprites baked at K ≈ 1.3 × (screen px / 360) px per world unit |
| Difficulty | 4/10 – silhouettes are easy; making many enemy types readable by outline alone takes thought |
| Fonts | Cinzel (numbers, titles), IM Fell English SC (small-caps labels), Cormorant Garamond (body) |
| Key colours | ink `#0b0510`, amber `#ffc662`, crimson `#f26a52`, violet `#b682dc`, teal `#76ccc6`, face gold `#ffd65e`, eye green `#d8ff62`, crack magenta `#ff5ad2` |

## When to use it

- **Great for hordes.** A flat silhouette reads at any size, and 200 black shapes on a glowing floor stay legible. In the late game the screen fills with ink and the emissive eyes still separate the enemy types.
- **Halloween, folklore, fairy tales, gothic storybooks.** The puppet-theatre framing adds narrative charm for free.
- **Silhouette platformers and puzzle games.** The light/ink split is the whole visual language.
- **Bad for colour-coded gameplay.** Team colours, element types or equipment cannot show on bodies; only small emissive marks are allowed.
- **Bad for daylight, sci-fi or "realistic" settings,** and for games whose characters need readable faces or costumes.
- **Bad for tiny units in dense strategy games.** Silhouettes under ~12 px tall lose their identifying curls.

## Color palette

| Swatch | Hex | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shadow Ink | `#0b0510` | Every silhouette, prop, curtain and HUD plate (25–35 % of the screen) |
| Lace Ink | `#16081c` | Ground seams (85 %) and lace decals (layer at 80 %) |
| Amber Core / Edge | `#ffc662` / `#ea7a2c` | Warm amber field: centre / near seams (largest field type) |
| Hot Gold | `#fff0c4` | Hot heart deep inside amber fields |
| Crimson Core / Edge | `#f26a52` / `#b02a42` | Crimson field |
| Violet Core / Edge | `#b682dc` / `#6840a2` | Dusk-violet field |
| Moon Teal Core / Edge | `#76ccc6` / `#2c748c` | Moonlit water field (ripple highlights rgb(215,255,245)) |
| Face Core → Ember | `#fffbe2` → `#ffd65e` → `#ff9a22` → `#ff6a10` | Carved face gradient (radial), bloom `rgba(255,150,40,.95)` |
| Hero Rim | `#ffb24a` | Hero's permanent rim of light |
| Eye Green | `#d8ff62` | Small-enemy eyes: `#ffffe0` → `#d8ff62` → `#7fe02a`, bloom `rgba(170,255,70,.95)` |
| Crack Magenta | `#ff5ad2` | Brute cracks (stroke `#ffb8f0`, shadow `rgba(255,70,210,1)`), core and eyes |
| Veil White | `#dcefff` | Ghost veil: `#fbfdff` → `#dcefff` → `#a9d4ff` |
| Ghost Hollow | `#1c0f36` | Ghost eye/mouth holes |
| Gem Aqua | `#3fe0d8` | Small XP gem (`#fff` → `#b8fff4` → `#3fe0d8`); big gem `#fff0a8` → `#ffb03a` |
| Velvet | `#2a0a20`, `#240818` | Curtain sheen stripes |
| HUD Gold | `#ffd98a` | HUD headings; hairline `rgba(255,196,120,.55)` |

Exact field colours (RGB, edge → core): teal `[44,116,140]→[118,204,198]`, violet `[104,64,162]→[182,130,220]`, crimson `[176,42,66]→[242,106,82]`, amber `[234,122,44]→[255,198,98]`.

**Palette rules**

- There are only two materials: **light** (the floor, glows and emissive parts) and **ink** (everything standing). No mid-tones on bodies.
- Silhouettes are always `#0b0510` at full opacity. Never tint a body in a field colour, and never use pure `#000`.
- Character colour must be small and emissive. One emissive hue per class: hero orange-gold, small enemies acid green, brutes magenta, ghosts cold blue-white.
- Fields always neighbour in the order teal | violet | crimson | amber, because they are thresholds of one noise value. Target roughly 40 % amber, 30 % crimson, 20 % violet and 10 % teal on screen.
- Warm light (gold/orange) belongs to the hero and friendly objects (lanterns, lit pumpkins, the follow-spot).

## Typography

- **Cinzel** 400/700/900 – https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Cinzel – timer, numbers, titles, level badge, damage numbers, card names.
  `font: 900 34px/1.05 'Cinzel', Georgia, serif; letter-spacing: 3px; color: #ffe4a6; text-shadow: 0 0 6px rgba(255,170,70,1), 0 0 16px rgba(255,110,40,.8);`
- **IM Fell English SC** 400 – https://fonts.google.com/specimen/IM+Fell+English+SC – small-caps labels and hints ("until midnight").
  `font: 13px 'IM Fell English SC', Georgia, serif; letter-spacing: 3px; color: #f4c99a;`
- **Cormorant Garamond** 500/600/700 – https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Cormorant+Garamond – body text, card descriptions, stats.
  `font: 700 20px/1.15 'Cormorant Garamond', Georgia, serif; color: #22081a;`

Text effects:
- Glowing HUD text uses ink shadows to cut it out of the floor, then an orange glow: `text-shadow: 0 0 2px #0b0510, 0 0 3px #0b0510, 0 0 8px rgba(255,150,60,.85), 0 0 18px rgba(255,110,40,.5)`.
- Big titles ("LEVEL UP!") are Cinzel 900 at 68 px, letter-spacing 4 px, `#ffe6ad`, with `text-shadow: 0 0 3px #0b0510, 0 0 12px rgba(255,170,70,1), 0 0 34px rgba(255,100,40,.8)`.
- **Damage numbers on canvas** are Cinzel 700 at 8.6 world units (12.5 for crits). Each gets an ink stroke of 0.24 × font size, drawn with `shadowBlur = 0.35 × size` in `rgba(255,190,110,.7)` (crits: 0.5 × size in `rgba(255,140,40,.95)`). The fill is a vertical gradient `#fff → #ffe2b0` (crits `#fff → #ffe07a → #ff8a22`). The number is baked to a sprite cache keyed by value.

## Rendering technique

The world is drawn in world units with 360 units visible vertically. The hero is about 18 units wide and 33 tall.

1. **Init: pick the bake resolution.** `K = clamp(round(screenHeightPx / 360 × 1.3 × 4) / 4, 2.5, 5)` px per world unit (DPR is capped at 2). The extra 1.3 keeps silhouettes crisp when they are slightly scaled.
2. **Bake every sprite** with `mk(x0, y0, x1, y1, draw, pad)`. It creates a canvas of `(x1 − x0 + 2·pad) × K` px and sets the transform to K. Fill and stroke are `#0b0510` with round caps and joins. The draw function then paints in world units with feet at (0, 0) and the figure facing +x.
3. **Per sprite, also bake:**
   - a mirrored copy, for facing −x;
   - a rim-light copy `rimSpr(s, colour, rad)`: tint the silhouette, stamp it 8 times around a circle of `d = rad·K·0.55` px, blur by `d`, then add the unblurred stamps at 60 %;
   - for the hero, a white "hurt" rim (`rad 1.1`);
   - for enemies, torn-paper shard sets for the death animation.
4. **Bake glows** as radial-gradient squares: `glowSpr(radius, stops)`. Examples: the warm pool (r 30), the face halo (r 9), gold (r 10), pink (r 12), cyan (r 6), embers (r 3) and the dark contact shadow (r 10, `rgba(14,5,20,.55)`).
5. **Ground chunks** of 256 world units are rendered by a generator (see next section) at up to 2.5 px per unit, then cached.
6. **Per frame, in order:**
   - ground chunks;
   - contact shadows and the hero's additive follow-spot;
   - props, enemies, hero, gems, orbitals and projectiles, all y-sorted;
   - particles;
   - damage numbers;
   - the theatre-frame overlay, baked once per screen size.
7. **Light is always additive.** Glows, rims, embers, flares and trails use `globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter'`. Ink is drawn with normal `source-over`.
8. **Blit with world-unit sizes.** Draw with `drawImage(c, x − ax/K, y − ay/K, w/K, h/K)`, and snap positions to device pixels when not rotating. Wobble and sway use a rotate transform around the feet.

## Background and ground

The floor is a **light field shader**, computed per pixel from one scalar noise value:

```
f(x, y) = (warped(x/1300, y/1300, seed 501, warp 0.85, 3 oct) − 0.5) × 9.5 + (fbm(x/420, y/420, seed 502, 2 oct) − 0.5) × 0.9
```

- **Bands.** The thresholds `TH = [−0.95, −0.3, 0.35]` split f into teal | violet | crimson | amber. Neighbouring bands blend over ±0.075 f-units (`smoothstep`).
- **Colour inside a band.** Take the depth into the band (its distance to the nearest threshold) and compute `t = smoothstep(0, 0.75, depth) × (0.55 + 0.45·gloss)`, where `gloss = fbm(x/520, y/520, 503, 3)`. The colour lerps from the edge colour towards the core colour by t. Amber also lerps towards the hot `#fff0c4` by `smoothstep(0.9, 2.2, depth) × (0.25 + 0.4·gloss)`. The result is finally multiplied by `0.9 + 0.2·gloss`.
- **Sampling grid.** f, gloss, colour, teal weight, ripple phase and a **signed distance to the nearest seam** are sampled on a 4-unit grid with an 8-unit margin. The distance is `sd = (f − nearestThreshold) / |∇f|`, clamped to ±60 units. Pixels interpolate the grid bilinearly.
- **Light bleed.** Where `|sd| < 6`, lerp towards rgb(255,240,215) by `(1 − |sd|/6)² × 0.22`. Each seam looks like a slit where light leaks through.
- **Moonlit ripples.** Only on teal: `phase = y·0.72 + 7·perlin(x/95, y/95) + 2.5·perlin(x/33, y/33)`. Where `sin(phase) > 0.86`, lerp towards rgb(215,255,245) by `(sin − 0.86) × 7.1 × tealWeight × 0.42`. This gives thin wavy horizontal highlight lines.
- **Paper grain.** A 256² Int8 tile: a 3×3 box sum of hash noise × 3.2 plus the raw value × 5, plus 70 random-walk fibres of 8–34 px (+4 each). It is added as R +g, G +0.9g, B +0.8g.
- **Seam line.** `a = (0.36 − |sd|)·res + 0.5`. Where `a > 0`, lerp towards `#16081c` by `min(1, a) × 0.85`. The line is about 0.72 units wide and anti-aliased.
- **Lace layer.** These are ink vector paths drawn into a separate canvas, then composited onto the chunk **once at 80 % alpha**, so the light glows faintly through.
  - **Seam beads.** Points are scattered every 4.2 units and kept where `|sd| < 2.4`. Each point is projected onto the seam (`p − n·sd`) and offset 1.1–1.5 units to one side. It becomes one of three motifs:
    - 45 %: a dot (r 0.62) inside a ring (r 1.25, 0.32-unit stroke);
    - 35 %: a pair of lens leaves (2.3 long);
    - 20 %: two dots (r 0.42 and 0.3).
  - **Field decals.** Each decal kind has its own scatter cell size, and decals are skipped within 0.06 f-units of a seam:
    - amber: grass tufts (cell 15), 5–9 tapered blades 3.5–8 units long, density raised by a noise mask; dandelion clocks (14 radial seeds on a stem);
    - crimson: filigree double scrolls (cell 30, 62 %, spirals 9–15 units with leaves) and lace rosettes (cell 64);
    - violet: small fallen leaves and maple shapes (cell 15/34) and 4–5-point cut-out stars plus additive light glints (cell 17);
    - teal: broken ripple ellipses (2–3 rings, radius 3.5 + 3.2k, height × 0.4, dashed in random gaps), reeds with cattail heads, lily pads;
    - large fern rosettes and branching root systems (cell 165).
- **Additive glints.** These go on top of the lace. Violet gets 4-point stars in `rgba(255,236,190,.55)` with a `rgba(255,250,230,.7)` dot. Teal ripples get pale ellipses in `rgba(220,255,250,.35)`.

Scale: fields are hundreds of units across (noise period about 1300 units), so one screen shows 2–4 fields. Decals are tiny: 2–15 units, with strokes of 0.25–0.85 units.

## Characters

**The hero** (reference: pumpkin-head Jack) measures about −14…9 units in x and −33…1.5 units in y, with the feet at the origin. Draw order, back to front:

1. **Back leg.** A jointed puppet leg: hip → knee (4.2 units) → foot (4.4 units) as a `limb` 1.15 → 0.9 wide. The foot is a 1.4 → 0.7 limb ending in a toe curl (2.2 long, turn −5.5).
2. **Back arm.** Shoulder at (−1.6, sh + 0.8), upper arm 3.4, forearm 3.2, a 1.0-unit limb ending in a hand circle (r 0.85).
3. **Front leg.**
4. **Cloak.** From the shoulders (y = −16.2 + bob) to a **jagged hem** of 7 zig-zag points alternating +1.3 / −0.7. The hem trails backwards by 2.2 units when walking. A small clasp curl sits at the back edge.
5. **Scarf.** An ellipse (3.5 × 1.3) plus two streaming tails: limbs 1.6 → 0.5, 11.6 units long when walking, hanging down when idle, waving at twice the step frequency.
6. **Front arm.** Width 1.1.
7. **Pumpkin head.** Four overlapping ellipses (`pumpkinShape`, rx 6.8, ry 5.4) at (0.8, −22.4). Add a stem limb (1.5 → 0.9) curving back, a leaf (4.2 long) and a long spiral curl (4.6, turn 6).
8. **Carved face**, the brightest thing on screen. Two triangular eyes, a triangle nose and a zig-zag grin with two teeth. It is filled by `glowFill` with the radial `FACE` gradient (centre `#fffbe2`, radius 6) and a 1.6-unit bloom.

**Frames.** There are 6 walk frames (phase i/6) and 4 idle frames, each baked with a warm rim (`#ffb24a`, rad 1.3), a white hurt rim and mirrored copies. The walk bob is `−|cos(phase)| × 0.9`, and the head bobs separately with a 0.4 phase lag.

**Per frame:**
- an additive follow-spot pool (r 30, scaled 1.1 × 0.62, alpha 0.55 ± 0.05);
- a contact shadow (0.8 × 0.26);
- the rim at 75 % ('lighter');
- the sprite;
- an additive face halo (r 9) at the head position, flickering `0.8 + 0.12·sin(11t) + 0.08·sin(27t)`.

## Enemies and props

Every type gets **a unique outline and one emissive colour**.

- **Small melee enemy** (turnip "creeper", about 24 × 30 units):
  - body: a bulb ellipse (7.8 × 7.0, or 7.0 × 7.6 for the variant) with a little top knob;
  - movement parts: two jointed root legs ending in curls, a taproot tail curling behind, curled arms, and root hairs;
  - **filigree leaf crown:** 3–4 curved stems (curlPts, 6.4–8.6 long) with a large leaf at each tip and two side leaves;
  - mouth: a zig-zag mouth **cut out** with `destination-out`, so the floor light shows through;
  - eyes: two angry slanted glowing eyes in acid green (bloom 1.3).

  It has 2 variants × 6 frames and rocks ±0.075 rad as it walks.
- **Fast enemy / ghost:**
  - the inversion of the rule: a white veil (head ellipse 5 × 5.6, a ragged lower edge, three curled tail wisps and two reaching arms with three long fingers);
  - colouring: tinted `source-atop` with a vertical gradient `#fbfdff → #dcefff → #a9d4ff`, then faded towards the tail with `destination-in` (95 % → 35 % alpha);
  - face: hollow eye and mouth ellipses in `#1c0f36`;
  - halos: the sprite is composited over a **dark halo** (tint `#160828`, blur 2.2·K px, alpha 0.42) and then a **light halo** (tint `#d6f0ff`, blur 1.4·K px, alpha 0.95), so it glows on any field.

  It has 4 frames and hovers.
- **Brute** (colossus, about 44 × 62 units):
  - body: a knobby bulb (radius 15 × 14 modulated by `1 + 0.07·sin(5a) + 0.05·sin(9a)`);
  - limbs: massive gorilla arms (5.2 → 2.6) with claws, and thick legs;
  - crown and beard: an **antler crown** of five thick curled stems with big leaves, and a dangling root beard;
  - emissive: **magenta cracks**, stroked `#ffb8f0` at 0.5–0.7 units with `shadowBlur 1.6·K` in `rgba(255,70,210,1)`, a diamond core and slit eyes in the same magenta;
  - extra glow: an additive pink glow (r 12) on the chest pulses at runtime.
- **Pickups:**
  - **small gems** are ink teardrops with an aqua glass interior and an additive cyan glow;
  - **big gems** are gold with a curl on top and a rotating 4-point flare.
- **Orbiting helper** (turnip lantern): an ink bulb with a leaf crown and a gold glowing carved face, plus an additive gold glow.
- **Props** are standing ink silhouettes baked once and y-sorted with the actors:
  - **trees:** recursive branching, three depths, tips ending in curls, about 4 leaves per tip, a cut-out knothole, roots with curls;
  - **iron gates:** pillars with cut-out arches, spear-tipped bars on an arched top, a ring lace band and scrolls;
  - **fences:** spear pickets with S-curls between the rails;
  - **graves:** a Celtic cross with a see-through ring, a round stone with a crescent-moon window, a crooked wooden cross with a wreath;
  - **scarecrows** with a crow;
  - **crow posts** (2-frame head flick);
  - **lantern poles** with a curled hook and a glowing pane;
  - **lit pumpkins** on curly vines, with an additive flickering gold glow;
  - **weeds** (thistles, tall grass, fiddlehead ferns).

  Trees and scarecrows sway like hinged puppets, weeds sway faster, and all props get a squashed contact shadow.

**Readability with many enemies.** Bodies all merge into one ink mass, so identity comes from:
1. the outline features that stick out (crowns, veils, antlers);
2. the emissive colour code (green dots = small enemies, magenta = brutes, white = ghosts, gold = hero);
3. the hero's constant warm rim and spotlight.

Enemies only get a rim when hit (cream `#fff6dc`, capped at 0.9, or 0.7 for brutes). Never give them a permanent rim.

## Effects and particles

All effects are light (additive) or paper (ink).

- **Projectile** (pumpkin seed):
  - a baked lens shape with a gradient `#ffcf7a → #fff6d8 → #fff` and a 1.2-unit bloom;
  - rotated along its velocity with a spin wobble of `sin(spin) × 0.6`;
  - an additive tapered trail 11 units long that grows in over the first 0.125 s;
  - an ember glow at 70 %, scaled 1.4.
- **Hit:**
  - 3 additive spark streaks (7-unit lens, transparent orange → `rgba(255,250,220,1)`), 0.22–0.32 s;
  - a 4-point flare for 0.16 s;
  - the enemy rim flash.
- **Death** (paper crumble):
  - for the first 0.14 s, the rim at 90 % over the sprite;
  - then the pre-cut **torn shards** (5 for small enemies, 4 for ghosts, 7 for brutes) fly outward by `2 + 10·outQuad(u)` units, rise 5 units, then fall `22·u²`, rotate ±(1.4–2.2)·u, shrink to 70 % and fade with `1 − u²`;
  - each shard's torn edge glows `#ff9a3a`;
  - paper-scrap particles (4–6-gon ink chips with one ember-lit edge) tumble with gravity 160;
  - embers rise;
  - a flare (size 1.1, or 2.4 for brutes).
- **Ghost death:** 5 pale curled wisps drift up, and cold embers.
- **Embers:** 3-unit additive radial sprites rising (gravity −18, drag 2.2), flickering `0.7 + 0.3·sin(30t + seed)`. There are warm, cold and pink variants.
- **Pickup:** one small ember (cold for small gems, warm for big ones).
- **Dash:** three ink-tinted afterimages (alpha 0.4/i, 6 units apart) and an ember trail.
- **Level up:**
  - a light ring (r 10.5) with 12 small stars, growing `0.4 + 1.2·outQuad(age)`;
  - a large flare (2.8);
  - 14 embers;
  - a rotating flare above the hero's head while `levelT > 0`.
- **Enemy spawn:** the enemy rises from a stage slot like a rod puppet. It uses `outBack(t × 1.15)` from 95 % of its height below, is clipped at the floor, shows a visible 0.7-unit ink rod, gets an additive warm slot glow and swings by `sin(14t)·(1 − t)·0.25` rad.

## Lighting, shadows and post-processing

- **There is no directional light.** The light comes from below and behind the paper, which means from the floor.
- **Contact shadows** are a dark radial sprite (`rgba(14,5,20,.55)` → 0), squashed to about 0.3 of its width under each actor. Prop shadow width comes from the prop's `sh` value, e.g. 1.9 for trees and 0.5 for crow posts.
- **Follow-spot:** an additive warm pool under the hero (r 30, `rgba(255,214,140,.55)` centre).
- **Emissive bloom** is baked: `glowFill` draws a gradient path once with `shadowBlur = bloom·K` and then again sharp. Additive glow sprites flicker around faces and lanterns at runtime.
- **Theatre frame overlay**, baked per screen size:
  - a radial vignette centred at (W/2, 0.52H), from 0.28·max(W, H) to 0.72·max(W, H): `rgba(14,4,22,0)` → `0.22` at 60 % → `0.7` at the edge;
  - **side curtains** 3.4 % of the width with a bezier tie-back waist at 42 % height, velvet sheen gradient `#0b0510 / #2a0a20 / #0b0510 / #240818 / #0b0510`, and an ink tassel;
  - a **scalloped valance** (16 scallops, 3.2 % of the height) with tassel cords and triangles;
  - an ink **stage lip** gradient over the bottom 6 %.
- **No colour grading or blur** at runtime. Everything is baked.

## UI and HUD

HUD pieces are **ink plates with a gold hairline**: an ink ring, a hairline ring, a second ink ring and a warm outer glow. Bars have glowing gradient fills inset 4–6 px. Numbers are Cinzel with an orange glow. The timer sits in a plate with a rounded-bottom "lambrequin" shape and has ink scroll ornaments (SVG) on both sides. Icons sit on a glowing radial disc (`#fff3c8 → #ffc35a → #ea6236 → #7a1c46`) with an ink border ring of 24 alternating beads, and the icon art is ink silhouettes with small emissive faces. Level-up cards are tiny stages: an amber-to-crimson radial glow, an ink curtain and scalloped valance cut-out over the top and sides, an ink stage-lip arc at the bottom with the key number in glowing gold, and a lift of 8 px plus a bigger glow on hover.

```css
.hud { font-family: 'Cormorant Garamond', Georgia, serif; color: #ffe9c4; }
.bar { height: 18px; background: #0b0510; border-radius: 9px; position: relative;
```

When the hero is hurt, the HP bar's hairline turns `#ff8a6a` and the glow grows to `0 0 26px 6px rgba(255,60,40,.8)`.

## Motion and animation

Everything moves like a **rod puppet**: jointed limbs swing, and whole sprites rock around the feet.

- **Hero:**
  - walk: 6 frames advanced at `anim × 1.5`; idle: 4 frames at 2.6 fps;
  - the legs swing ±0.6 rad and the knees bend by `0.55·max(0, sin(phase + side·1.4))`;
  - the cloak hem flutters at 2× the step frequency;
  - when hurt, the sprite blinks to 45 % alpha at 14 Hz during i-frames and the white rim is added.
- **Small enemy:** 6 frames at 4.8 per anim second, rocking ±0.075 rad, with a per-enemy seed offset so crowds never march in sync.
- **Brute:** 6 frames at 3.6 per anim second, rocking ±0.035 rad, with feet lifted up to 3.6 units.
- **Ghost:** 4 frames at 6 fps. It floats 2.2 units up, bobs ±1.2 units at 3.1 rad/s and sways ±0.06 rad. It has no walk cycle.
- **Props:** trees sway ±0.012 rad and scarecrows ±0.02 rad at 0.7 rad/s. Weeds sway ±0.05 rad at 1.3 rad/s. The crow flicks its head on every 4th beat (0.8 Hz). Lanterns and pumpkins flicker with `0.75 + 0.15·sin(9t) + 0.1·sin(23t)`.
- **Gems:** bob ±0.8 units at 3 rad/s, the glow pulses 0.75–1.0 at 5 rad/s, and on pickup they pop up to 1.6×.
- **Damage numbers:** pop from 1.6× to 1× in 0.08 s and fade over the last 0.25 s.

## Do and don't

**Do**
- Make the floor the brightest, most colourful layer, and keep everything standing flat ink.
- Build shapes from tapered limbs, lens leaves and spiral curls, and end every tip in a curl or leaf.
- Give each enemy class a unique silhouette feature and exactly one emissive colour.
- Keep the hero permanently rim-lit in a warm follow-spot, because it must win against any crowd.
- Carve holes (`destination-out`) for mouths, windows and knotholes so the light shows through.
- Bake everything at init (frames, mirrors, rims, glows, shards) and only blit per frame.
- Frame the scene as a stage: curtains, valance, vignette and stage lip.

**Don't**
- Don't outline or gradient-shade silhouettes. The lit edge comes only from the additive rim copy.
- Don't paint features in body colour, or give enemies warm emissives that compete with the hero's face.
- Don't let lace decals rival the actors. Keep them fine (0.25–0.85-unit strokes) at 80 %.
- Don't use pure black, grey or photo textures. Ink is indigo-black `#0b0510`.
- Don't run `ctx.filter` or `shadowBlur` per frame.
- Don't make the light fields small and noisy. They are hundreds of units across.
- Don't add a directional sun shadow. Shadows are only soft contact blobs.

## Implementation recipe

1. Set up a world-unit camera (360 units tall). Compute `K = clamp(round(hPx / 360 × 1.3 × 4) / 4, 2.5, 5)`.
2. Implement the toolkit: `spline`, `limb(pts, w0, w1)`, `curlPts`/`curl`, `leaf`, `ell`, `circ`, `poly`, `star`, `cut`, `pumpkinShape` (or your own primitive bulb) and `glowFill`.
3. Implement `mk()` (bake at K, feet at origin, ink fill), `flip`, `tint`, `rimSpr` (8 stamps + blur) and `glowSpr`.
4. Design the hero as a puppet: torso and cloak, jointed limbs with curl tips, a distinctive head with one emissive feature. Bake 6 walk + 4 idle frames with rim copies.
5. Design each enemy class with a unique protruding feature and one emissive colour. Bake 4–6 frames each, plus a hit rim and torn shards.
6. Write the ground shader: one warped-noise scalar → 4 threshold bands → edge-to-core colour → light bleed near the seam → optional ripples → paper grain → seam line. Use a 4-unit sample grid with bilinear interpolation, and render chunks in a generator.
7. Draw the lace layer: seam beads projected onto `sd = 0`, then field-specific ink decals. Composite it at 80 %.
8. Bake props as silhouettes, scatter them by field (warm props on amber and crimson, reeds on teal) and y-sort them with the actors.
9. Per frame: draw the ground, contact shadows, the hero spotlight, y-sorted sprites (rim 'lighter' first, then ink), additive emissive halos, particles and numbers, then the theatre frame.
10. Effects: additive flares, sparks, embers and trails; ink paper scraps; torn-shard deaths.
11. Build the HUD with ink plates, gold hairline rings, glowing gradient bars and Cinzel numbers.

## Code

These are the core techniques, ported from the reference module so they run standalone. `starter.js` has the complete runnable kit: ground shader, lace, hero, small enemy, ghost, brute, gems, projectile, frame. The full reference is `../../js/styles/shadow.js`.

```js
// Tapered cut-paper limb along a Catmull-Rom-smoothed polyline (the basic building block).
function spline(p, sub) {
  const o = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < p.length - 1; i++) {
    const p0 = p[i - 1] || p[i], p1 = p[i], p2 = p[i + 1], p3 = p[i + 2] || p[i + 1];
    for (let k = 0; k < sub; k++) {
      const t = k / sub, t2 = t * t, t3 = t2 * t;
      o.push([0, 1].map((j) => 0.5 * (2 * p1[j] + (-p0[j] + p2[j]) * t + (2 * p0[j] - 5 * p1[j] + 4 * p2[j] - p3[j]) * t2 + (-p0[j] + 3 * p1[j] - 3 * p2[j] + p3[j]) * t3)));
    }
  }
  o.push(p[p.length - 1]);
  return o;
}
function limb(c, pts, w0, w1, sub) {
  const s = pts.length > 2 ? spline(pts, sub || 5) : pts, n = s.length, L = [], R = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const a = s[Math.max(0, i - 1)], b = s[Math.min(n - 1, i + 1)];
    let dx = b[0] - a[0], dy = b[1] - a[1]; const d = Math.hypot(dx, dy) || 1; dx /= d; dy /= d;
    const w = (w0 + (w1 - w0) * (i / (n - 1))) * 0.5;
    L.push([s[i][0] - dy * w, s[i][1] + dx * w]); R.push([s[i][0] + dy * w, s[i][1] - dx * w]);
  }
  c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(L[0][0], L[0][1]);
  for (let i = 1; i < n; i++) c.lineTo(L[i][0], L[i][1]);
  for (let i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) c.lineTo(R[i][0], R[i][1]);
  c.closePath(); c.fill();
  c.beginPath(); c.arc(s[0][0], s[0][1], w0 / 2, 0, Math.PI * 2); c.fill();
}
// Spiral that tightens towards its end – every tip in this style finishes in one.
function curlPts(x, y, a, len, turn, n = 12) {
  const p = [[x, y]]; let h = a;
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const t = i / n; h += (turn * (0.25 + 1.75 * t)) / n;
    const s = (len / n) * (1.35 - 0.85 * t);
    x += Math.cos(h) * s; y += Math.sin(h) * s; p.push([x, y]);
  }
  return p;
}
// usage: ctx.fillStyle = '#0b0510'; limb(ctx, curlPts(0, 0, -1.2, 6, 5.5), 0.8, 0.1, 3);
```

```js
// Emissive fill (carved face / eyes / lantern pane): gradient + baked bloom. K = px per world unit.
const FACE = [[0, '#fffbe2'], [0.35, '#ffd65e'], [0.75, '#ff9a22'], [1, '#ff6a10']];
function glowFill(c, path, cx, cy, r, stops, bloom, bloomCol, K) {
  c.save();
  const g = c.createRadialGradient(cx, cy, 0, cx, cy, r);
  stops.forEach((s) => g.addColorStop(s[0], s[1]));
  c.fillStyle = g;
  c.shadowColor = bloomCol; c.shadowBlur = bloom * K;   // pass 1: bloom halo
  c.beginPath(); path(c); c.fill();
  c.shadowBlur = 0;                                     // pass 2: crisp shape on top
  c.beginPath(); path(c); c.fill();
  c.restore();
}
// Hole in the paper: the floor light shows through.
function cut(c, fn) { c.save(); c.globalCompositeOperation = 'destination-out'; c.fillStyle = '#000'; fn(); c.restore(); }
```

```js
// Rim of light around a baked silhouette (hero aura, hit flash). Add it with 'lighter' BEFORE the ink sprite.
function tint(src, col) {
  const c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width = src.width; c.height = src.height;
  const x = c.getContext('2d'); x.drawImage(src, 0, 0);
  x.globalCompositeOperation = 'source-atop'; x.fillStyle = col; x.fillRect(0, 0, c.width, c.height);
  return c;
}
function rimSprite(src, color, rad, K) {          // rad in world units: hero 1.3, small enemy 1.2, brute 1.6
  const t = tint(src, color), d = Math.max(1, rad * K * 0.55);
  const tmp = document.createElement('canvas'); tmp.width = src.width; tmp.height = src.height;
  const tc = tmp.getContext('2d');
  for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) { const a = (i / 8) * Math.PI * 2; tc.drawImage(t, Math.cos(a) * d, Math.sin(a) * d); }
  const out = document.createElement('canvas'); out.width = src.width; out.height = src.height;
  const oc = out.getContext('2d');
  oc.filter = `blur(${d.toFixed(1)}px)`; oc.drawImage(tmp, 0, 0); oc.filter = 'none';
  oc.globalAlpha = 0.6; oc.drawImage(tmp, 0, 0);
  return out;
}
// per frame: ctx.globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter'; ctx.globalAlpha = 0.75; ctx.drawImage(rim, …);
//            ctx.globalCompositeOperation = 'source-over'; ctx.globalAlpha = 1; ctx.drawImage(ink, …);
```

```js
// Ground light fields: one noise scalar f → four glowing bands. Per pixel, add bleed, seam line, grain.
const TH = [-0.95, -0.3, 0.35], BW = 0.075, HOT = [255, 240, 196];
const BANDS = [ { e: [44,116,140], c: [118,204,198] }, { e: [104,64,162], c: [182,130,220] },
                { e: [176,42,66], c: [242,106,82] },   { e: [234,122,44], c: [255,198,98] } ];
const ss = (a, b, x) => { let t = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, (x - a) / (b - a))); return t * t * (3 - 2 * t); };
function bandCol(i, f, gloss, o) {
  let d = i === 0 ? TH[0] - f : i === 3 ? f - TH[2] : Math.min(f - TH[i - 1], TH[i] - f); if (d < 0) d = 0;
  const B = BANDS[i], t = ss(0, 0.75, d) * (0.55 + 0.45 * gloss);
  for (let k = 0; k < 3; k++) o[k] = B.e[k] + (B.c[k] - B.e[k]) * t;
  if (i === 3) { const h = ss(0.9, 2.2, d) * (0.25 + 0.4 * gloss); for (let k = 0; k < 3; k++) o[k] += (HOT[k] - o[k]) * h; }
}
function fieldColor(f, gloss, out) {
  const s0 = ss(TH[0] - BW, TH[0] + BW, f), s1 = ss(TH[1] - BW, TH[1] + BW, f), s2 = ss(TH[2] - BW, TH[2] + BW, f);
  const w = [1 - s0, s0 - s1, s1 - s2, s2], t = [0, 0, 0]; out[0] = out[1] = out[2] = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) if (w[i] > 0.001) { bandCol(i, f, gloss, t); for (let k = 0; k < 3; k++) out[k] += t[k] * w[i]; }
  for (let k = 0; k < 3; k++) out[k] *= 0.9 + 0.2 * gloss;
}
// sd = (f - nearestThreshold) / |grad f|  (world units to the seam), res = px per unit
function shadePixel(rgb, sd, res, grain) {
  const a = Math.abs(sd);
  if (a < 6) { const e = 1 - a / 6, k = e * e * 0.22; rgb[0] += (255 - rgb[0]) * k; rgb[1] += (240 - rgb[1]) * k; rgb[2] += (215 - rgb[2]) * k; }
  rgb[0] += grain; rgb[1] += grain * 0.9; rgb[2] += grain * 0.8;
  const l = (0.36 - a) * res + 0.5;
  if (l > 0) { const t = Math.min(1, l) * 0.85; rgb[0] += (22 - rgb[0]) * t; rgb[1] += (8 - rgb[1]) * t; rgb[2] += (28 - rgb[2]) * t; }
}
```

## Adapting it to your game

- **Keep fixed:**
  - the light-floor / ink-actor split;
  - ink `#0b0510`;
  - the limb / leaf / curl vocabulary with curled tips;
  - one emissive colour per actor class;
  - the additive rim on the hero;
  - the seam-plus-lace ground;
  - the theatre frame.
- **Re-theme the fields.** You may swap the four band colours as long as they stay luminous, saturated and ordered from cool to warm. A winter game could use ice-blue | lilac | rose | pale gold, and a desert game indigo | magenta | orange | sand. Keep the hot heart in the warmest band.
- **Re-theme the emissives.** Use the warmest colour (gold/orange) for the player and friendly lights, and cooler or acid colours for enemies.
- **New characters.** Start from a bulb, a body or a veil, add one protruding identity feature (crown, horns, wings, antlers, hat), jointed limbs ending in curls, and an emissive face or carved mouth. Test the silhouette at 30 px tall in ink only.
- **Side-view games.** Use the same silhouettes and use the light fields as a horizontal backdrop (bands by height plus noise). This is the classic Reiniger look.
- **Other resolutions.** Everything is in world units. Only K changes. Keep K ≥ 2.5 or the thin curls break up.

## Performance notes

- **Baked once:**
  - all frames, mirrors and rim and hurt-rim copies. A rim costs 8 drawImages + 1 blur filter at bake time only;
  - ghost halos (2 blurred passes);
  - torn shards, glows, about 20 prop sprites, icons;
  - number sprites (cached per value, cleared above 300 entries);
  - the theatre frame (per screen size).
- **Per frame:** only `drawImage` with transforms, about 1–3 per actor (shadow, rim when flashing, sprite, glow), plus particles. Hundreds of enemies stay cheap. Cap hit-rim alpha and particle counts in big crowds.
- **The ground is the hot spot:**
  - per 256-unit chunk: about a 70² noise grid (domain-warped fbm = 3 fbm calls per sample) plus a per-pixel loop at up to 2.5 px/unit (about 400k pixels);
  - run it as a generator that yields every 2 rows and every 32 lace motifs, so chunks stream without frame drops;
  - lace decals are vector paths into one offscreen canvas per chunk.
- **Check filter support** (`ctx.filter = 'blur(1px)'`), and fall back to unblurred stamps on browsers without it.

## Copy-paste prompt

```text
Build my game <X> in the "Shadow Theatre" style (backlit paper shadow-puppet theatre, Lotte Reiniger / Limbo):
- The FLOOR is the light: huge organic glowing colour fields from one domain-warped noise value, thresholds -0.95/-0.3/0.35
  → moon teal #76ccc6 | dusk violet #b682dc | crimson #f26a52 | amber #ffc662 (edge colours #2c748c/#6840a2/#b02a42/#ea7a2c, amber gets a hot #fff0c4 heart).
- Seams between fields: thin ink line #16081c (0.72 world units) with light bleeding 6 units out of it; paper grain over everything.
- Ink lace on the floor at 80 % opacity: beads/rings/leaf pairs along seams, grass tufts on amber, filigree scrolls on crimson, leaves and stars on violet, broken ripple rings on teal.
- EVERYTHING standing is a flat silhouette in #0b0510, no outlines, no shading, built from tapered limbs, lens leaves and spiral curls; every tip ends in a curl.
- Only colour on silhouettes is emissive: hero face gold (#fffbe2→#ffd65e→#ff6a10 with bloom), small enemies acid-green eyes #d8ff62, brutes magenta cracks #ff5ad2. Carve mouths with destination-out.
- Ghost-type enemies invert: pale blue-white veil with a dark blurred halo under a light blurred halo.
- Hero always has a warm #ffb24a rim (8 tinted offset stamps, blurred, drawn with 'lighter') and an additive follow-spot pool; enemies get a cream rim only when hit.
- Each enemy class = unique outline feature + one emissive colour, so a crowd of 200 stays readable.
- Effects are light (additive flares, sparks, embers, glowing seed trails) or paper (torn shards with glowing #ff9a3a edges, ink scraps).
- Motion like rod puppets: jointed limb swings, whole-sprite rocking, enemies rise from stage slots on a rod.
- Frame: vignette, velvet curtains, scalloped valance with tassels, stage lip. HUD = ink plates with gold hairline rings, glowing gradient bars, Cinzel numbers, IM Fell English SC labels, Cormorant Garamond body.
- Bake all sprites/rims/glows once at ~1.3 × screen px per world unit; per frame only blit.
```
